evidence.ai_role: The models ranked discriminatory metabolites and selected features for disease classification; the team integrated these with pathway results to prioritize candidate biomarkers. DHEAS and citrate were then measured using ELISA and a biochemical assay, with patterns assessed in the validation cohort. Machine learning aided biomarker selection and classification; assays and clinical data supplied validation.

title: Machine-learning metabolomics prioritizes succinate in sepsis-associated encephalopathy
summary: In plasma samples from 29 controls, 32 sepsis patients and 27 patients with sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE), LC–MS/MS plus machine-learning feature selection identified a 12-metabolite profile. Succinate rose stepwise from controls to sepsis to SAE, ranked among the five leading XGBoost features, and correlated with APACHE II, SOFA and lactate. In a cecal-ligation-and-puncture mouse model, dietary succinate supplementation before sepsis worsened cognitive-test performance, neuronal injury and microglial activation; succinate also increased inflammatory gene expression in cultured microglia.
ai_technology: Random forest and support-vector-machine feature ranking with XGBoost classification
organization: Tongji Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology

evidence.tested: In a cecal-ligation-and-puncture mouse model, dietary succinate supplementation before sepsis worsened cognitive-test performance, neuronal injury and microglial activation; succinate also increased inflammatory gene expression in cultured microglia.
evidence.unknown: The human discovery cohort comprised 88 participants and the held-out model test set had 18 participants, so diagnostic performance and metabolite ranking need larger external cohorts. Succinate supplementation was given before CLP in mice, and cell experiments used a microglial cell line; these are preclinical perturbations and do not prove that succinate causes human SAE or that targeting it improves patient outcomes. Associations with severity scores are observational.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning feature selection and classifier comparison were applied to the measured plasma metabolomics to identify discriminatory features; succinate ranked among the top five XGBoost features. Researchers then tested its functional relevance through supplementation in a mouse sepsis model and in cultured microglia. The animal/cell experiments were human-directed follow-up, not model-generated predictions.

title: Machine learning and Mendelian randomization prioritize CA2 as a diabetic nephropathy biomarker
summary: Across six kidney-expression datasets, researchers identified 314 differentially expressed genes in diabetic nephropathy and used LASSO, SVM-RFE and random forest to prioritize seven candidate genes. Mendelian-randomization integration further prioritized carbonic anhydrase II (CA2); its ROC AUC exceeded 0.878 across the analyzed datasets. The authors also reported qPCR validation of CA2 in clinical patient and control samples and an association with inferred immune-cell infiltration.
ai_technology: LASSO, support-vector-machine recursive feature elimination and random-forest feature selection
organization: Shanghai Tenth People’s Hospital, Tongji University School of Medicine; Yangpu Hospital, Tongji University School of Medicine

evidence.tested: The authors also reported qPCR validation of CA2 in clinical patient and control samples and an association with inferred immune-cell infiltration.
evidence.unknown: This is a candidate biomarker study, not evidence of a clinically deployed test or patient benefit. Reported AUC values are retrospective dataset performance; qPCR validation supports differential expression but does not establish CA2 as causal or disease-specific. The accessible abstract does not report the clinical validation sample size, so none is inferred.
evidence.ai_role: Three machine-learning approaches integrated candidate-gene selection from kidney-expression datasets; Mendelian randomization with expression-QTL data then prioritized CA2, which was evaluated as a diagnostic biomarker and measured by qPCR in clinical samples. The models supported gene prioritization and discrimination, while qPCR supplied the wet-lab follow-up.

title: Machine learning prioritizes 1-methylnicotinamide as a serum signal across HBV cirrhosis-to-HCC progression
summary: Untargeted serum metabolomics from 69 participants, including eight patients followed from HBV-related cirrhosis to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), was analyzed with LASSO and random forest to prioritize metabolites. 1-methylnicotinamide (1-MNAM) declined across healthy, cirrhosis and HCC groups and was lower at the HCC than cirrhosis stage in the eight progressors. Targeted mass spectrometry in a separate cohort of 25 healthy controls and 25 early-stage HCC patients confirmed lower 1-MNAM in HCC (AUC 0.954 for HCC versus healthy controls).
ai_technology: LASSO regression and random forest classifier applied to serum metabolomics
organization: Centre for Medical Research, Ningbo No. 2 Hospital; Liver Disease Department of Integrative Medicine, Ningbo No. 2 Hospital

evidence.tested: Targeted mass spectrometry in a separate cohort of 25 healthy controls and 25 early-stage HCC patients confirmed lower 1-MNAM in HCC (AUC 0.954 for HCC versus healthy controls).
evidence.unknown: The longitudinal transition signal comes from eight HBV-cirrhosis patients who progressed during follow-up. The independent targeted cohort compared 25 early-HCC patients with 25 healthy controls; it did not validate prediction of progression among cirrhosis patients. The authors describe the overall sample as small and call for larger prospective validation. 1-MNAM is a known endogenous metabolite; this record concerns the study-specific association and selection result, not discovery of a new compound, causal mechanism, or clinical test.
evidence.ai_role: The authors used LASSO and random forest to select ten candidate metabolites distinguishing cirrhosis from HCC, then identified 1-MNAM as the sole candidate with a consistent decline across healthy, cirrhosis and HCC groups. The algorithms prioritized the measured metabolite; targeted mass spectrometry in a separate cohort provided assay follow-up.

title: Multi-omics machine learning identifies lysophosphatidic acid in PRRSV infection and links it to immune suppression
summary: Machine-learning analysis of untargeted serum metabolomic and lipidomic profiles from clinical pig cohorts identified lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) as a PRRSV-associated biomarker. Follow-up infection experiments reported increased LPA with autotaxin upregulation; in porcine alveolar macrophages, LPA manipulation altered RIG-I/type-I-interferon responses and viral replication. In infected pigs, targeting LPA was reported to protect against infection and associated disease outcomes.
ai_technology: Random-forest analysis of serum metabolomic and lipidomic profiles
organization: Sun Yat-sen University; Huazhong Agricultural University; Wen’s Foodstuff Group Co. Ltd.; Stanford University

evidence.tested: Machine-learning analysis of untargeted serum metabolomic and lipidomic profiles from clinical pig cohorts identified lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) as a PRRSV-associated biomarker.
evidence.unknown: The clinical classifier and biomarker work concerns pigs, not human diagnosis. The infection challenge experiments were small (figure descriptions report five piglets per group), and cell assays were performed in vitro. The authors report that the mechanism by which LPA suppresses RIG-I remains unclear; the findings do not establish a treatment for people or broad field effectiveness in livestock.
evidence.ai_role: Random-forest analysis ranked metabolite and lipid features from clinical PRRSV-positive and negative pig cohorts and contributed to identification of LPA as the candidate biomarker. The authors then tested LPA in infection models, including cultured porcine alveolar macrophages and infected pigs, to examine host-response and disease outcomes.

title: Machine-learning metabolomics distinguishes SARS-CoV-2, influenza A and RSV from respiratory swabs
summary: Untargeted metabolomics and machine learning identified upper-respiratory-swab signatures for SARS-CoV-2 positivity, followed by targeted LC-MS/MS profiling. Across 1,226 samples (521 SARS-CoV-2-positive, 97 influenza A, 96 RSV, 211 other respiratory viruses and 301 virus-negative), the best SARS-CoV-2 LightGBM model had AUC 0.99, sensitivity 0.96 and specificity 0.95. Separate models reported AUC 0.97 for influenza A and 0.99 for RSV. The top-ranked SARS-CoV-2 features included 3-oxo-heneicosanoic acid and 2-(4-hydroxyphenyl) ethanol.
ai_technology: Light Gradient Boosting Machine and other machine-learning classifiers applied to mass-spectrometry metabolomics
organization: British Columbia Centre for Disease Control Public Health Laboratory; University of British Columbia; Stanford University School of Medicine; Stanford Health Care; Chan Zuckerberg Biohub

evidence.tested: Separate models reported AUC 0.97 for influenza A and 0.99 for RSV.
evidence.unknown: This is an assay-validation study using stored respiratory specimens, not a prospective clinical-impact trial. Results establish classification in the studied cohorts and do not show improved patient outcomes or routine deployment. The source notes unresolved oxo-position/isomer assignment for several features. The metabolite signals are candidate host-response markers, not proof of virus-specific causal biology.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning feature ranking identified metabolite signatures in untargeted profiles; the team adapted candidate signatures to targeted LC-MS/MS, and evaluated classification in respiratory-virus sample cohorts. The models supplied the sample-level classification and feature ranking, while mass spectrometry measured the metabolites.

title: Multi-omics machine learning prioritizes a plasma lipid signature for active tuberculosis differentiation
summary: Machine-learning integration of plasma functional-omics data in two discovery cohorts and a validation cohort identified biosignatures that distinguished active tuberculosis from nontuberculous mycobacterial infection, latent TB infection and other lung diseases. Cohorts included 76 people in the TB–NTM discovery set, 72 in the TB–LTBI–other-lung-disease set, and 68 TB plus 30 LTBI participants in the validation set. PC(14:0_22:6) was the most important predictor and was lower in active TB; additional external datasets yielded reported AUCs of 0.77–1.00.
ai_technology: Multi-omics integration and machine-learning predictive models for feature selection and classification
organization: Inje University College of Medicine; Ton Duc Thang University; Hanoi University of Pharmacy; University of Copenhagen; Korea University Guro Hospital

evidence.tested: Machine-learning integration of plasma functional-omics data in two discovery cohorts and a validation cohort identified biosignatures that distinguished active tuberculosis from nontuberculous mycobacterial infection, latent TB infection and other lung diseases.
evidence.unknown: The article calls PC(14:0_22:6) a candidate differential-diagnostic biomarker. Reported AUCs vary by comparator group and dataset; they do not establish prospective performance, clinical utility, or replacement of microbiological diagnosis. The PubMed abstract does not provide all cohort-level assay details, so this summary remains bounded to abstract-reported information.
evidence.ai_role: The authors used machine-learning predictive modeling across integrated functional-omics measurements to identify and prioritize plasma signatures that discriminate active TB from clinically relevant non-TB groups. PC(14:0_22:6) emerged as the leading lipid feature; the analysis was evaluated across discovery, validation and two external datasets.

title: TriSCOPE links cell-type-specific Alzheimer’s expression programs to inherited risk loci
summary: TriSCOPE combined cell-level predictive modeling, donor-aware differential expression and pseudotime analysis across six single-nucleus RNA-sequencing datasets (about 4.2 million nuclei from 627 donors). It identified cell-type-specific predictively expressed genes that were often missed by univariate differential-expression analysis; conditional GWAS–eQTL colocalization supported 27 gene–cell-type pairs at Alzheimer’s risk loci, including pairs without significant differential expression. Selected gene signals and analytical branches were compared across independent cohorts.
ai_technology: TriSCOPE, using LightGBM-based multivariate predictive modeling integrated with differential expression and pseudotime analysis
organization: Harvard Medical School; Harvard College; New York Genome Center; Rush Alzheimer’s Disease Center, Rush University

evidence.tested: Selected gene signals and analytical branches were compared across independent cohorts.
evidence.unknown: This is a computational reanalysis of previously published, post-mortem cross-sectional datasets; it did not collect new tissue or perform perturbation experiments. The authors state the framework is for feature discovery rather than clinical prognosis, cannot establish temporal ordering, and requires functional perturbation studies to distinguish pathogenic drivers from protective or reactive signals. The reported cell-level AUCs are modest and should not be presented as patient-level diagnostic performance.
evidence.ai_role: The supervised machine-learning branch prioritized gene-expression features that predicted clinical Alzheimer’s diagnosis within cell types, conditional on demographics and APOE genotype. The study integrated those model-ranked features with donor-aware differential expression, pseudotime and GWAS–eQTL colocalization to nominate genetically supported cell-type programs.

title: Spatial glycan imaging and machine learning identify a serum N-glycan panel for HCC in cirrhosis
summary: Spatial N-glycan imaging of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) tissue and paired serum identified thirteen altered glycan structures; glycoproteomics linked them to more than 50 proteins, and sixteen glycoproteins were assessed in a separate patient set. Machine-learning algorithms combining glycan/glycoprotein features with clinical variables differentiated early-stage HCC from cirrhosis in a case-control cohort of 100 HCC and 101 cirrhosis-only patients, with reported AUROC values across the algorithms of 0.88–0.97.
ai_technology: Machine-learning algorithms using serum N-glycan and glycoprotein features, age, sex and AFP
organization: Medical University of South Carolina; GlycoPath, Inc.; HTX Technologies; University of California San Diego; University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center

evidence.tested: Machine-learning algorithms combining glycan/glycoprotein features with clinical variables differentiated early-stage HCC from cirrhosis in a case-control cohort of 100 HCC and 101 cirrhosis-only patients, with reported AUROC values across the algorithms of 0.88–0.97.
evidence.unknown: The discovery samples included 53 HCC tissues and 23 matched sera; the 201-patient testing set was a case-control cohort, not prospective surveillance. The paper notes that sialic acid was removed before analysis, excluding an important class of glycan modification. It does not establish screening benefit or prospective clinical utility. Individual glycoforms were weak classifiers; performance came from combined feature algorithms.
evidence.ai_role: Researchers used spatial glycan imaging and glycoproteomics to select altered tissue and matched-serum features, then used machine-learning algorithms to combine selected glycan/glycoprotein measurements with clinical variables for HCC-versus-cirrhosis classification. The source reports model performance in an independent case-control patient set.

title: Multimodal AI distinguishes ten dementia etiologies across nine clinical datasets
summary: A multimodal AI model analyzed demographics, personal and family history, medications, cognitive and functional testing, and neuroimaging across nine datasets totaling 51,269 participants. It assigned probabilities to ten primary or contributing dementia etiologies and addressed mixed cases. The paper reports microaveraged AUROC 0.96 for dementia-etiology differentiation; model probabilities aligned with etiology-specific biomarkers and postmortem pathology. In a review of 100 cases, AI-augmented neurologist assessment outperformed neurologist-only ratings.
ai_technology: Multimodal machine-learning model combining clinical, neuropsychological, functional and neuroimaging data
organization: Boston University; Stanford University; Peking Union Medical College Hospital; Columbia University Irving Medical Center; University of Nebraska Medical Center; additional clinical and research centers contributing cohorts

evidence.tested: A multimodal AI model analyzed demographics, personal and family history, medications, cognitive and functional testing, and neuroimaging across nine datasets totaling 51,269 participants.
evidence.unknown: The nine-dataset analysis is retrospective and includes in-house as well as external cohorts. The 100-case clinician comparison is small, and the study did not test prospective changes in care or patient outcomes. The authors call for prospective studies before claiming improved patient care. Model probabilities aligned with available biomarkers and postmortem evidence but are not histopathologic confirmation for every individual prediction.
evidence.ai_role: The model integrated routinely collected clinical variables and multimodal neuroimaging to estimate cognitive status and probabilities for ten dementia etiologies, including mixed etiologies and cases with incomplete features. It was evaluated across independent cohorts and compared with neurologist assessments; its output is the etiology-specific classification and probability result.

title: Machine-learning metabolomics prioritizes serum metabolites for SLE diagnosis and activity assessment
summary: Targeted serum metabolomics compared 89 patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and 44 healthy participants, identifying 146 differential metabolites. The authors combined statistical screening with seven machine-learning models to prioritize eight diagnostic biomarker candidates (reported AUCs above 0.95). Two additional metabolites, N-methyl-L-glutamic acid and L-2-aminobutyric acid, were evaluated by ELISA in a 90-patient SLE validation cohort and associated with SLE Disease Activity Index scores.
ai_technology: Seven machine-learning classification models applied to targeted serum metabolomics
organization: The Affiliated Guangzhou Panyu Central Hospital of Guangzhou Medical University; Guangzhou University of Chinese Medicine; Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hospital, Sun Yat-sen University; Panyu District Central Hospital

evidence.tested: The authors combined statistical screening with seven machine-learning models to prioritize eight diagnostic biomarker candidates (reported AUCs above 0.95).
evidence.unknown: This retrospective case-control study has modest cohorts and does not establish a clinically deployed test, causal SLE mechanism, or patient benefit. Reported diagnostic AUCs and SLEDAI associations require independent prospective replication; the validation cohort described in the abstract consists of SLE patients and does not by itself establish performance against a new external healthy/control population. The authors’ pathway interpretation is hypothesis-generating.
evidence.ai_role: The study iteratively compared seven machine-learning models to select candidate metabolites for SLE classification and combined the selected features with statistical screening. N-methyl-L-glutamic acid and L-2-aminobutyric acid were subsequently assessed by ELISA in a patient validation cohort; the machine-learning analysis nominated candidates, while the assays supplied biological measurement follow-up.

title: EHR machine learning and genetic colocalization link osteoporosis to female Alzheimer’s risk near MS4A6A
summary: Random-forest models trained on UCSF records (749 expert-diagnosed Alzheimer’s disease cases and 250,545 controls) identified clinical features predictive up to seven years before the recorded onset; the seven-year model’s AUROC was 0.72 using clinical features alone. Matched-cohort follow-up in external University of California health-system records found faster Alzheimer’s diagnosis after osteoporosis in women. Genetic colocalization analyses supported a female-specific shared signal between Alzheimer’s disease, low heel bone mineral density and MS4A6A expression near the MS4A gene cluster. The paper also reports shared APOE-locus support for hyperlipidemia and Alzheimer’s disease.
ai_technology: Random-forest models on longitudinal electronic health records, interpreted with the SPOKE biomedical knowledge network
organization: University of California, San Francisco; Stanford University; University of California health-system collaborators; University of Oxford

evidence.tested: Matched-cohort follow-up in external University of California health-system records found faster Alzheimer’s diagnosis after osteoporosis in women.
evidence.unknown: This is hypothesis-generating observational work. EHR features may reflect healthcare access, clinician behavior, coding and biological processes; the authors explicitly state that further validation across omics data types is needed. Genetic colocalization and matched cohort associations do not establish that osteoporosis causes Alzheimer’s disease or that treating osteoporosis prevents it. The prediction model is not a prospective clinical-impact evaluation, and early risk discrimination is modest with the low-prevalence outcome.
evidence.ai_role: Random-forest models ranked EHR-derived clinical features associated with future Alzheimer’s diagnosis. The team used matched models to prioritize hypotheses, then used SPOKE to connect clinical predictors to biological networks and independent health-system data plus GWAS/eQTL colocalization to examine the osteoporosis and hyperlipidemia associations. The model-generated prioritization led to follow-up of the female-specific osteoporosis signal near MS4A6A.

title: Machine-learning proteomics identifies a replicated plasma signature associated with Alzheimer’s disease
summary: A three-stage analysis of plasma proteomics from 1,270 people with clinical Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and 2,096 cognitively normal controls identified 416 proteins associated with clinical AD, including 294 that the paper classified as not previously associated with AD in large-scale plasma or CSF proteomic studies. A LASSO-selected seven-protein model predicted clinical AD and biomarker-defined AD status, with validation in external cohorts and orthogonal assays; the signature also stratified later progression to symptomatic AD among initially cognitively normal participants.
ai_technology: LASSO feature selection with logistic regression, using five-fold cross-validation and age/sex covariates
organization: Washington University School of Medicine and Knight Alzheimer Disease Research Center; Stanford Alzheimer’s Disease Research Center; Rush Alzheimer’s Disease Center; Global Neurodegeneration Proteomics Consortium; collaborating Alzheimer research centers

evidence.tested: A LASSO-selected seven-protein model predicted clinical AD and biomarker-defined AD status, with validation in external cohorts and orthogonal assays; the signature also stratified later progression to symptomatic AD among initially cognitively normal participants.
evidence.unknown: The cohort analysis is observational and does not establish that the associated proteins cause AD. The model’s clinical-status AUC was 0.72 in replication; performance was comparable to p-tau217 in the study’s comparison, but the reported AUC for frontotemporal dementia was also 0.73, limiting disease specificity. Orthogonal platform validation covered only subsets of the seven proteins (four proteins on Olink and two on Alamar), and the authors state that further work is needed before clinical use. The reported “new” designation is relative to prior large-scale plasma/CSF proteomic studies, not proof that each protein is biologically novel.
evidence.ai_role: The team used LASSO to select a compact protein panel from the proteins associated with AD in discovery and replication analyses, then retrained logistic regression to predict clinical AD status. This model-driven panel was evaluated against amyloid and tau biomarkers, external cohorts and orthogonal protein platforms; the analysis also tested associations with progression to symptomatic AD and memory decline.

title: Deep learning identifies previously unreported protein interactions in human bacterial pathogens
summary: A RoseTTAFold2-Lite pipeline combined residue coevolution, deep-learning complex prediction and AlphaFold modelling to screen protein pairs across 19 human bacterial pathogens. In a validation set selected using the deep-learning pipeline, co-immunoprecipitation detected four of six predicted interactions. Three pairs lacked prior direct interaction evidence: E. coli UbiE–YcaR, P. aeruginosa PA4105–PA4106, and P. aeruginosa WbpG–HisF2. The PA4105–PA4106 structural similarity to proteins in 3-thiaglutamate biosynthesis and the WbpG–HisF2 result provide functional hypotheses, not established native-pathogen mechanisms.
ai_technology: RoseTTAFold2-Lite integrated with direct coupling analysis and AlphaFold complex modelling
organization: University of Washington Institute for Protein Design; University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center; Broad Institute; Massachusetts General Hospital; University of Connecticut; Seoul National University; collaborating institutions

evidence.tested: In a validation set selected using the deep-learning pipeline, co-immunoprecipitation detected four of six predicted interactions.
evidence.unknown: The positive interaction evidence comes from heterologous co-immunoprecipitation/pull-down assays, with two independent experiments per positive pair, rather than native-pathogen systems. The validation subset was small (four positives among six AI-selected candidates); most of the thousands of predicted interactions remain untested, and false positives and false negatives are expected. Proposed roles for PA4105–PA4106 and UbiE–YcaR remain hypotheses; this paper does not establish their physiological function or a therapeutic target.
evidence.ai_role: RoseTTAFold2-Lite used residue–residue coevolution and predicted complex structures to rank candidate protein pairs in a proteome-wide screen. The authors selected six pairs from the final deep-learning pipeline for co-immunoprecipitation tests; four yielded positive interaction signals. Three were described as lacking previously reported direct interaction evidence, including UbiE–YcaR, PA4105–PA4106 and WbpG–HisF2. The models enabled the experimental target selection; they did not themselves establish physical interactions.

title: Machine learning identifies plasma metabolite panels for gastric-cancer diagnosis and prognosis
summary: In a multicenter study of 702 participants, targeted plasma metabolomics and machine learning produced a 10-metabolite gastric-cancer diagnostic model and separate 28-metabolite survival-risk model. The diagnostic model was evaluated in an independent 95-person cohort (AUROC 0.920; sensitivity 0.905, specificity 0.75) and detected stage IA disease with AUROC 0.909. Among 181 patients followed for a median 40 months, the prognostic model achieved test-set concordance index 0.83. Succinate, uridine and lactate were among diagnostic features.
ai_technology: LASSO, random forest and random survival forest
organization: Tsinghua University; National Cancer Center/National Clinical Research Center for Cancer, China; Harbin Medical University Cancer Hospital; collaborating Chinese cancer centers

evidence.tested: The diagnostic model was evaluated in an independent 95-person cohort (AUROC 0.920; sensitivity 0.905, specificity 0.75) and detected stage IA disease with AUROC 0.909.
evidence.unknown: Case-control cohorts do not establish population screening performance. External diagnostic test n=95; prognosis cohort median follow-up 40 months with right-censored outcomes. The paper says direct clinical use is premature and requires quality-control samples. Associations are not causal and no model-guided benefit was tested.
evidence.ai_role: LASSO selected ten plasma metabolites for a diagnostic model evaluated in internal and independent external cohorts. Random survival forest selected a 28-metabolite prognostic panel, evaluated in a held-out patient set.

title: Machine-learning selection and external mass-spectrometry testing identify an ARDS 28-day prognosis protein panel
summary: A multicenter observational serum multi-omics study used LASSO and Boruta to select candidate biomarkers for 28-day outcome in acute respiratory distress syndrome. Eight proteins (VCAM1, LDHB, MSN, FLG2, TAGLN2, LMNA, MBL2 and LBP) showed consistency in an independent cohort of 183 patients and were confirmed by targeted parallel-reaction-monitoring mass spectrometry. The protein model AUC was 0.802 in validation versus 0.738 for the clinical model. The discovery analysis also reported sphingosine-1-phosphate association with ARDS prognosis and an enriched sphingolipid pathway.
ai_technology: LASSO and Boruta feature selection; machine-learning prognostic model; targeted PRM validation
organization: Fudan University; Zhongshan Hospital, Fudan University; Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine; collaborating Shanghai hospitals

evidence.tested: Eight proteins (VCAM1, LDHB, MSN, FLG2, TAGLN2, LMNA, MBL2 and LBP) showed consistency in an independent cohort of 183 patients and were confirmed by targeted parallel-reaction-monitoring mass spectrometry.
evidence.unknown: Observational prognostic associations do not show proteins cause outcomes or that biomarker-guided care improves survival. Discovery n=130 ARDS patients; validation n=183. PRM confirmation is not independent replication by another group; deployment and prospective benefit were not established.
evidence.ai_role: LASSO, fold-change screening and Boruta prioritized candidate 28-day ARDS prognostic proteins; candidates were tested by targeted PRM in an external cohort.

title: Integrated radiogenomic machine learning predicts neoadjuvant chemotherapy response in metastatic ovarian cancer
summary: The IRON ensemble combined baseline clinical data, CA-125, ctDNA and CT radiomics from primary and metastatic lesions to estimate tumor-volume change during neoadjuvant chemotherapy for high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma. In an independent 42-patient Barts cohort, the integrated model achieved AUC 0.78 for RECIST 1.1 response classification versus 0.47 for a clinical-only model; radiomics-containing scores significantly correlated with volume change in internal holdout. The study also measured spatial heterogeneity, with omental lesions showing better response than pelvic/ovarian disease.
ai_technology: IRON ensemble combining elastic net, support-vector regression and random forest
organization: University of Cambridge and Cambridge University Hospitals; Barts Health NHS Trust; Medical University of Vienna; collaborating institutions

evidence.tested: In an independent 42-patient Barts cohort, the integrated model achieved AUC 0.78 for RECIST 1.1 response classification versus 0.47 for a clinical-only model; radiomics-containing scores significantly correlated with volume change in internal holdout.
evidence.unknown: Model analysis of two prospective observational cohorts (training n=72, internal holdout n=20, external n=42), not a decision trial. External ctDNA unavailable and imputed to training means. Sample size limits generalizability; treatment benefit from model-guided decisions was not tested.
evidence.ai_role: Pretreatment clinical, blood and multi-lesion radiomic features predicted volumetric response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Held-out and external evaluation showed radiomics added predictive information beyond clinical variables.

title: Elastic-net proteomic risk modeling and multi-cohort validation identify proteins associated with incident diabetes
summary: An untargeted analysis of 4,955 plasma proteins in the ARIC cohort identified 140 associations with incident diabetes; 64 were significant in an internal sample and 47 (including 22 reported as novel) were associated in the external Singapore Multi-Ethnic Cohort. Elastic-net Cox modeling selected a 27-protein panel for 20-year risk prediction. In internal validation, adding those proteins to conventional risk factors including fasting glucose and HbA1c increased the C statistic from 0.720 to 0.731. Genetic-instrument analyses supported possible causal roles for SHBG, ATP1B2 and GSTA1, although ATP1B2’s genetic and observational directions differed.
ai_technology: Elastic-net Cox regression for protein feature selection and incident-diabetes risk prediction
organization: Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health; Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities study centers; National University of Singapore; New York University Grossman School of Medicine; collaborating institutions

evidence.tested: An untargeted analysis of 4,955 plasma proteins in the ARIC cohort identified 140 associations with incident diabetes; 64 were significant in an internal sample and 47 (including 22 reported as novel) were associated in the external Singapore Multi-Ethnic Cohort.
evidence.unknown: The 47-protein associations were externally tested in Singapore MEC; the elastic-net predictive model itself was internally validated in ARIC, not independently externally validated. Its incremental C statistic over covariates including fasting glucose and HbA1c was modest (0.011; P=0.04), and the protein model overestimated observed diabetes risk across internal-validation deciles. The causal claims are genetic-instrument inferences, not experimental proof; ATP1B2 had opposite directions in genetic-instrument versus observational analyses. Cohort associations do not establish clinical utility.
evidence.ai_role: Elastic net selected a 27-protein combination from candidate proteins to improve 20-year incident-diabetes risk prediction beyond clinical and cardiometabolic covariates. The model was trained in the ARIC discovery subset and internally evaluated in a held-out ARIC subset. Separate Cox association and genetic-instrument analyses reported the externally validated protein associations; the record does not attribute those analyses to machine learning.

title: Machine-learning models identify cerebrospinal-fluid protein signatures for multiple-sclerosis activity and disability progression
summary: Using Olink proteomics of 1,463 proteins in CSF and plasma from two prospective Swedish cohorts, the study trained prediction models for multiple-sclerosis diagnosis, 2-year disease activity and long-term disability worsening. Lower CSF neurofilament light (NfL) predicted absence of disease activity at two years (replication AUC 0.77). A stepwise model using 11 CSF proteins (CXCL13, LTA, FCN2, ICAM3, LY9, SLAMF7, TYMP, CHI3L1, FYB1, TNFRSF1B and NfL) predicted normalized age-related MS severity; subgroup classification AUCs in the replication cohort ranged from 0.88 to 0.90.
ai_technology: Stepwise logistic regression for diagnosis and disease activity; stepwise linear regression for long-term disability severity
organization: Linköping University; University of Skövde; Karolinska Institutet and Karolinska University Hospital; collaborating Swedish institutions

evidence.tested: Using Olink proteomics of 1,463 proteins in CSF and plasma from two prospective Swedish cohorts, the study trained prediction models for multiple-sclerosis diagnosis, 2-year disease activity and long-term disability worsening.
evidence.unknown: The study included 143 people with early-stage MS and 43 healthy controls across discovery and replication cohorts; the replication MS cohort had 51 participants. The 2-year disease-activity comparison in replication was especially small (45 with activity versus 5 without). The 11-protein severity model predicted observational disability scores rather than treatment benefit. The plasma severity model had only 12 eligible replication samples and performed less convincingly. These are cohort-level results, not a clinically validated diagnostic assay or independent replication by another research group.
evidence.ai_role: The study used statistical differential-expression testing to select disease-associated candidate proteins, then fitted logistic-regression models to predict MS diagnosis and 2-year disease activity and a linear-regression model to predict long-term normalized age-related MS severity. Stepwise feature selection produced the protein combinations; the frozen models were evaluated in a separate prospective cohort.

title: Unsupervised clustering identifies three blood immune endophenotypes associated with distinct multiple-sclerosis trajectories
summary: In two multicenter longitudinal cohorts of early multiple sclerosis (discovery n=309; validation n=232), unsupervised clustering of high-dimensional flow-cytometry and serum-proteomics profiles identified three peripheral-blood immune endophenotypes. Follow-up associated the groups with different trajectories of inflammation versus early structural damage. In the endophenotype-3 subgroup, patients subsequently treated with interferon beta had higher four-year progression and MRI activity than patients receiving other therapies.
ai_technology: Unsupervised clustering of high-dimensional flow-cytometry and serum-proteomics profiles (the reviewed abstract does not name the clustering algorithm)
organization: University of Münster; German Competence Network Multiple Sclerosis; Max Delbrück Center; Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin; collaborating German and international centers

evidence.tested: In two multicenter longitudinal cohorts of early multiple sclerosis (discovery n=309; validation n=232), unsupervised clustering of high-dimensional flow-cytometry and serum-proteomics profiles identified three peripheral-blood immune endophenotypes.
evidence.unknown: The source reports cohort associations, not randomized treatment effects. The higher progression and MRI activity among endophenotype-3 patients treated with interferon beta may be affected by treatment selection and other confounding; it does not establish that interferon beta caused worse outcomes or that the signature can guide care. The validation cohort is an independent patient cohort within the study, not independent replication by another research group. The reviewed abstract does not provide the clustering algorithm name or establish prospective clinical utility.
evidence.ai_role: The researchers combined flow-cytometry immune measurements and serum-protein profiles, then used unsupervised clustering to define three immune endophenotypes in the discovery cohort and assess them in an independent multicenter validation cohort. The clustering generated the patient groups whose longitudinal clinical and paraclinical trajectories were compared; the repository abstract does not specify the algorithm name.

title: LightGBM feature selection identifies a four-protein panel associated with incident chronic kidney disease
summary: In a prospective UK Biobank cohort of 27,429 participants without baseline chronic kidney disease, the study evaluated 2,920 plasma proteins and found 205 associated with incident CKD after protein-wide Cox regression with Bonferroni correction. LASSO reduced these to 23 candidates and LightGBM feature selection identified EDA2R, GDF15, HAVCR1 and SCARB2 as a four-protein panel. The protein panel alone had an AUC of 0.796 versus 0.805 for demographic variables; adding the proteins to the demographic model raised AUC to 0.830 in the study data.
ai_technology: Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) and Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) feature selection
organization: Nanjing Medical University, School of Public Health, Department of Epidemiology and Center for Global Health; UK Biobank

evidence.tested: In a prospective UK Biobank cohort of 27,429 participants without baseline chronic kidney disease, the study evaluated 2,920 plasma proteins and found 205 associated with incident CKD after protein-wide Cox regression with Bonferroni correction.
evidence.unknown: The abstract reports a prospective UK Biobank cohort and internal analyses; the four-protein model did not outperform the demographic model alone (AUC 0.796 vs 0.805, p=0.14), though combining the proteins with demographics improved AUC to 0.830. The authors state external validation is needed before clinical application. Protein associations and model selection do not establish causal roles or clinical utility.
evidence.ai_role: After protein-wide Cox association screening, LASSO selected 23 candidate proteins and LightGBM-based feature selection identified four proteins for the incident-CKD prediction panel. The study assessed their predictive contribution with demographic covariates and sensitivity analyses; these algorithms selected risk markers rather than demonstrating causal protein effects.

title: External validation reveals distinct plasma proteomic signatures across biopsy-proven primary glomerular diseases
summary: Profiling 5,416 plasma proteins in Korean cohorts, the study found distinct signatures across four biopsy-proven primary glomerular diseases. An elastic-net model using 93 proteins differentiated disease subtypes and controls in discovery and external validation cohorts. It achieved AUCs above 0.8 for minimal change disease, membranous nephropathy and IgA nephropathy; the model correctly classified 14 of 15 minimal-change cases and 20 of 32 IgA-nephropathy cases, but only 3 of 14 focal-segmental glomerulosclerosis cases. Functional analysis highlighted hemostasis-related proteins in minimal change disease.
ai_technology: Elastic-net-regularized logistic regression using plasma proteomic features
organization: Seoul National University College of Medicine and Seoul National University Hospital; KORNERSTONE investigators; collaborating Korean hospitals

evidence.tested: Profiling 5,416 plasma proteins in Korean cohorts, the study found distinct signatures across four biopsy-proven primary glomerular diseases.
evidence.unknown: The discovery cohort contained 147 participants and the external validation cohort 85; subtype-level validation samples were small. Classification was strong for minimal change disease, membranous nephropathy and IgA nephropathy but poor for focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (3/14 correctly classified). The findings support cohort-level proteomic differentiation and do not establish a clinically deployable noninvasive replacement for kidney biopsy or causal roles for the selected proteins.
evidence.ai_role: The model used elastic-net regularization to select and combine a 93-protein plasma signature for classifying biopsy-proven primary glomerular disease subtypes and controls. The model was evaluated in an independent external validation cohort. Functional analysis of key proteins was used to characterize subtype-associated pathways, including hemostasis in minimal change disease.

title: Machine-learning analysis separates genetic from environmental drivers of stimulated cytokine responses in healthy adults
summary: In 406 healthy GEOCODE cohort participants, whole-blood cytokine responses to Toll-like-receptor (TLR) and T-cell-receptor (TCR) stimulation varied across people, including high- and low-IL-6-response profiles associated with monocyte counts, sex and sampling season. Feature-importance analysis of machine-learning models found TCR-induced cytokine predictions were mainly driven by genetic features, whereas TLR-induced predictions were driven more by environmental and biological features. Combining genetic with biological and environmental data improved prediction by about 0.2 on average, and the reported findings were evaluated in the independent Milieu Intérieur cohort.
ai_technology: Machine-learning models including random forest, gradient-boosted trees, artificial neural networks and elastic net; random forest feature-importance analysis
organization: Université libre de Bruxelles; Hôpital Erasme; Milieu Intérieur cohort collaborators

evidence.tested: In 406 healthy GEOCODE cohort participants, whole-blood cytokine responses to Toll-like-receptor (TLR) and T-cell-receptor (TCR) stimulation varied across people, including high- and low-IL-6-response profiles associated with monocyte counts, sex and sampling season.
evidence.unknown: The discovery cohort was a selected healthy-adult sample (406 participants), and the correlations for TLR-induced response prediction were modest (average 0.27; TCR-induced 0.53). Genetic-only models may overestimate predictive accuracy, as the authors report. Feature importance identifies predictive contribution, not causal biological effects; results do not establish disease-specific immune mechanisms or treatment response.
evidence.ai_role: Models predicted measured cytokine levels following TLR or TCR stimulation from genetic, biological and environmental participant features. Random-forest permutation importance identified which input categories contributed to predictions; the study also compared predictions across cross-validation and a separate Milieu Intérieur cohort. Feature importance is associational and does not establish that a feature causally regulates cytokine production.

title: Stability-based machine learning selects IL-8 and CCL3 as a two-protein serum signature for early silicosis
summary: A stability-based feature-selection workflow combining LASSO, random forest and SVM recursive feature elimination identified serum IL-8 and CCL3 as a two-protein signature distinguishing Stage I silicosis from controls. The study used a discovery cohort of 57 cases and 57 matched controls, then assessed the signature in an independent, unmatched cohort of 40 cases and 40 controls. The article reports validation AUC 0.973, specificity 95.0% and sensitivity 77.5%; both proteins were lower in silicosis cases.
ai_technology: Stability-based ensemble feature selection using LASSO, random forest and SVM recursive feature elimination, followed by logistic regression
organization: Nanjing Medical University; Jiangsu Provincial Center for Disease Control and Prevention; Southeast University; China University of Mining and Technology

evidence.tested: The study used a discovery cohort of 57 cases and 57 matched controls, then assessed the signature in an independent, unmatched cohort of 40 cases and 40 controls.
evidence.unknown: The discovery cohort was small (57 cases/57 matched controls); the validation cohort was also small and unmatched (40/40), with 77.5% sensitivity despite high specificity. This is retrospective biomarker validation and does not establish population screening performance, clinical utility, or causal involvement of IL-8 or CCL3 in silicosis.
evidence.ai_role: Across 100 iterations, the machine-learning feature-selection framework selected a stable two-protein signature from targeted serum proteomics. A logistic-regression classifier used those selected features and was evaluated by cross-validation and an independent validation cohort. The study reports reduced IL-8 and CCL3 as the signature components.

title: Computer-vision and metabolomics fusion links paired serum–urine flux mismatch to early diabetic kidney disease
summary: In a two-center cohort of 364 participants with type 2 diabetes and controls, targeted serum/urine metabolite measurements found a high-serum/low-urine pattern for indoxyl sulfate and related metabolites in early diabetic kidney disease (DKD), consistent with reduced tubular secretion. Computer vision quantified urine foam stability and chromaticity; Random Forest recursive feature elimination selected these image features together with metabolite ratios and clinical variables for the FluxPro-DKD classifier. It distinguished DKD from diabetes without kidney disease with AUC 0.90 in discovery and 0.85 in a geographically distinct external cohort of 82.
ai_technology: Computer-vision urine phenotyping and Random Forest recursive feature elimination (RF-RFE) for multimodal feature selection
organization: Beijing University of Chinese Medicine; Dongfang Hospital; Third Affiliated Hospital of Beijing University of Chinese Medicine; Tianjin Institute of Nephropathy

evidence.tested: In a two-center cohort of 364 participants with type 2 diabetes and controls, targeted serum/urine metabolite measurements found a high-serum/low-urine pattern for indoxyl sulfate and related metabolites in early diabetic kidney disease (DKD), consistent with reduced tubular secretion.
evidence.unknown: The external cohort validation was cross-sectional; the paper says longitudinal follow-up for hard kidney outcomes is ongoing. Its projected three-year event rates are theoretical Monte Carlo simulations based on cross-sectional data and are not observed outcomes. The study did not measure proximal-tubule transporter expression or compare directly against KIM-1 or NGAL, and generalization beyond the two Chinese centers and population requires further validation. Metabolite flux supports, but does not prove, tubular transport dysfunction.
evidence.ai_role: Computer vision quantified urine foam half-life and chromaticity from standardized sample images. RF-RFE selected eight predictors, including digital urine features and serum-to-urine metabolite ratios, for the fusion classifier distinguishing early DKD from type 2 diabetes without DKD. The paper reports external cohort evaluation. The biochemical interpretation of flux mismatch as reduced tubular secretory capacity is based on measured metabolite ratios and literature-supported interpretation; transporter expression was not measured.

title: SONAR identifies 3′UTR sequence features that raise T-cell receptor protein expression and CD8-cell killing
summary: The XGBoost-based SONAR pipeline modeled protein abundance from thousands of sequence features across human immune cells and cell lines, identifying cell-type- and activation-dependent regulatory patterns. Reporter assays found that CT-rich 3′UTR motifs increased protein output while AG-rich motifs were generally repressive. SONAR-informed synthetic 3′UTRs raised CDK4-specific T-cell-receptor protein without increasing its mRNA; engineered CD8+ T cells carrying the CT-rich constructs killed CDK4-expressing melanoma cells more effectively in a coculture assay.
ai_technology: SONAR, an XGBoost machine-learning pipeline using thousands of sequence features to predict protein abundance
organization: Sanquin Blood Supply Foundation; University of Amsterdam; Amsterdam UMC; Oncode Institute

evidence.tested: Reporter assays found that CT-rich 3′UTR motifs increased protein output while AG-rich motifs were generally repressive.
evidence.unknown: The target-cell killing experiment used engineered CD8+ cells in vitro and three donors; no animal or patient treatment outcome was tested. Protein abundance prediction used limited cell and immune-subset datasets, and model feature importance is not itself causal evidence. The assay supports effects for the tested synthetic 3′UTRs and CDK4-specific TCR in the reported system, not all proteins or therapeutic settings.
evidence.ai_role: SONAR learned sequence-feature patterns associated with protein abundance in immune cells, including cell-type- and activation-dependent feature importance. Its outputs guided selection of 3′UTR motifs and synthetic sequence design; reporter assays and a CDK4-specific TCR construct then tested their effects on protein output and CD8+ T-cell cytotoxicity. The model generated design hypotheses; the downstream experiments established the measured motif and T-cell results.

title: Few-shot protein-language-model design yields high-output bicyclogermacrene synthase variants
summary: After experimentally screening activity-enhancing single mutants of LdTPS5, the researchers used PIFS-PLM, a few-shot model that selects features from protein-language-model embeddings using active-site and conserved-residue information, to propose mutation combinations. All 10 tested model-predicted combinations were active; nine produced more than 100 mg/L bicyclogermacrene in yeast, and the top variant produced 213.59 mg/L versus 2.93 mg/L for wild type (about 73-fold higher yield). A related selectivity-optimized combination increased bicyclogermacrene selectivity by 15%.
ai_technology: PIFS-PLM (Physics-Inspired Feature Selection of Protein Language Models), using ESM-2 embeddings with a few-shot mutation-combination classifier
organization: Tsinghua University; Tianjin University; Inner Mongolia University; Zhejiang Institute of Tianjin University

evidence.tested: After experimentally screening activity-enhancing single mutants of LdTPS5, the researchers used PIFS-PLM, a few-shot model that selects features from protein-language-model embeddings using active-site and conserved-residue information, to propose mutation combinations.
evidence.unknown: The 73-fold result is product yield in the reported yeast system, reflecting effects of enzyme activity and expression; it is not a 73-fold increase in catalytic rate. The selectivity improvement was 15%. The model relies on a defined active site/conserved-site set and a small, enzyme-specific experimental dataset. Product profiles differed between cell-free extracts and yeast; these results do not establish universal performance across enzymes or production settings.
evidence.ai_role: After single substitutions were screened and activity-enhancing mutations experimentally validated, PIFS-PLM used 60–100 measured combinations to learn from selected ESM-2 features at active-site and conserved residues and predict beneficial combinations. Ten predicted LdTPS5 variants were tested; all were active, and the top variants substantially increased measured yeast product yield. The model also guided a selectivity optimization test. Initial single-mutation nomination used MM/GBSA or sequence conservation analysis, separate from PIFS-PLM combinatorial predictions.

title: Tree-based machine learning nominates Parabacteroides merdae and N-acetyl-D-mannosamine as ulcerative-colitis alleviators in a mouse model
summary: The researchers combined personalized gut-microbiome community metabolic models from human iHMP data with tree-based machine-learning feature selection to identify microbial strains and metabolites associated with ulcerative-colitis samples. Parabacteroides merdae ATCC 43,184 and N-acetyl-D-mannosamine were among the most predictive features; the strain was also the main modeled microbial contributor to the metabolite. In a DSS-induced mouse colitis experiment, oral administration of the bacterium or metabolite improved reported colitis measures.
ai_technology: Tree-based supervised classifiers including random forest, gradient-boosted regression trees, XGBoost, XGBoost-random forest and LightGBM, combined with individualized genome-scale microbiome community models
organization: Jiangnan University; Wuxi Translational Medicine Research Center; Jiangsu Translational Medicine Research Institute Wuxi Branch; Wuxi People’s Hospital

evidence.tested: In a DSS-induced mouse colitis experiment, oral administration of the bacterium or metabolite improved reported colitis measures.
evidence.unknown: The human data are observational microbiome samples, while intervention was tested in a DSS-induced mouse model, not in people. The animal groups contained eight mice each; findings do not establish treatment efficacy or safety in human ulcerative colitis. Metabolite-production associations came from community-model simulations and were not direct evidence of individual strain production in each person. The model provides candidate prioritization, not a causal human mechanism.
evidence.ai_role: Personalized community metabolic models estimated strain-level contributions to secreted metabolites in human iHMP samples. Tree-based classifiers selected discriminative strain and metabolite features; XGBRF feature attribution ranked P. merdae ATCC 43,184 and N-acetyl-D-mannosamine highly, motivating the mouse validation. The AI analysis nominated these targets; it did not establish human therapeutic efficacy.

title: XGBoost-guided splice switching identifies NEDD4L exon 13 as a TNBC cell vulnerability
summary: SpliceCore’s XGBoost models used splicing-factor RNA-binding and spliceosome information to nominate NEDD4L exon 13 (NEDD4Le13) and the SSO-0205 binding site. In triple-negative breast-cancer MDA-MB-231 cells, SSO-0205 increased exon inclusion (67% versus 15% control), reduced proliferation and decreased migration by 40–50%; the effects were not observed in the non-tumorigenic MCF10A comparator under the reported assays.
ai_technology: SpliceCore XGBoost models with SHAP and out-of-bag feature analysis
organization: Envisagenics, Inc.

evidence.tested: In triple-negative breast-cancer MDA-MB-231 cells, SSO-0205 increased exon inclusion (67% versus 15% control), reduced proliferation and decreased migration by 40–50%; the effects were not observed in the non-tumorigenic MCF10A comparator under the reported assays.
evidence.unknown: Experiments were in vitro, including three breast-cell lines and limited biological replicates; the migration assay used two to three replicates. These results do not establish tumor control in animals, patient benefit, safety or clinical efficacy. The source reports the target as novel in the studied context; this is not evidence that the SSO is a treatment.
evidence.ai_role: The models prospectively nominated the NEDD4L exon-13 splice event, predicted functional SSO binding sites, and prioritized implicated splicing factors. Researchers synthesized selected oligonucleotides and tested splicing, proliferation and migration in cell lines.

title: Machine-learning multi-omics links gut metabolites to GPCR targets and tau changes in Alzheimer’s patient-derived neurons
summary: A machine-learning and multi-omics framework screened 1.09 million pairs across 408 human GPCRs and 335 gut microbial metabolites. It prioritized orphan receptor GPR84 and the metabolite triacanthine, which activated GPR84 in a cell assay. In Alzheimer’s patient-derived iPSC neurons, agmatine reduced C3AR and tau markers, while phenethylamine reduced phosphorylated and total tau in the reported experiments.
ai_technology: Extra Trees machine-learning model integrated with molecular docking, multi-omics and Mendelian-randomization analyses
organization: Cleveland Clinic; Case Western Reserve University; Frederick National Laboratory for Cancer Research; Tel Aviv University and collaborating institutions

evidence.tested: It prioritized orphan receptor GPR84 and the metabolite triacanthine, which activated GPR84 in a cell assay.
evidence.unknown: The metabolite–receptor screen is computational and many pairs remain predictions. Receptor activation was tested in a cell assay and tau-marker effects in patient-derived neurons; these experiments do not demonstrate clinical benefit, in-vivo efficacy or that altered tau markers translate to disease modification. Mendelian-randomization results and model scores are not proof of causality.
evidence.ai_role: The ML model ranked predicted metabolite–GPCR associations over a large search space; multi-omics and genetic analyses prioritized Alzheimer’s-related receptors and metabolites. These predictions guided follow-up assays, including triacanthine activation of GPR84 and testing agmatine and phenethylamine in patient-derived neurons.

title: Machine-learning selection identifies a six-metabolite signature for one-year cardiovascular events after PCI in type 2 diabetes
summary: VSURF feature selection prioritized six serum metabolites—ADPR, 1-methylnicotinamide, D-ribose 5-phosphate, nicotinamide, L-tryptophan and phosphatidylcholine PC(36:2)—for one-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) after PCI in patients with type 2 diabetes. Random-forest and XGBoost models were tested in a nested case-control study and an independent prospective cohort of 301 patients; in the external cohort, reported AUCs were 0.92 and 0.94 for MACEs, respectively. The study also linked NAD+ biosynthesis perturbation to altered bioenergetics, inflammation and proliferation in high-glucose-cultured human aortic smooth-muscle cells.
ai_technology: VSURF random-forest variable selection; random forest and XGBoost classifiers
organization: The First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University; Zhongnan Hospital of Wuhan University

evidence.tested: Random-forest and XGBoost models were tested in a nested case-control study and an independent prospective cohort of 301 patients; in the external cohort, reported AUCs were 0.92 and 0.94 for MACEs, respectively.
evidence.unknown: The discovery component was a matched nested case-control sample (108 cases and 108 controls) from a single center; external validation was in a separate Chinese cohort of 301 patients, so transportability to other populations is unknown. AUCs describe retrospective/prospective cohort validation, not demonstrated clinical utility or improved patient outcomes. HASMC experiments do not prove the metabolites cause clinical events, and the paper states further mechanistic work is needed.
evidence.ai_role: VSURF selected a six-metabolite feature set from serum metabolomic profiles. Random-forest and XGBoost models used that panel to predict one-year post-PCI outcomes; targeted metabolite testing evaluated the panel in a separate prospective cohort.

title: Machine learning prioritizes a protective Arabidopsis leaf fungus that suppresses oomycete infection
summary: Four classifiers (random forest, support-vector machine, logistic regression and multilayer perceptron) used six years of natural Arabidopsis leaf-microbiome data to prioritize taxa associated with Albugo infection status. Follow-up plant assays found that selected health-associated microbes reduced infection; Cystofilobasidium macerans OTU126 gave the strongest individual protection, reducing Albugo infection by an average of 73%. In a 15-member synthetic leaf community, adding this fungus increased the reported infection reduction to 40.25%, compared with 19.36% for the community alone.
ai_technology: Random forest, support-vector machine, logistic regression and multilayer perceptron classifiers with cross-validated feature selection
organization: University of Tübingen; Université Claude Bernard Lyon 1 and collaborating institutions

evidence.tested: Follow-up plant assays found that selected health-associated microbes reduced infection; Cystofilobasidium macerans OTU126 gave the strongest individual protection, reducing Albugo infection by an average of 73%.
evidence.unknown: This is a controlled Arabidopsis–Albugo plant-pathogen model, not a field crop efficacy trial. ML features are associations with infection status; they do not establish the microbes caused naturally observed health status. Isolates were matched to predicted OTUs using marker sequences, which the authors note do not fully establish strain-level functional identity. Genomic terpene-cluster hypotheses were not directly tested. No commercial or field-ready biocontrol performance is established.
evidence.ai_role: Models classified infected versus uninfected plants from microbial community profiles and prioritized disease-associated and health-associated taxa for follow-up. Researchers then tested selected cultured isolates in planta and tested Cystofilobasidium in a synthetic community.

title: Machine learning identifies bacterial strains and combinations that reduce pathogen colonization in Arabidopsis
summary: Random forest and elastic-net models analyzed 136 synthetic communities, each composed of five bacterial strains, and identified strain identity as the strongest predictor of protection against Pseudomonas syringae DC3000 in Arabidopsis. Independent test communities confirmed predictive performance, and follow-up plant assays showed that Acidovorax Leaf76, Rhizobium Leaf68 and Pseudomonas Leaf15 each reduced pathogen colonization by about two orders of magnitude versus axenic controls; a Rhizobium Leaf371–Arthrobacter Leaf337 combination also reduced colonization.
ai_technology: Random forest and elastic-net generalized linear models (GLMNet)
organization: ETH Zurich, Institute of Microbiology

evidence.tested: Independent test communities confirmed predictive performance, and follow-up plant assays showed that Acidovorax Leaf76, Rhizobium Leaf68 and Pseudomonas Leaf15 each reduced pathogen colonization by about two orders of magnitude versus axenic controls; a Rhizobium Leaf371–Arthrobacter Leaf337 combination also reduced colonization.
evidence.unknown: The experiments used gnotobiotic Arabidopsis thaliana and P. syringae DC3000, not field crops. Validation was in the same study, with 24 plants per treatment in the key individual-strain validation assay. The work establishes protection in this model system; it does not establish the underlying mechanisms, efficacy in other plants or field performance.
evidence.ai_role: Models predicted pathogen outcomes from strain presence or abundance across the 136 screened communities and ranked strains by feature importance. Researchers tested the leading strains and combinations in additional plant experiments, validating the model-prioritized protection results.

title: Machine-learning-guided PBMC proteomics identifies SLE diagnosis and activity biomarker panels
summary: A random-forest and OPLS-DA prioritization pipeline applied to peripheral-blood mononuclear-cell proteomics identified candidate protein combinations for distinguishing systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) from healthy and rheumatoid-arthritis controls and for separating active from inactive SLE. ELISA in a separate 80-person cohort supported a six-protein diagnosis panel (IFIT3, MX1, TOMM40, STAT1, STAT2 and OAS3; AUC 0.723 versus healthy controls and 0.815 versus rheumatoid arthritis) and a nine-protein activity panel (AUC 0.990). Single-cell RNA-sequencing analysis mapped several associated interferon-signature proteins to specific immune-cell populations.
ai_technology: POC-SLE: random-forest feature ranking with 1,000 bootstrap iterations, combined with OPLS-DA variable-importance selection
organization: Jinan University; Shenzhen People’s Hospital; collaborating institutions

evidence.tested: ELISA in a separate 80-person cohort supported a six-protein diagnosis panel (IFIT3, MX1, TOMM40, STAT1, STAT2 and OAS3; AUC 0.723 versus healthy controls and 0.815 versus rheumatoid arthritis) and a nine-protein activity panel (AUC 0.990).
evidence.unknown: The study is cross-sectional and the ELISA validation cohort contained 80 people from the same clinical setting; it does not establish longitudinal flare prediction, treatment response, causal mechanisms or clinical utility. The six-protein panel had moderate discrimination versus healthy controls (AUC 0.723) and better but still cohort-specific discrimination versus rheumatoid arthritis (AUC 0.815). The activity-panel AUC of 0.990 was reported for active versus inactive groups in this validation cohort and needs broader independent validation. Authors note limited sample size/ethnic diversity and need for mechanistic study.
evidence.ai_role: The random forest ranked differentially expressed proteins from discovery-cohort PBMC proteomics; its selected proteins were intersected with OPLS-DA features to construct candidate diagnosis and activity panels. Researchers evaluated those panels with ELISA in a separate cohort and used single-cell transcriptomic data to examine immune-cell sources.

title: Integrated proteomics and metabolomics with LASSO nominate a four-analyte early IgA-nephropathy plasma panel
summary: A study of biopsy-confirmed IgA nephropathy (IgAN) integrated plasma proteomics and untargeted metabolomics and used LASSO logistic regression to select PRKAR2A, IL6ST, SOS1 and palmitoleic acid as candidate discriminators from healthy controls. The panel had AUC 0.994 in the training set and 0.977 in the test split; ELISA assays in a separate 9-case/10-control sample set yielded an AUC of 0.91. Proteomic and metabolomic analyses also indicated complement/immune activation and altered energy and amino-acid metabolism in the studied cases.
ai_technology: LASSO logistic regression (glmnet), with tenfold cross-validation and additional random-forest/SVM model checks
organization: Zhejiang Provincial People’s Hospital and collaborating institutions

evidence.tested: A study of biopsy-confirmed IgA nephropathy (IgAN) integrated plasma proteomics and untargeted metabolomics and used LASSO logistic regression to select PRKAR2A, IL6ST, SOS1 and palmitoleic acid as candidate discriminators from healthy controls.
evidence.unknown: This is an early candidate biomarker result, not a validated clinical test or biopsy replacement. The discovery analysis included 33 biopsy-confirmed IgAN cases and 20 healthy controls; the separate ELISA group contained only 9 IgAN cases and 10 controls from the same hospital. The test split is small, and the study did not test specificity against other kidney diseases or demonstrate prospective/clinical utility. The proposed biomarker biology remains speculative.
evidence.ai_role: LASSO feature selection on integrated proteomic and metabolomic measurements nominated the four-analyte panel; the study evaluated its classification in a held-out split and measured the selected analytes by ELISA in an independent sample batch.

title: Machine-learning proteomics prioritizes four plasma markers associated with ankylosing-spondylitis activity
summary: A plasma-proteomics study of 48 active ankylosing-spondylitis (AS) patients, 21 stable-stage patients and 35 healthy controls combined random-forest and OPLS-DA scores to prioritize candidate markers. SAA1, FERMT3, ILK and TLN1 were elevated in active-stage AS and returned toward control levels in stable-stage patients; ELISA in a separate cohort (27 active, 28 stable, 24 controls) reproduced these patterns. A combined ELISA model distinguished active AS from healthy controls with AUC 0.932. FERMT3, ILK and TLN1 are integrin-pathway proteins.
ai_technology: Machine-learning biomarker scoring matrix combining random forest and OPLS-DA
organization: Guang’anmen Hospital, China Academy of Chinese Medical Sciences; Beijing Institute of Lifeomics; collaborating institutions

evidence.tested: SAA1, FERMT3, ILK and TLN1 were elevated in active-stage AS and returned toward control levels in stable-stage patients; ELISA in a separate cohort (27 active, 28 stable, 24 controls) reproduced these patterns.
evidence.unknown: This is an observational, cross-sectional plasma-biomarker study; it does not establish causal integrin-pathway activity, prognosis over time, treatment response, or clinical utility. The independent ELISA cohort had 79 participants and was drawn from the same clinical setting. The combined AUC 0.932 applies to active AS versus healthy controls; discrimination against other inflammatory diseases was not demonstrated. SAA1 has been previously reported as an AS-associated marker; the AI-supported novelty is the combined panel and the integrin-related proteins, not discovery of SAA1 itself.
evidence.ai_role: Random-forest classification accuracy/Gini importance and OPLS-DA variable-importance scores were combined with proteomic fold-change and significance terms to rank candidate proteins. The team then measured the four prioritized proteins by ELISA in an independent cohort.

title: Machine-learning-guided electrochemical screening isolates five new reaction products
summary: A machine-learning-guided, chemist-in-the-loop screen predicted electrochemical reactivity for 38,865 potential partners with 1,4-dicyanobenzene (DCB). Automated tests of 20 prioritized, previously untested partners yielded DCB conversion in 16; five produced an isolable major product judged of synthetic or mechanistic interest. The reported examples include a silyl-enol-ether coupling and electrochemical benzylic arylation of benzyltrimethylsilane with DCB, plus three mechanistically unexpected products.
ai_technology: Machine-learning-guided reaction-competency classifier using a DFT-informed molecular representation
organization: Massachusetts Institute of Technology; collaborating institutions

evidence.tested: Automated tests of 20 prioritized, previously untested partners yielded DCB conversion in 16; five produced an isolable major product judged of synthetic or mechanistic interest.
evidence.unknown: This is an early reaction-discovery demonstration under one fixed DCB electrolysis system, not a general reaction predictor or optimized synthetic platform. Seven of the 16 DCB-converting selected reactions gave complex mixtures without an appreciable single isolated product; five yielded isolable major products, reported at low yields and without method optimization. DCB conversion alone does not establish a product identity, and the three mechanistically ambiguous outcomes require further study.
evidence.ai_role: The model screened a 38,865-member virtual set for reaction competency and, with chemist selection, prioritized 20 new partners for automated electrolysis. The experiments measured DCB conversion, then product analysis isolated and characterized five major products from the selected set.

title: Machine-learning-guided photoredox design experimentally enables three transformations
summary: A workflow combining a variational-autoencoder latent space of 11,069 literature photoredox reactions with random-forest catalyst/reagent recommendations was used to propose three transformations. Experiments synthesized a previously inaccessible substituted dihydroquinolinone 43 using fac-Ir(ppy)3, a related oxidative cross-coupling product 46 in 64% yield, and heterocycle product 49 in 74% yield. The paper presents these as experimentally validated transformations identified through model-assisted precedent retrieval and condition selection.
ai_technology: Variational autoencoder for reaction-space navigation and random-forest multilabel catalyst/reagent recommendation
organization: Wuhan University; HOURS Inc.; collaborating institutions

evidence.tested: Experiments synthesized a previously inaccessible substituted dihydroquinolinone 43 using fac-Ir(ppy)3, a related oxidative cross-coupling product 46 in 64% yield, and heterocycle product 49 in 74% yield.
evidence.unknown: The work is a human-guided photoredox design workflow, not autonomous synthesis. The three examples were selected by researchers and use a literature-trained model; the paper establishes feasibility for these tested transformations, not general transfer or broad yield improvement. Reported 64% and 74% yields apply only to the specific demonstrated products; further optimization and substrate-scope work are needed.
evidence.ai_role: The VAE organized 11,069 literature-derived reactions to retrieve traceable precedents; random-forest models recommended catalyst and reagent classes for proposed reactant-product pairs. Chemists used the model-suggested conditions to test three transformations, including two modifications beyond the reported precedent and one previously undocumented photoredox synthesis, then measured isolated product yields.

title: Cross-tissue machine learning prioritizes a 13-gene rheumatoid-arthritis activity score
summary: A machine-learning feature-selection pipeline integrated public whole-blood (1,885 samples) and synovial-tissue (284 samples) transcriptomic datasets and selected a 13-gene rheumatoid-arthritis score. Across five independent transcriptomic datasets, the score tracked DAS28 disease activity, distinguished rheumatoid arthritis from osteoarthritis, separated polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis from healthy controls, and was associated with treatment effects. In an independent immunoblot cohort, two of six tested proteins, TNFAIP6/TSG-6 and HSP90AB1/HSP90, were confirmed.
ai_technology: Cross-tissue machine-learning feature-selection pipeline for transcriptomic data
organization: University of California, San Francisco; Oregon Health & Science University

evidence.tested: In an independent immunoblot cohort, two of six tested proteins, TNFAIP6/TSG-6 and HSP90AB1/HSP90, were confirmed.
evidence.unknown: The transcriptomic inputs were previously published datasets and the reported clinical associations are observational; the study does not establish a deployable diagnostic test or causal disease mechanism. The independent protein follow-up confirmed two of six proteins tested, not the entire 13-gene panel, and validation in larger prospective cohorts is needed. Treatment-effect association should not be interpreted as prospective prediction of individual response.
evidence.ai_role: The pipeline selected a compact 13-gene signature from public blood and synovial expression datasets; the study evaluated its association with disease activity and diagnostic distinctions across five independent transcriptomic datasets, then tested six selected proteins by immunoblot in a separate patient cohort.

title: Random-forest metabolite profiling reduces false-positive newborn screens for four inherited disorders
summary: A 121-analyte LC–MS/MS panel combined established markers, untargeted-metabolomics features and chromatographically resolved isobars with random-forest classification of California newborn-screen dried blood spots. In 883 archived infant samples, the study reports that the second-tier approach maintained 100% sensitivity while reducing false positives by 83% for glutaric acidemia type I, 84% for methylmalonic acidemia, 100% for ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency and 51% for very-long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency. Several long-chain acylcarnitine and hydroxy-acylcarnitine isobar features contributed to classification, although their chemical identities were unresolved.
ai_technology: Random Forest classifier trained on targeted LC–MS/MS metabolite profiles
organization: Stanford Health Care; Yale University; California Department of Public Health

evidence.tested: In 883 archived infant samples, the study reports that the second-tier approach maintained 100% sensitivity while reducing false positives by 83% for glutaric acidemia type I, 84% for methylmalonic acidemia, 100% for ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency and 51% for very-long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency.
evidence.unknown: This was a proof-of-principle second-tier simulation on residual archived California newborn-screen specimens, not a prospective implementation study. The validation sample was not a fully independent external set, and archived-sample degradation and processing batch effects limited biomarker discovery; some discriminating isobar identities and biological significance remain unknown. The reported sensitivity and false-positive reductions are cohort-specific and do not establish improved health outcomes or routine clinical utility.
