Researchers report that these experimentally successful settings solved a process-development problem that had resisted several months of manual trials, enabling GRCop-42 fabrication on lower-power platforms. This is a manufacturing-process result for an existing alloy, not a new alloy composition.
ai_technology: BEAM (Bayesian Experimental design for Additive Manufacturing)
organization: Washington State University

evidence.tested: A closed-loop Bayesian experimental-design method, BEAM, found multiple defect-free directed-energy-deposition configurations for GRCop-42 copper alloy at infrared laser powers from 950 down to 500 W.
evidence.unknown: The paper establishes feasible configurations in one directed-energy-deposition system for one alloy. It does not demonstrate aerospace-qualified components, service life or broader transfer to other machines and alloys. The reported defect-free characterization is bounded to the study's print assessment.
evidence.ai_role: BEAM uses a probabilistic surrogate and adaptive experimental-design strategy to select small batches of process configurations for laboratory testing; print outcomes update its feasibility model and guide subsequent tests. The loop identified successful configurations at 950, 700, 600 and 500 W, where prior manual trials had failed for months.

title: Machine-learning screening and experiments identify two new superconductors, Be₂HfNb₂ and Be₂Hf₂Nb
summary: An AI-accelerated workflow screened more than 1.3 million material structures, combining a graph-neural-network model of superconducting properties with density-functional calculations and stability filters. The researchers experimentally synthesized and confirmed superconductivity in Be₂HfNb₂ and Be₂Hf₂Nb, reporting two previously unreported compounds among 741 computationally screened stable candidates. The two compounds were confirmed in the Be₂Nb₃ substitution series; other listed candidates remain computational predictions.
ai_technology: BEE-NET equivariant graph neural networks in an AI-accelerated high-throughput screening workflow
organization: University of Florida; Oak Ridge National Laboratory; Quantum Formatics

evidence.tested: An AI-accelerated workflow screened more than 1.3 million material structures, combining a graph-neural-network model of superconducting properties with density-functional calculations and stability filters.
evidence.unknown: The AI model accelerated candidate selection but did not itself perform the synthesis; DFT and laboratory confirmation were essential. The paper reports an overall screening precision of 86%, so most candidate predictions were not experimentally verified in this study.
evidence.ai_role: Predicted Eliashberg spectral functions and superconducting transition temperatures to prioritize candidate structures, followed by DFT stability calculations and experimental synthesis/characterization by the research team.

title: Machine-learning triage identifies a dormant wandering black hole in a galaxy’s outskirts
summary: The off-nuclear transient TDE 2025abcr revealed a dormant supermassive black hole about 9.3 kiloparsecs from its host galaxy’s center, with a mass described as similar to the Milky Way’s central black hole. A machine-learning program searching for tidal-disruption flares anywhere in the sky selected the event for follow-up three months after deployment; astronomers then collected multi-instrument evidence and interpreted it as the strongest known wandering-black-hole case. Its precise origin remains uncertain, with stripped remnant and black-hole-ejection scenarios both discussed.
ai_technology: Off-nuclear tidal-disruption-event classifier (tdescore)
organization: University of Maryland; NASA Goddard Space Flight Center; University of California Observatories and collaborators

evidence.tested: The off-nuclear transient TDE 2025abcr revealed a dormant supermassive black hole about 9.3 kiloparsecs from its host galaxy’s center, with a mass described as similar to the Milky Way’s central black hole.
evidence.unknown: The specific off-nuclear transient was AI-selected, but the paper’s evidence and interpretation are observational follow-up, not a model-generated discovery. The black hole’s formation history is unresolved; the host has no obvious surrounding galaxy at the black-hole position.
evidence.ai_role: Ranked the transient as a candidate tidal-disruption event away from a galaxy nucleus, prompting spectroscopic and multi-wavelength follow-up; the astrophysical interpretation relied on subsequent human analysis and observations.

title: AI-guided autonomous experiments map phase domains in bismuth–titanium oxide films
summary: A robotic active-learning campaign using SARA-H mapped processing regions that stabilize δ-Bi₂O₃ and Bi₂Ti₂O₇ in thin films and examined dwell-dependent phase behavior in the Bi–Ti–O system. The study also experimentally supported the prediction that bismuth substitution in TiO₂ inhibits the anatase-to-rutile transformation. This is a human-in-the-loop experimental materials result; the compounds/phases were not all newly discovered, while the mapped processing domains and comparative evidence are the study-specific contribution.
ai_technology: SARA-H (Scientific Autonomous Reasoning Agent with human input) and automated probabilistic phase labeling
organization: Cornell University; California Institute of Technology; Liquid Sunlight Alliance

evidence.tested: A robotic active-learning campaign using SARA-H mapped processing regions that stabilize δ-Bi₂O₃ and Bi₂Ti₂O₇ in thin films and examined dwell-dependent phase behavior in the Bi–Ti–O system.
evidence.unknown: This is a published, human-guided experimental study, but the phases themselves are not claimed as newly discovered compounds. The study-specific finding is experimentally mapped processing/dwell behavior in the Bi–Ti–O campaign and evidence that Bi substitution inhibits anatase-to-rutile transformation. Scope is thin films and tested processing conditions, not bulk phase stability or universal behavior.
evidence.ai_role: Used phase-identification outputs to select and interpret robotic laser-annealing experiments, with human domain guidance improving search efficiency.

title: Multiscale machine-learning microscopy identifies robust paleomagnetic carriers in meteorite WIS 91600
summary: A multiscale microscopy study of carbonaceous chondrite WIS 91600 used a deep-learning classifier to segment magnetic remanence-carrying ensembles and quantify their volume and texture. Combined chemical mapping, 3D nanotomography, and diffraction showed fine matrix-hosted magnetite has paleomagnetic recording potential comparable to magnetite framboids but is less susceptible to strong interactions; transient heating also reduced the contribution of matrix pyrrhotite through its vacancy-ordering state. This is one meteorite case study, and the mineralogical conclusions draw on the full microscopy and diffraction workflow, not AI alone.
ai_technology: UNET segmentation, SIGMA interactive machine-learning mineral analysis, and few-shot image segmentation
organization: University of Cambridge and collaborators

evidence.tested: A multiscale microscopy study of carbonaceous chondrite WIS 91600 used a deep-learning classifier to segment magnetic remanence-carrying ensembles and quantify their volume and texture.
evidence.unknown: The source is a single meteorite case study. The AI classified/quantified image ensembles, while mineral identities and remanence interpretation use additional microscopy, chemical mapping, nanotomography, and diffraction; extrapolation to other carbonaceous chondrites requires more samples.
evidence.ai_role: Classified remanence-carrying ensembles in microscopy images and quantified their volumes and morphologies; complementary imaging and diffraction supported mineral identification and interpretation.

title: A machine-learning-assisted TESS search confirms a previously unknown hot Jupiter
summary: The T16 pipeline processed 83.7 million TESS Cycle 1 full-frame-image light curves and reported 10,091 new transiting-planet candidates, alongside previously known candidates. Radial-velocity follow-up confirmed TIC 183374187 b as a newly identified hot Jupiter, demonstrating that the semi-automated search yielded at least one bona fide new planet. Most entries in the catalog remain candidates rather than confirmed planets.
ai_technology: T16 semi-automated transit search with random-forest machine-learning vetting
organization: Princeton University and collaborating institutions

evidence.tested: The T16 pipeline processed 83.7 million TESS Cycle 1 full-frame-image light curves and reported 10,091 new transiting-planet candidates, alongside previously known candidates.
evidence.unknown: The 10,091 entries are planet candidates, most unconfirmed. The cited discovery claim here is limited to TIC 183374187 b, which the authors say was confirmed with radial-velocity follow-up; the pipeline is described as machine-learning-assisted, not fully autonomous.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning-assisted pipeline classified light curves and prioritized possible transit signals; human vetting and Magellan/PFS radial-velocity observations confirmed the highlighted planet.

title: Machine-learning X-ray analysis provides bulk evidence for a Bragg-glass phase in PdₓErTe₃
summary: Researchers combined extensive X-ray diffraction with X-ray Temperature Clustering (X-TEC) to identify Bragg-glass signatures in the charge-density-wave material PdₓErTe₃. Their analysis extracted diffraction features across about 20,000 Brillouin zones and found a diverging correlation length and a phase diagram consistent with a Bragg-glass transition. The result provides bulk diffraction evidence for a phase that had been difficult to establish experimentally.
ai_technology: X-ray Temperature Clustering (X-TEC), a machine-learning analysis of X-ray diffraction peaks
organization: Cornell University; Stanford University; Argonne National Laboratory; University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign

evidence.tested: Researchers combined extensive X-ray diffraction with X-ray Temperature Clustering (X-TEC) to identify Bragg-glass signatures in the charge-density-wave material PdₓErTe₃.
evidence.unknown: The authors frame the result as evidence for the Bragg-glass phase based on characteristic diffraction behavior, rather than direct imaging of all underlying defects. Machine learning enabled the scale of peak extraction; physical interpretation and measurements were done by the team.
evidence.ai_role: Automatically extracted and clustered charge-density-wave diffraction peaks across temperature and momentum, enabling high-throughput estimation of peak spread/correlation length from a large set of Brillouin zones; researchers interpreted these features as evidence for Bragg-glass order.

title: Machine-learning image search helps identify Pavo, an isolated star-forming dwarf galaxy
summary: A search combining low-surface-brightness galaxy detection and machine-learning candidate classification identified Pavo in Dark Energy Camera Legacy Survey imaging. Follow-up Magellan imaging resolved young and old stellar populations and measured a tip-of-the-red-giant-branch distance of about 1.99 Mpc, establishing Pavo as an extremely isolated, low-mass star-forming dwarf galaxy just beyond the Local Group.
ai_technology: Machine-learning image candidate classifier used with low-surface-brightness galaxy search algorithms
organization: University of Arizona; University of Chicago; University of Minnesota Duluth; and collaborators

evidence.tested: A search combining low-surface-brightness galaxy detection and machine-learning candidate classification identified Pavo in Dark Energy Camera Legacy Survey imaging.
evidence.unknown: The AI contributed candidate classification within a broader image-search workflow. The discovery was verified by follow-up observations and astrophysical analysis. AAS conference abstract from 2024 also describes this same Pavo discovery and is not a separate result.
evidence.ai_role: Classified image-search candidates in DECaLS imaging; the search team selected Pavo for follow-up, and telescope imaging and color-magnitude analysis established its distance and galaxy properties.

title: Deep learning reveals more than 500 previously unrecognized earthquakes beneath David Glacier
summary: A deep-learning analysis of regional Antarctic seismic records identified more than 500 previously unrecognized intermediate-depth earthquakes roughly 100–150 km beneath David Glacier in East Antarctica. The earthquakes occur within a tectonic plate rather than at a plate boundary. The authors explain the concentration through bending stresses associated with variable thermally driven uplift and an abrupt change in lithospheric strength; the ice sheet may also affect regional stress.
ai_technology: Deep-learning seismic-event detector applied to regional seismic records
organization: University of Alabama; Complutense University of Madrid; University of Oklahoma

evidence.tested: A deep-learning analysis of regional Antarctic seismic records identified more than 500 previously unrecognized intermediate-depth earthquakes roughly 100–150 km beneath David Glacier in East Antarctica.
evidence.unknown: The discovery concerns a newly recognized concentration of intraplate events, not a new earthquake mechanism conclusively proven. Proposed stress sources are interpretations; the paper notes similar events elsewhere may remain undetected.
evidence.ai_role: Detected intermediate-depth earthquake signals in regional seismic data that were not recognized in prior catalogs; the authors then located and interpreted the events using seismological and geodynamic analysis.

title: Swin-Transformer discovery of planetary nebulae with spectroscopic confirmation in VPHAS+
summary: A Swin-Transformer search of VPHAS+ Hα images identified faint, resolved planetary-nebula candidates in crowded Galactic fields that prior point-source searches missed. Follow-up spectroscopy and HASH classification of 31 targets found 16 true, two likely and four possible planetary nebulae, alongside contaminants and a supernova-remnant fragment. This is one validated search-sample result, not 22 equally secure confirmations.
ai_technology: Swin-Transformer deep-learning classifier trained on known planetary nebulae
organization: The University of Hong Kong; Taiyuan University of Technology; Peng Cheng Laboratory

evidence.tested: A Swin-Transformer search of VPHAS+ Hα images identified faint, resolved planetary-nebula candidates in crowded Galactic fields that prior point-source searches missed.
evidence.unknown: The 31 follow-up targets were selected from more than 800 high-quality candidates, so the sample is not a completeness or population estimate. Spectroscopic classifications comprise 16 true, two likely and four possible PNe; these confidence levels are not merged into a claim that all 22 are confirmed. Two non-emitter late-type contaminants and other emission-line contaminants were found. The result counts the paper-level AI-assisted search and validation campaign once.
evidence.ai_role: Scanned survey images and ranked candidate planetary nebulae; follow-up spectroscopy and standard HASH classification established which selected targets were nebulae and which were contaminants.

title: Active learning identifies 28 new DFT-validated pressure-induced phase transitions
summary: Across 13 active-learning cycles, a graph neural network screened phase pairs for pressure-induced transitions and selected cases for density-functional-theory (DFT) calculations. DFT confirmed 28 previously unreported transformations; 14 high-pressure phases were dynamically stable at transition pressure, including 10 also predicted dynamically stable at zero pressure. The study also identifies a previously unrecorded dynamically stable monoclinic P2₁/c phase of Cr₂O₃.
ai_technology: MEGNet graph neural network with five-model ensemble and iterative active learning
organization: Purdue University

evidence.tested: Across 13 active-learning cycles, a graph neural network screened phase pairs for pressure-induced transitions and selected cases for density-functional-theory (DFT) calculations.
evidence.unknown: These are computational predictions corroborated by DFT, not experimentally synthesized or observed phases. Of 28 transitions, 14 high-pressure structures were dynamically stable at transition pressure; only 10 were also predicted stable at zero pressure. Two selected phase-pair calculations remained difficult to converge. The paper's discovery count excludes 18 rediscoveries, and individual stability remains subject to DFT approximations.
evidence.ai_role: The GNN screened 7,677 phase pairs for consensus transition-pressure predictions. Active learning selected high-confidence pairs for DFT equation-of-state calculations, and the resulting DFT outcomes were added to training data for subsequent cycles. The AI search was the discovery and prioritization mechanism; DFT calculations supplied the physical verification of the transitions.

title: Representation learning uncovers the extragalactic X-ray transient XRT 200515 in Chandra archives
summary: A representation-learning pipeline searched archived Chandra event data and identified XRT 200515, a previously unnoticed extragalactic fast X-ray transient in the Large Magellanic Cloud. Its light curve has a sharp sub-10-second hard burst followed by an approximately 800-second oscillating tail with spectral softening. The paper discusses possible origins including a low-energy giant magnetar flare or a Type I burst from a faint low-mass X-ray binary; the source's physical nature is unresolved.
ai_technology: Unsupervised representation-learning pipeline using sparse autoencoders, dimensionality reduction and density-based clustering
organization: Stanford University; Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics; Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory; collaborators

evidence.tested: A representation-learning pipeline searched archived Chandra event data and identified XRT 200515, a previously unnoticed extragalactic fast X-ray transient in the Large Magellanic Cloud.
evidence.unknown: The transient is a real source-reported observational event, but its astrophysical progenitor remains unresolved. The study also catalogs candidate flares and dips; those catalog candidates are not counted as separately confirmed discoveries.
evidence.ai_role: Converted Chandra photon event files into time-energy representations, learned low-dimensional embeddings and clustered similar events; anomalous transient-dominated clusters surfaced XRT 200515 for subsequent human inspection and astrophysical analysis.

title: Data-driven equations reveal rainfall-linked North Atlantic decadal variability
summary: Using SINDy equation discovery on monthly observational indices from 1950–2022, researchers derived three linked low-order equations for Atlantic Multidecadal Variability, the North Atlantic Oscillation and North Atlantic precipitation. The model recovered a distinct roughly 20-year component and highlighted precipitation-linked terms as robust components of the learned dynamics; tests against the independent 1900–1939 record found skill for statistics of the variability indices and rainfall. The equations generate hypotheses about ocean-atmosphere feedbacks; they do not establish a single causal mechanism or guarantee forecasts.
ai_technology: Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy) equation-discovery algorithm
organization: University of Oxford; UK Centre for Ecology & Hydrology; UK Met Office

evidence.tested: Using SINDy equation discovery on monthly observational indices from 1950–2022, researchers derived three linked low-order equations for Atlantic Multidecadal Variability, the North Atlantic Oscillation and North Atlantic precipitation.
evidence.unknown: The learned equations are compact models/hypotheses from observational associations. The paper and Oxford source note that proposed mechanisms need further evaluation; reported hindcast skill is not prospective climate prediction validation.
evidence.ai_role: Searched candidate dynamical models against observational time series and selected sparse, interpretable coupled equations; the researchers analyzed robust equation terms and compared the resulting model against a historical holdout period.

title: LHCb reports first single-experiment evidence for B⁰ → μ⁺μ⁻ decay
summary: Using 18 fb⁻¹ of Run 3 data and earlier LHCb data, the collaboration reports first single-experiment evidence for the rare B⁰→μ⁺μ⁻ decay, with a combined significance of 3.2σ and measured branching fraction (1.14 +0.42/−0.39 stat. +0.06/−0.05 syst.)×10⁻¹⁰. A boosted decision tree classified candidates and suppressed combinatorial background in the fit. This is evidence below the 5σ discovery threshold; results agree with Standard Model expectations. The date is the original preprint submission; CERN announced the result on 3 November 2026.
ai_technology: LHCb boosted decision tree (BDT) candidate classifier and multivariate trigger classifiers
organization: LHCb Collaboration; CERN

evidence.tested: Using 18 fb⁻¹ of Run 3 data and earlier LHCb data, the collaboration reports first single-experiment evidence for the rare B⁰→μ⁺μ⁻ decay, with a combined significance of 3.2σ and measured branching fraction (1.14 +0.42/−0.39 stat.
evidence.unknown: This is a preprint submitted to Physical Review X and reports 3.2σ evidence, not a 5σ observation. Earlier joint LHCb–CMS evidence was not confirmed by later Run 1–2 analyses; this result is the first single-experiment evidence, not the first ever claim. The paper reports all measurements as consistent with Standard Model expectations. Machine learning contributes to candidate selection/background control along with substantial detector upgrades.
evidence.ai_role: The primary analysis uses a BDT to suppress combinatorial background, scores candidates and divides the dimuon mass fit into five response bins to improve signal sensitivity; it also uses multivariate classifiers in the software trigger. CERN states that machine-learning background suppression, together with detector upgrades, enabled the analysis to isolate these rare signals. The measured evidence comes from the collaboration's collision data and statistical fit, not an AI prediction.

title: Machine learning reveals two previously undetected phases in Rydberg-atom quantum-simulator data
summary: An interpretable hybrid unsupervised/supervised learning analysis of experimental snapshots from a programmable Rydberg-atom array mapped phase regions on a square lattice and identified signatures of two previously undetected phases: boundary-ordered and rhombic. The rhombic pattern had been predicted theoretically, so the result is its experimental-data signature rather than a wholly unanticipated theoretical phase; the boundary-ordered phase was revealed from edge correlations.
ai_technology: Hybrid-correlation convolutional neural network (Hybrid-CCNN) with PCA and clustering
organization: Harvard University; Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Cornell University; collaborators

evidence.tested: An interpretable hybrid unsupervised/supervised learning analysis of experimental snapshots from a programmable Rydberg-atom array mapped phase regions on a square lattice and identified signatures of two previously undetected phases: boundary-ordered and rhombic.
evidence.unknown: The study reanalyzes experimental quantum-simulator snapshots; the rhombic phase was previously predicted by theory, while the paper reports its finite-size experimental manifestation. The paper characterizes phases using data and numerical interpretation, not bulk material synthesis.
evidence.ai_role: Unsupervised clustering exposed phase regions in experimental snapshots; interpretable supervised correlator networks refined boundaries and identified edge and multi-point correlation motifs characteristic of the previously undetected boundary-ordered and rhombic regions.

title: Deep learning resolves subtle seismic-wave changes across the 2016 Norcia earthquake cycle
summary: A seven-layer convolutional neural network classified raw seismic waveforms recorded near Italy’s 2016 Mw 6.5 Norcia earthquake as pre- or post-mainshock and separated time-to-failure intervals with over 90% test accuracy. The authors interpret the model’s performance, frequency dependence and null tests as evidence that local waveforms encode evolving attenuation and elastic properties consistent with progressive fault damage before rupture and postseismic recovery.
ai_technology: Seven-layer convolutional neural network trained on local seismic waveforms
organization: Sapienza University of Rome; Pennsylvania State University

evidence.tested: A seven-layer convolutional neural network classified raw seismic waveforms recorded near Italy’s 2016 Mw 6.5 Norcia earthquake as pre- or post-mainshock and separated time-to-failure intervals with over 90% test accuracy.
evidence.unknown: Authors studied one earthquake sequence and state that generalization to other tectonic settings and prospective real-time precursor detection remain untested. Related changes in elastic properties were already reported by field studies; the paper's new contribution is applying deep learning to infer them from this local waveform sequence.
evidence.ai_role: Classified the waveform signals by their temporal relation to the mainshock; controlled tests using incorrect mainshock times, distant stations and filtered frequencies helped expose subtle local seismic-wave property changes associated with the fault cycle.

title: Three spectroscopically confirmed z≈6 quasars found through contrastive learning
summary: A self-supervised contrastive-learning search of Dark Energy Survey imaging isolated a group of 11 sources that included seven known z≈6 quasars. Follow-up Gemini-South and archival NTT spectroscopy confirmed three additional quasars at redshifts 5.94–6.07. One source, J0109−5424, shows evidence of a foreground object and is a lensed-quasar candidate, but its multiple-image status requires high-resolution imaging.
ai_technology: Self-supervised contrastive-learning neural network trained on Dark Energy Survey imaging data
organization: University of Cambridge; Max Planck Institute for Astronomy; Gemini Observatory/NSF NOIRLab; INAF; collaborators

evidence.tested: A self-supervised contrastive-learning search of Dark Energy Survey imaging isolated a group of 11 sources that included seven known z≈6 quasars.
evidence.unknown: The three quasar identifications are spectroscopically confirmed, but the possible gravitational lens interpretation of J0109−5424 remains unconfirmed pending high-resolution imaging. The reported 91% efficiency refers to ten quasars among the eleven-source island, including seven previously known objects; three of the four previously unclassified targets were confirmed quasars. It is not a universal completeness estimate.
evidence.ai_role: Grouped sources into a learned embedding-space island that prioritized four unclassified candidates; spectroscopy confirmed three as quasars, including one source missed by conventional color selection because foreground light contaminated the photometry.

title: AI-enhanced seismic catalog exposes a ring-fault system at Campi Flegrei
summary: A retrained machine-learning workflow applied to continuous seismic records from 2022–2025 expanded the Campi Flegrei earthquake catalog from about 12,000 to more than 54,000 events. The more complete locations delineated a sharply defined, shallow caldera ring-fault system, illuminated previously unclear northern faults, and identified very shallow hybrid events likely associated with the hydrothermal system. The authors report no direct signature of upward magma migration in the analyzed data.
ai_technology: Retrained machine-learning seismic detection and phase-picking workflow developed at Stanford
organization: Stanford University; Istituto Nazionale di Geofisica e Vulcanologia – Osservatorio Vesuviano; University of Naples Federico II

evidence.tested: A retrained machine-learning workflow applied to continuous seismic records from 2022–2025 expanded the Campi Flegrei earthquake catalog from about 12,000 to more than 54,000 events.
evidence.unknown: The observations cover 21 January 2022–20 March 2025. The inferred hydrothermal source is described as likely, and the mapped faults do not establish imminent eruption or earthquake timing. Full Science article text was access-restricted in this review; the original abstract and reporting institution's article were read.
evidence.ai_role: Detected and located small earthquakes missed by the prior monitoring catalog, providing denser observations that made the ring-fault geometry and shallow seismic structures visible.

title: Machine-learning-guided synthesis confirms superconductivity in Mo20Re6Si4
summary: Researchers used a deep-learning composition model to prioritize a sigma-phase ternary compound, synthesized Mo20Re6Si4, and measured bulk superconductivity with a critical temperature of 5.4 K. Magnetic susceptibility and a specific-heat anomaly support the bulk transition. The paper reports mixed model performance on its small test set and describes the model as guidance alongside chemical intuition.
ai_technology: Deep-learning neural network that classifies compositions as superconducting and predicts critical temperature
organization: Rutgers University; Flatiron Institute; University of South Carolina; Princeton University; Michigan State University

evidence.tested: Researchers used a deep-learning composition model to prioritize a sigma-phase ternary compound, synthesized Mo20Re6Si4, and measured bulk superconductivity with a critical temperature of 5.4 K.
evidence.unknown: The result is experimental and supported by bulk measurements, but the preprint reports a small, specialized evaluation set and mixed predictor performance. Chemical intuition also guided candidate selection; AI's contribution was a search hint, not independent autonomous discovery. The compound is a materials-physics finding rather than a new general superconducting mechanism.
evidence.ai_role: Provided composition-based hints that helped researchers select Mo20Re6Si4 for synthesis; laboratory resistivity, magnetic-susceptibility and specific-heat measurements established the superconducting result.

title: Semi-supervised image classifiers lead to confirmation of a new lensed quasar
summary: Semi-supervised image classifiers trained on Pan-STARRS and DESI imagery surfaced five quasar-lens candidates for Keck follow-up. Spectroscopy confirmed GRALJ140833.73+042229.98 as a previously undiscovered gravitationally lensed quasar: a z=2.998 quasar lensed by a z=0.542 early-type galaxy. Three other targets were quasar-plus-star or quasar-plus-galaxy interlopers, and one remained unresolved.
ai_technology: Semi-supervised image-classifier pipeline using a convolutional autoencoder with a classifier, plus a convolutional network trained with virtual adversarial training
organization: University of Sydney; University of California, Irvine; California Institute of Technology; collaborators

evidence.tested: Semi-supervised image classifiers trained on Pan-STARRS and DESI imagery surfaced five quasar-lens candidates for Keck follow-up.
evidence.unknown: Only one of five observed candidates was confirmed; three were interlopers and one could not be resolved. The successful identification came from a previous model iteration during model development, so this is an AI-assisted discovery with limited follow-up yield, not a prospective performance demonstration.
evidence.ai_role: Image-only classifiers prioritized candidate lenses; a prior iteration of the autoencoder-classifier surfaced the object, which Keck spectroscopy subsequently confirmed. The paper notes the observed candidates were selected during model development, not from a strictly prospective frozen-model test.

title: Self-supervised imaging search identifies 16 spectroscopically confirmed quasars at z≈5.94–6.45
summary: Contrastive learning on DESI Legacy Survey DR10 multiband images, followed by SED-fit prioritization, selected sources for spectroscopy; follow-up confirmed 16 quasars at z=5.94–6.45. Several show uncommon narrow Lyα lines, strong Lyα+N V equivalent widths or mildly red observed-frame NIR slopes, and three lie in regions traditional color cuts would miss. The 16-object reported sample includes 15 new literature discoveries and one independently confirmed DESI DR1 source; the 45% follow-up yield includes previously known quasars among 40 observed targets.
ai_technology: Self-supervised contrastive-learning neural network applied to DESI Legacy Survey DR10 multiband images, with SED-fit prioritization
organization: Max Planck Institute for Astronomy; Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile; Jet Propulsion Laboratory; Universidad Diego Portales; University of Geneva; collaborators

evidence.tested: Contrastive learning on DESI Legacy Survey DR10 multiband images, followed by SED-fit prioritization, selected sources for spectroscopy; follow-up confirmed 16 quasars at z=5.94–6.45.
evidence.unknown: Only 40 candidates were followed up from 1,139 high-priority candidates, so the reported 45% follow-up yield is not completeness or precision over the full sample. That yield counts 18 quasars among 40 targets, including previously known recoveries. The publisher abstract calls all 16 new; the paper body distinguishes 15 new literature discoveries and one additional candidate independently confirmed in DESI DR1 but not reported in literature at the time. Do not overstate population completeness.
evidence.ai_role: Learned an image embedding where candidate quasars formed overdensities, allowing atypical sources beyond standard color selection to be prioritized for spectroscopic validation. Spectroscopy confirmed the quasars; AI did not determine their redshifts alone.

title: Deep learning and spectroscopy confirm four faint quasars at redshift about 5
summary: A deep-learning and Bayesian-information-criterion search of Subaru Hyper Suprime-Cam photometry selected four faint high-redshift quasar candidates. Palomar spectroscopy found broad Lyman-alpha emission and breaks in all four, confirming redshifts between 4.7 and 5.6; one object also received a black-hole mass estimate.
ai_technology: Deep-learning photometric classifier combined with Bayesian information criterion
organization: Seoul National University; Kyungpook National University; Kavli Institute for Astronomy and Astrophysics, Peking University

evidence.tested: A deep-learning and Bayesian-information-criterion search of Subaru Hyper Suprime-Cam photometry selected four faint high-redshift quasar candidates.
evidence.unknown: The paper spectroscopically confirms four targeted candidates, not the full 35-object catalog. The selection method combines deep learning with a Bayesian information criterion and conventional candidate filtering; AI was one component rather than the sole discovery mechanism.
evidence.ai_role: The classifier shortlisted high-redshift quasar candidates from survey photometry; human researchers selected four for observation and used telescope spectra to confirm all four as quasars.

title: The QUBRICS machine-learning survey spectroscopically identifies 224 new bright high-redshift quasars
summary: The QUBRICS survey applied a machine-learning selection pipeline to southern optical and infrared catalogs and followed candidates spectroscopically. The paper reports 224 newly identified bright quasars at z≥2.5, including 15 at z>4, and provides a large southern sample for cosmological observations.
ai_technology: QUBRICS machine-learning photometric selection with Canonical Correlation Analysis redshift regression
organization: INAF Astronomical Observatory of Trieste; INAF Astronomical Observatory of Padova; Las Campanas Observatory; Sapienza University of Rome; other QUBRICS collaboration institutions

evidence.tested: The QUBRICS survey applied a machine-learning selection pipeline to southern optical and infrared catalogs and followed candidates spectroscopically.
evidence.unknown: The 224 are cumulative QUBRICS discoveries across its pilot and follow-up publications. The paper estimates a 68% success rate for the current selection; contaminants include lower-redshift quasars/AGN. Five objects in the sample had already appeared in literature and were independently selected, so the total is a survey result, not 224 exclusive first publications in this paper.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning selection ranked photometric sources for follow-up; the team obtained and analyzed optical/infrared spectra to identify and measure redshifts. The paper reports the cumulative survey sample, not 224 objects newly found by a single autonomous run.

title: AI-assisted seismic mapping reveals segmented fault activity at the Discovery transform fault
summary: A machine-learning earthquake-detection and relocation workflow applied to 2008 ocean-bottom seismometer records found that the western Discovery transform-fault strand may comprise seven patches with distinct seismicity. The authors also identify a seismicity-gap zone that they interpret as possibly linked to an active small off-ridge rift.
ai_technology: PhaseNet phase picker, GaMMA phase association, and machine-learning-enhanced seismic event workflow
organization: University of California, Santa Cruz; Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution

evidence.tested: A machine-learning earthquake-detection and relocation workflow applied to 2008 ocean-bottom seismometer records found that the western Discovery transform-fault strand may comprise seven patches with distinct seismicity.
evidence.unknown: The seven-patch segmentation and possible off-fault rift relationship are interpretations of one year of local 2008 seismic data, not a causal or universal transform-fault model. The location and tectonic interpretations are supported by the new catalog and follow-up cross-correlation relocation; the source describes the rift explanation as possible.
evidence.ai_role: The AI workflow detected P/S arrivals from noisy ocean-bottom recordings and associated event phases; cross-correlation relocation and geological interpretation by the research team produced the fault-pattern interpretation.

title: EqGPT infers a previously unreported equation for steepening surface gravity waves
summary: A knowledge-guided generative model trained on mathematical handbook equations generated candidate PDEs, then evaluated and optimized them against data. In a real-data case study of strongly nonlinear surface gravity waves approaching breaking, the authors report an equation not previously reported for that process.
ai_technology: EqGPT, a generative transformer using equation tokenization and a generation–evaluation–optimization loop
organization: China University of Petroleum (East China); Imperial College London; Southern University of Science and Technology; Hong Kong University of Science and Technology; University of Oxford

evidence.tested: A knowledge-guided generative model trained on mathematical handbook equations generated candidate PDEs, then evaluated and optimized them against data.
evidence.unknown: The claimed new governing equation is an inference from a particular real-world laboratory dataset and remains a model-derived description, not a universally established law. Authors used human fluid-mechanics analysis; this was one new equation result within a methods paper that also rediscovers known PDEs.
evidence.ai_role: The model proposed free-form PDE candidates using structures learned from 221 handbook equations; data-driven fit evaluation selected a candidate for the breaking-wave dataset, after which researchers analyzed its physical interpretation.

title: Autonomous X-ray mapping reveals previously unseen block-copolymer morphologies, including a nanoscale ladder
summary: An autonomous experiment planner selected synchrotron X-ray measurements across a combinatorial block-copolymer blend sample. The resulting map and targeted electron microscopy revealed previously unreported alternating, skew/bilayer, and ladder-like self-assembled morphologies, and the authors infer a general mechanism of local subdomain partitioning.
ai_technology: gpCAM autonomous experimentation framework for selecting high-value measurements
organization: Brookhaven National Laboratory Center for Functional Nanomaterials and National Synchrotron Light Source II; Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory CAMERA

evidence.tested: An autonomous experiment planner selected synchrotron X-ray measurements across a combinatorial block-copolymer blend sample.
evidence.unknown: The newly discovered results are nanoscale morphologies in one specific polymer-blend/template system; the paper does not show that each morphology is already useful in a device. AI selected measurements, while domain researchers performed electron-microscopy confirmation and interpretation.
evidence.ai_role: The algorithm autonomously chose where to collect synchrotron X-ray scattering data and updated its model online; researchers then used electron microscopy to validate and interpret the novel morphologies.

title: Physics-based differentiable imaging detects 51 Eridani b in a JWST band where standard processing did not
summary: A physics-based coronagraph model optimized with automatic differentiation and gradient descent recovered 51 Eridani b in JWST/NIRCam F430M images at 4.3 μm, where the published standard-processing result was a non-detection. The paper also reports two- to fifteen-fold sensitivity gains across its test observations.
ai_technology: FLIP (Physics-based Learning for Imaging Planets), a differentiable instrument model optimized with automatic differentiation
organization: Northwestern University; California Institute of Technology; Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Space Telescope Science Institute

evidence.tested: A physics-based coronagraph model optimized with automatic differentiation and gradient descent recovered 51 Eridani b in JWST/NIRCam F430M images at 4.3 μm, where the published standard-processing result was a non-detection.
evidence.unknown: The planet 51 Eridani b was already discovered by ground-based imaging in 2015; the new finding is its first JWST image in the 4.3 μm carbon-dioxide band, not discovery of a previously unknown planet. Performance estimates are based on a limited set of three target systems and should not be generalized to all JWST data.
evidence.ai_role: Optimized telescope aberration and detector parameters against the observed JWST point-spread function to subtract starlight; this image analysis recovered a 6.3σ signal at 4.3 μm in a dataset whose original analysis reported no detection.

title: SMDET-selected ultracool-dwarf candidates include two objects with spectroscopically confirmed T-dwarf types
summary: The SMDET image-level neural network identified 118 previously uncatalogued high-proper-motion ultracool-dwarf candidates in WISE time-series images. Follow-up near-infrared spectra for two selected objects yielded T5 and T3 classifications, confirming their estimated spectral types within one subtype.
ai_technology: SMDET, a convolutional neural network for detecting faint moving sources in WISE time-series coadds
organization: Backyard Worlds: Planet 9 collaboration; NASA Goddard Space Flight Center; California Institute of Technology/IPAC; Northern Arizona University

evidence.tested: The SMDET image-level neural network identified 118 previously uncatalogued high-proper-motion ultracool-dwarf candidates in WISE time-series images.
evidence.unknown: Most of the 118 objects remain candidates, and the study spectroscopically checks only two. Some candidates were also identified by citizen scientists, so the AI was part of a human/algorithm discovery process. The counted finding is limited to the two spectra and the candidate search result as one paper-level report.
evidence.ai_role: Scanned WISE image sequences and prioritized faint, fast-moving source candidates; researchers cross-checked catalogs, estimated photometric types and distances, and acquired spectra for two objects to verify their T-dwarf classifications.

title: Machine-learning tremor catalog reveals Japan Trench spatial and slow-slip relationships
summary: A machine-learning monitoring system applied to eight years of S-net seafloor records detected seven times more tectonic tremors than the previous envelope-correlation catalog. The denser catalog resolved tremor activity extending along strike and dip, tremor patterns synchronized with slow-slip events, higher tremor energy rates near large-earthquake asperities, and a positive relationship between energy rate and recurrence interval; authors interpret the latter as evidence consistent with plate-boundary frictional heterogeneity.
ai_technology: DiET convolutional neural network and GrASP graph-based station association, with hybrid envelope-correlation/energy-ratio hypocenter location
organization: Geological Survey of Japan, National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology; Tohoku University

evidence.tested: A machine-learning monitoring system applied to eight years of S-net seafloor records detected seven times more tectonic tremors than the previous envelope-correlation catalog.
evidence.unknown: The paper reports a substantial catalog expansion and interprets energy-rate patterns as suggestive of frictional heterogeneity; this is not a prospective earthquake forecast or proof of a causal friction mechanism. The abstract states prior work had already observed complementary tremor/earthquake distributions in the region, so the new contribution is the expanded catalog and improved resolution of the relationships, not the first observation of any complementary distribution.
evidence.ai_role: The CNN classified station spectrograms as earthquake, tremor or noise; graph clustering associated station detections, enabling a higher-resolution catalog from continuous S-net data. Human researchers interpreted the spatial and temporal relationships.

title: Deep learning reveals a new seismicity distribution along the Kabaw Fault in central Myanmar
summary: A deep-learning-based catalog pipeline processed 18 months of seismic-array data and located 1,891 shallow earthquakes, more than twice the 849 events in the prior manual catalog. The denser catalog shows that shallow Kabaw Fault seismicity disappears south of about 22.8°N while deeper events occur west of the fault, and it fills part of a previously under-sampled seismicity gap; the authors interpret this contrast as potentially reflecting along-strike variation in deformation associated with oblique Indian-plate subduction.
ai_technology: DEPALORE pipeline using Earthquake Transformer, transfer-learned PickNet, REAL association, NonLinLoc location and HypoDD relocation
organization: Chinese Academy of Sciences; Zhejiang Ocean University; collaborators

evidence.tested: A deep-learning-based catalog pipeline processed 18 months of seismic-array data and located 1,891 shallow earthquakes, more than twice the 849 events in the prior manual catalog.
evidence.unknown: The source reports catalog-derived patterns and offers a tentative tectonic explanation; the catalog contains 1,891 localized events and location uncertainties of several kilometers. The AI enabled detections and resolution, while geological interpretation remains the authors’ analysis.
evidence.ai_role: Deep-learning detectors and phase-picking models extracted seismic arrivals from continuous array waveforms; association and location stages produced the higher-completeness catalog from which researchers interpreted fault patterns.

title: Unsupervised machine learning reveals previously missed hydraulic-fracturing seismicity in Live Oak County
summary: An unsupervised repeating-signal detector, combined with template matching, exposed small earthquake bursts in a region of the Eagle Ford shale where conventional catalogs had detected little seismicity. The authors report that the new events temporally coincided with hydraulic-fracturing activity, and their regional analysis found detectable seismicity began after injection flux exceeded about two million barrels per month despite similar cumulative injection volume; this supports, but does not prove, a causal role for injection rate and is limited by sparse station coverage.
ai_technology: Repeating Signal Detector (RSD), an unsupervised machine-learning waveform-family detector
organization: Miami University; University of Kansas

evidence.tested: An unsupervised repeating-signal detector, combined with template matching, exposed small earthquake bursts in a region of the Eagle Ford shale where conventional catalogs had detected little seismicity.
evidence.unknown: The RSD detections were manually inspected and some event locations were poorly constrained; the authors note station density limits detection and do not establish causation from temporal correlation alone. This paper extends an earlier Eagle Ford study but reports a distinct Live Oak County seismicity region and subsequent time-period catalog.
evidence.ai_role: RSD searched continuous seismograms without relying on preselected earthquake templates, clustered similar signals, and revealed small-magnitude event bursts missed by the previous catalog. Researchers manually inspected signals and analyzed their timing relative to hydraulic-fracturing records.

title: A self-driving laboratory discovers lens-and-grating patterns that steer spontaneous emission
summary: A self-driving nanophotonics experiment discovered that combining lens-like refractive-index curvature with grating-like spatial gradient can steer incoherent light emission from a semiconductor metasurface beyond conventional momentum-matching designs. Across a 74° field of view, optimized patterns produced average peak directivity 2.2 times that of sawtooth-grating controls, reaching 67% peak directivity; a fitted equation learner extracted a compact relationship from the experiments.
ai_technology: Variational autoencoder, active-learning experimental planner and neural-network equation learner
organization: Sandia National Laboratories

evidence.tested: A self-driving nanophotonics experiment discovered that combining lens-like refractive-index curvature with grating-like spatial gradient can steer incoherent light emission from a semiconductor metasurface beyond conventional momentum-matching designs.
evidence.unknown: The article reports local optima under a finite experiment budget, not a global optimum. Measurements were made on a specific GaAs/InAs quantum-dot metasurface; extensions to other emitters or devices remain untested in this study.
evidence.ai_role: The VAE generated pump-pattern configurations, an active-learning agent selected closed-loop physical experiments using measured photoluminescence, and an equation-learning network distilled observed structure–property relationships. The experimental setup measured and human researchers interpreted the results.

title: A self-driving lab finds a polymer shell with record energy-absorbing efficiency
summary: A human-supervised self-driving laboratory selected and physically tested more than 25,000 additively manufactured polymer shell designs across an 11-dimensional parameter space. The campaign found a structure with 75.2% energy-absorbing efficiency, exceeding the paper’s previously reported maximum of 71.8% for balsa wood, and the authors derived transferable design heuristics from the resulting dataset. The result is a structural design for specified compression thresholds, not a universal material efficiency ranking.
ai_technology: MAMA BEAR self-driving laboratory with Bayesian optimization and automated additive manufacturing/testing
organization: Boston University; U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command Soldier Center

evidence.tested: A human-supervised self-driving laboratory selected and physically tested more than 25,000 additively manufactured polymer shell designs across an 11-dimensional parameter space.
evidence.unknown: The result concerns generalized cylindrical shells made from a limited set of polymers and a defined nondimensional metric, whose value depends on threshold stress. The optimization was human-in-the-loop, and transfer to other geometries, materials or operational settings is not established.
evidence.ai_role: Bayesian optimization selected designs from over a trillion possible parameter combinations; the laboratory manufactured and mechanically tested candidates, while human researchers monitored and periodically modified the campaign.

title: Machine learning helps identify 61 new cataclysmic variables in SDSS-V spectroscopy
summary: A convolutional neural network shortlisted cataclysmic-variable candidates from more than two million SDSS-V spectra, reducing the spectra requiring visual inspection to about 2% of the total. Human review and follow-up analysis of the resulting 504-object sample reported 61 previously unreported cataclysmic variables, spectroscopically confirmed 248 candidates and yielded 82 new or improved orbital periods; the article discusses selection biases and the CNN missed 27 spectra later found by human review.
ai_technology: Convolutional neural network classifier for SDSS-V/BOSS spectra
organization: SDSS-V collaboration; University of Warwick and collaborating institutions

evidence.tested: A convolutional neural network shortlisted cataclysmic-variable candidates from more than two million SDSS-V spectra, reducing the spectra requiring visual inspection to about 2% of the total.
evidence.unknown: This is one grouped paper-level survey result, not 61 separate records. The CNN was a triage aid rather than an autonomous confirmation system; authors report completeness/selection limitations and 27 misclassified spectra discovered through human inspection.
evidence.ai_role: Ranked over two million spectra for likely cataclysmic variables, reducing the manual-inspection workload; human investigators visually inspected candidate spectra and established source classifications and periods.

title: Spectroscopic follow-up revises Gaia machine-learning white-dwarf classifications and reveals a large magnetic and carbon-rich population
summary: Follow-up spectra for 255 Gaia white dwarfs were compared with machine-learning classifications from low-resolution Gaia spectra. The study reports that only 5 of 112 objects classified as massive DBs were genuine DB white dwarfs; most were magnetic white dwarfs or warm DQ stars. Its spectroscopy also catalogued 63 magnetic white dwarfs and 29 warm DQs in the selected sample, while confirming high classification accuracy for major spectral types within the classifier’s training set.
ai_technology: Random-forest spectral classifier applied to Gaia low-resolution spectra
organization: Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya; Universitat de Barcelona and collaborators

evidence.tested: Follow-up spectra for 255 Gaia white dwarfs were compared with machine-learning classifications from low-resolution Gaia spectra.
evidence.unknown: The result is a follow-up characterization of a selected 500-pc sample, not a complete census of white dwarfs. It corrects a specific machine-learning-labelled ‘massive DB’ subpopulation; reported counts should not be extrapolated to Gaia’s full white-dwarf population.
evidence.ai_role: The classifier assigned initial white-dwarf spectral types and selected objects of interest; astronomers obtained Gran Telescopio Canarias medium-resolution spectra and visually inspected them to determine the objects’ types and magnetic features.

title: Unsupervised learning reveals mixed-frequency seismic precursors before Axial Seamount’s 2015 eruption
summary: An analysis of four months of Axial Seamount seismicity combined supervised event discrimination with unsupervised spectral clustering and found a mixed-frequency earthquake class whose counts rose rapidly about 15 hours before the 2015 eruption. The events migrated along mapped eruptive fissures; the authors interpret them as brittle crack opening associated with magma or volatile influx. This is a retrospective single-eruption finding, not an operationally validated forecast.
ai_technology: Unsupervised machine-learning spectral clustering, with supervised event discrimination
organization: Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory, Columbia University; University of Washington; Chinese University of Hong Kong

evidence.tested: An analysis of four months of Axial Seamount seismicity combined supervised event discrimination with unsupervised spectral clustering and found a mixed-frequency earthquake class whose counts rose rapidly about 15 hours before the 2015 eruption.
evidence.unknown: The result is retrospective and concerns a single 2015 eruption at one well-instrumented submarine volcano. The proposed crack-opening/magma-or-volatile explanation is the authors’ interpretation; applicability to future eruptions or other volcanoes remains untested.
evidence.ai_role: Discriminated volcanic earthquakes from other signal sources and clustered waveform spectral features, revealing a previously unrecognized mixed-frequency event pattern and its timing and migration before eruption.

title: Machine learning identifies regional low-magnitude seismic unrest before the Ridgecrest and Anchorage earthquakes
summary: A random-forest method using statistical features from earthquake catalogs identified abnormal low-magnitude seismicity spreading across roughly 15–25% of Southern California and Southcentral Alaska up to about three months before the 2019 Ridgecrest sequence and 2018 Anchorage M7.1 earthquake. Finite-element mechanics models were used to propose a pore-fluid-pressure explanation. This is a retrospective analysis of two target events, not a demonstrated reliable warning system.
ai_technology: Random-forest machine-learning algorithm with earthquake-catalog statistical features
organization: Institute of Geophysics, Spanish National Research Council (CSIC); University of Edinburgh

evidence.tested: A random-forest method using statistical features from earthquake catalogs identified abnormal low-magnitude seismicity spreading across roughly 15–25% of Southern California and Southcentral Alaska up to about three months before the 2019 Ridgecrest sequence and 2018 Anchorage M7.1 earthquake.
evidence.unknown: The study analyzes two retrospective target events and explicitly notes that earthquake precursors remain ambiguous and reliable alert systems are not established. The pore-pressure mechanism is proposed from modeling rather than directly measured, and the finding is not prospective validation.
evidence.ai_role: Detected regional nonlinear patterns in low-magnitude seismic catalogs that the authors report as precursory unrest before two large earthquake sequences; the AI analysis identified the statistical pattern, while finite-element models supported a proposed mechanism.

title: Weakly supervised deep learning maps seamount morphology patterns associated with tectonic setting
summary: A weakly supervised deep-learning analysis combining satellite-derived gravity and bathymetry produced a global seamount inventory and reported systematic morphology differences: broad edifices along fast-spreading ridges and steeper forms near intraplate hotspots. The authors interpret these differences as reflecting geodynamic controls on volcanic construction. Many detections rely on indirect gravity/bathymetry data rather than shipborne mapping, so individual feature identifications and causal interpretations require further validation.
ai_technology: Weakly supervised deep-learning detector with vision foundation model, iterative pseudo-label refinement, and elliptical Gaussian fitting
organization: University of Science and Technology of China; Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory

evidence.tested: A weakly supervised deep-learning analysis combining satellite-derived gravity and bathymetry produced a global seamount inventory and reported systematic morphology differences: broad edifices along fast-spreading ridges and steeper forms near intraplate hotspots.
evidence.unknown: The publisher abstract describes numerous previously undocumented features but does not establish shipborne confirmation for every mapped detection. The reported morphology-setting relationship is an observational pattern and should not be read as proof of a unique causal mechanism.
evidence.ai_role: Detected and morphologically characterized seamount features in global gravity and bathymetry data despite sparse labels, enabling the cross-setting comparison that revealed tectonically organized morphology patterns.

title: Machine learning identifies predicted zero- and extreme-thermal-expansion monolayers
summary: High-throughput calculations and symbolic regression identified mechanical descriptors that classify positive- versus negative-thermal-expansion 2D crystals, then used those descriptors to predict monolayers with near-zero thermal expansion (2D Invar) and unusually large positive or negative expansion (anti-Invar). The paper reports multiple specific predicted crystals and explains the phonon/deformation-mode basis. The materials are computational predictions rather than experimentally synthesized monolayers.
ai_technology: High-throughput calculations combined with symbolic regression machine learning
organization: Soochow University; Xi’an Jiaotong University

evidence.tested: High-throughput calculations and symbolic regression identified mechanical descriptors that classify positive- versus negative-thermal-expansion 2D crystals, then used those descriptors to predict monolayers with near-zero thermal expansion (2D Invar) and unusually large positive or negative expansion (anti-Invar).
evidence.unknown: The identified materials and thermal-expansion properties are from computational/high-throughput predictions and were not experimentally validated in this paper. This is a new 2D monolayer property result, distinct from previously cataloged bulk high-entropy Invar alloys.
evidence.ai_role: Learned interpretable relationships between in-plane tensile stiffness, out-of-plane bending stiffness and thermal-expansion class, then used them to screen 2D-crystal databases for predicted Invar and anti-Invar materials.

title: Machine-learning-assisted design predicts Netsene, a 3D carbon nodal-surface semimetal
summary: A theory-guided inverse-design study combined a crystal diffusion variational autoencoder with a Crystal Transformer to propose a body-centered tetragonal C24 allotrope, Netsene. First-principles calculations report dynamical and mechanical stability and a nested nodal-surface semimetal band structure with drumhead surface states. This is a computationally predicted allotrope and electronic phase, not an experimentally synthesized material.
ai_technology: Crystal diffusion variational autoencoder (CDVAE) and Crystal Transformer, guided by symmetry-engineering theory
organization: Authors’ institutions include Nanjing University and associated materials-physics groups (see arXiv record)

evidence.tested: A theory-guided inverse-design study combined a crystal diffusion variational autoencoder with a Crystal Transformer to propose a body-centered tetragonal C24 allotrope, Netsene.
evidence.unknown: The allotrope and its properties are computational predictions validated by first-principles calculations; the paper does not report synthesis or experimental observation. The finding is one proposed material/phase result from one paper, not a claim that AI alone established the physical existence of Netsene.
evidence.ai_role: Generated and ranked candidate crystal structures within a theory-guided inverse-design workflow; the resulting Netsene structure was then assessed with first-principles calculations for stability and topological band properties.

title: A radio survey reveals megaparsec-scale diffuse emission around a cosmic-web node
summary: Radio U-Net prompted reanalysis of LOFAR, XMM-Newton, DESI optical/near-infrared and weak-lensing data around cluster PSZ2 G083.29−31.03. The team reports previously unnoticed diffuse radio emission extending about 5 Mpc and aligned with X-ray emission and galaxies; lensing supports a complex mass distribution with two low-mass systems on either side of the cluster. The authors propose that these systems are merging substructures in a massive cosmic-web node, while noting alternative interpretations remain possible.
ai_technology: Radio U-Net, a machine-learning detector for diffuse radio emission
organization: University of Bologna; INAF; University of Milano-Bicocca; National Central University, Taiwan; University of Tokyo; INAF Istituto di Radioastronomia; CINECA

evidence.tested: Radio U-Net prompted reanalysis of LOFAR, XMM-Newton, DESI optical/near-infrared and weak-lensing data around cluster PSZ2 G083.29−31.03.
evidence.unknown: The radio morphology and multiwavelength associations are reported observational results. The interpretation that the two faint components are subclusters merging with the central cluster is proposed rather than uniquely established; redshift/mass uncertainties and low radio resolution leave other emission classifications possible.
evidence.ai_role: Flagged diffuse low-surface-brightness radio emission in LoTSS data that had escaped prior human analysis, motivating the multiwavelength and weak-lensing study that characterized this new extended structure.

title: Deep-learning tracking of mantle simulations finds continental-margin subduction zones persist longer
summary: A fully convolutional network segmented subduction zones in two-dimensional mantle-convection simulations using temperature, vertical velocity and fineness fields. Across the modeled runs, zones forming near continental margins were generally longer-lived and less sensitive to internal heating than oceanic zones, supporting the hypothesis that continental lithosphere can stabilize subduction during early-Earth-like conditions. This is a computational-model result rather than direct observation of ancient Earth.
ai_technology: Attention-based fully convolutional network with custom segmentation loss
organization: Pennsylvania State University; Georgia Institute of Technology

evidence.tested: A fully convolutional network segmented subduction zones in two-dimensional mantle-convection simulations using temperature, vertical velocity and fineness fields.
evidence.unknown: The physical inference comes from two-dimensional numerical mantle-convection models and their selected parameter space, not empirical reconstruction of Earth's early subduction history. The AI performs segmentation/tracking; the tectonic contrast is a statistical result from model outputs.
evidence.ai_role: Provided threshold-free, spatially contextual tracking of evolving subduction zones in simulation outputs; the resulting tracked histories enabled statistical comparison of lifetimes and sensitivity to mantle convective vigor by tectonic setting.

title: Machine learning maps modeled fault-system CO₂ flux within active tectonic regions worldwide
summary: A stacked ensemble trained on 867 compiled degassing records and geospatial raster predictors generated a continuous 0.10° map of model-estimated CO₂ flux within an active-tectonics applicability mask. The authors report spatially coherent high-flux estimates along the Andes, Pacific Ring of Fire and other active orogens. This is a new model-derived spatial estimate for fault-system flux, rather than a direct global survey or measurement.
ai_technology: Stacked regression ensemble combining support-vector, k-nearest-neighbor, decision-tree, random-forest and gradient-boosting models
organization: Universidad Nacional de Colombia; Academia Colombiana de Ciencias Exactas

evidence.tested: A stacked ensemble trained on 867 compiled degassing records and geospatial raster predictors generated a continuous 0.10° map of model-estimated CO₂ flux within an active-tectonics applicability mask.
evidence.unknown: Predictions are model estimates based on 867 compiled records with heterogeneous dates and measurement techniques, not direct measurements at every pixel. The mask is limited to areas within 40 km of mapped active faults or with PGA ≥0.10 g; the 0.10° raster smooths local geology. The abstract reports R²=0.677, while the full text gives stacking test R²=0.693 and validation R²=0.552; fit is moderate. Sampling gaps include central Africa, eastern Asia and North America. High-flux belts overlap known tectonic/geothermal regions, and SHAP associations do not establish causal controls.
evidence.ai_role: Five regression learners were tuned and combined in a stacking regressor; that model predicted flux pixel by pixel from global raster inputs and generated the paper’s continuous map of estimated fault-system flux. The mask excluded areas outside the model’s stated tectonically active applicability domain.

title: Deep learning finds comet C/2020 T2 in a single ZTF image
summary: The Tails EfficientDet model identified the extended object C/2020 T2 in one Zwicky Transient Facility Twilight Survey image on 2020 October 7. Follow-up orbital work confirmed it as a long-period comet. The study reports this as the first comet discovery assisted by deep learning; it also recovered a previously known comet, which is not counted as a new discovery here.
ai_technology: Tails, an EfficientDet-based deep-learning comet detector
organization: California Institute of Technology; IPAC; Zwicky Transient Facility collaboration

evidence.tested: The Tails EfficientDet model identified the extended object C/2020 T2 in one Zwicky Transient Facility Twilight Survey image on 2020 October 7.
evidence.unknown: The model surfaced the object, while human/standard follow-up established its orbit and comet classification. The entry counts only the newly discovered C/2020 T2, not recovery of P/2016 J3/P/2021 A3 or the detector’s performance metrics.
evidence.ai_role: Detected the comet’s extended coma/tail morphology in a single survey image and surfaced C/2020 T2 for discovery/follow-up; this enabled detection without requiring multi-epoch orbit linking at the initial search stage.

title: UMAP analysis of DESI spectra surfaces newly recognized inhomogeneous white dwarfs
summary: A machine-learning-guided analysis of DESI multi-epoch spectra used UMAP to identify three systems with strongly varying spectral signatures that were proposed as new ‘double-faced’ white dwarfs with inhomogeneous surface composition. Follow-up phase-resolved time-series spectra verified the interpretation for one system; the other two remain candidates. This is one paper-level result and only the verified system is counted as confirmed.
ai_technology: UMAP dimensionality reduction applied to multi-epoch white-dwarf spectroscopy, alongside a neural-network spectral classifier
organization: University of Warwick; University of Leicester; University of Barcelona; Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias; DESI collaboration

evidence.tested: A machine-learning-guided analysis of DESI multi-epoch spectra used UMAP to identify three systems with strongly varying spectral signatures that were proposed as new ‘double-faced’ white dwarfs with inhomogeneous surface composition.
evidence.unknown: The paper describes three new candidates, but only one has validating phase-resolved time-series spectra; the remaining two have limited/unequal signal-to-noise and are not included as confirmed objects. Existing classification of the first source as a DA+DB binary was challenged, not assumed disproven without the authors’ supporting phase-dependent evidence.
evidence.ai_role: Mapped spectral/photometric features and flagged white dwarfs with strongly changing multi-epoch spectra for expert review; this identified the systems subsequently investigated with phase-resolved spectroscopy.

title: Claude-assisted analytic proof establishes a+b=1 for mean-field jamming exponents
summary: Giorgio Parisi and Francesco Zamponi provide an analytic proof that the critical exponents a and b in the full replica-symmetry-breaking scaling solution for infinite-dimensional dense hard spheres obey a+b=1. The identity links gap, contact-force and overlap scaling relations and had previously been known numerically but not analytically. The authors report that Claude Opus 4.7 derived the core proof idea with minimal supervision, with Sonnet 4.6 helping refine it; the authors found and corrected errors in an early draft, then verified and edited the final proof.
ai_technology: Anthropic Claude Opus 4.7 and Claude Sonnet 4.6
organization: Sapienza University of Rome; CNR-Nanotec Rome; INFN Sezione di Roma 1; Beihang University

evidence.tested: Giorgio Parisi and Francesco Zamponi provide an analytic proof that the critical exponents a and b in the full replica-symmetry-breaking scaling solution for infinite-dimensional dense hard spheres obey a+b=1.
evidence.unknown: The theorem is scoped to the fullRSB scaling equations for the infinite-dimensional dense hard-sphere jamming solution; it is not a general proof about every finite-dimensional jamming system. The result is peer-reviewed and published, but proof validation and correction are attributed to the human authors.
evidence.ai_role: After numerical investigation, Opus generated the analytic proof strategy and proof draft for the previously unproven scaling identity; Sonnet refined minor steps. The authors report 40 prompts, corrected early inconsistencies and verified/edited the published proof.

title: AI-assisted transfer-matrix analysis yields an exact solution for the 1D frustrated q-state Potts model
summary: The study exactly solves the one-dimensional J₁–J₂ q-state Potts model for arbitrary q by reducing its q²×q² transfer matrix to a 2×2 maximally symmetric subspace and mapping it to an effective q-state Potts model in a field. OpenAI’s o3-mini-high reasoning model helped derive the q=3 case; the author then generalized the result to arbitrary q and checked the formulas numerically. The solution nontrivially extends an older mapping known for q=2/Ising and yields q-dependent phase and residual-entropy behavior.
ai_technology: OpenAI o3-mini-high reasoning model
organization: Brookhaven National Laboratory

evidence.tested: The study exactly solves the one-dimensional J₁–J₂ q-state Potts model for arbitrary q by reducing its q²×q² transfer matrix to a 2×2 maximally symmetric subspace and mapping it to an effective q-state Potts model in a field.
evidence.unknown: The AI contribution was to the q=3 transfer-matrix solution; the general-q theorem and full paper are the human author’s derivation, so this is an AI-assisted paper-level theoretical discovery, not an autonomous AI solution for arbitrary q. The exact result concerns the one-dimensional model and does not itself demonstrate a material realization.
evidence.ai_role: Proposed a transfer-matrix construction that enabled an exact solution of the q=3 frustrated Potts model; the author used that result as a starting point to generalize the exact mapping to arbitrary q, prove the subspace correspondence and numerically check the resulting formulas.

title: Gemini derives an exact analytic solution for the cosmic-string gravitational-radiation power integral
summary: A Gemini Deep Think system, guided by tree search and numerical feedback, derived closed-form spectral coefficients for the integral determining gravitational radiation power from cosmic-string loops, resolving the paper’s stated open calculation. The authors compare the expressions against direct numerical integration over ranges of loop harmonic and geometry parameters, finding close agreement. This is a theoretical/computational result, not a new astronomical detection.
ai_technology: Google Gemini Deep Think integrated with tree search, executable Python evaluation and high-precision numerical feedback
organization: Affiliations are not recorded as an organization claim because the consulted arXiv page did not expose them in the checked abstract.

evidence.tested: A Gemini Deep Think system, guided by tree search and numerical feedback, derived closed-form spectral coefficients for the integral determining gravitational radiation power from cosmic-string loops, resolving the paper’s stated open calculation.
evidence.unknown: The source is an unrefereed arXiv preprint. The paper provides derivations and numerical cross-checks, not proof-assistant verification or independent replication. The first recurrence attempt contained an error that the later Gemini-assisted review corrected. The claim is limited to the stated integral for the cosmic-string radiation model and its exact analytic evaluation.
evidence.ai_role: Gemini generated and refined analytical approaches inside a tree-search workflow whose Python harness compared candidate expressions with high-precision numerical integration. A later human-initiated session with a more advanced Gemini model identified a recurrence error and telescoped the series into a finite analytic expression; this was a human–AI handoff, not a fully autonomous end-to-end result.

title: Machine learning identifies disordered twist-angle sequences with strongly reduced thermal conductivity in multilayer graphene
summary: Bayesian optimization and a CNN, coupled to non-equilibrium molecular dynamics, selected two-angle disordered twisted multilayer graphene structures with substantially lower simulated cross-plane thermal conductivity than aligned and periodic stacks. The optimized 14-layer sequence reached 0.095 W m−1 K−1 versus 0.512 W m−1 K−1 in aligned graphene in the reported model; phonon participation ratios and dynamical structure factors support strong partial phonon localization.
ai_technology: Bayesian optimization (COMBO) and convolutional neural network coupled to molecular-dynamics simulations
organization: Sun Yat-sen University

evidence.tested: Bayesian optimization and a CNN, coupled to non-equilibrium molecular dynamics, selected two-angle disordered twisted multilayer graphene structures with substantially lower simulated cross-plane thermal conductivity than aligned and periodic stacks.
evidence.unknown: This is a computational prediction supported by molecular-dynamics calculations, not a measured thermal-conductivity result from fabricated multilayer samples. The paper reports 80% reduction relative to aligned graphene for an optimized sequence and interprets phonon participation/structure-factor analyses as evidence of partial localization.
evidence.ai_role: Bayesian optimization selected low-conductivity twist sequences; the CNN screened the larger configuration space and proposed low-conductivity structures for subsequent molecular-dynamics evaluation.

title: Machine-learning analysis attributes the apparent pre-Norcia earthquake b-value rise to changing activity across two fault structures
summary: For the 2016–2017 central Italy sequence, a combination of machine-learning techniques resolved two seismicity volumes with distinct fault orientations and Gutenberg–Richter b-values.
