evidence.tested: The source presents a proof discovered autonomously by GPT-6 Pro establishing an O_d(r^{-1/2}) zero-probability bound for degree-d multilinear polynomials with r disjoint degree-d monomials, improving the prior bound by removing a polylogarithmic factor and resolving the Nguyen–Vu conjecture.
evidence.unknown: This is an arXiv preprint. The author reports personally verifying and rewriting the proof; this review has not independently formalized it. Bound and related rational-function influence result are counted once because the paper derives them as a connected argument.
evidence.ai_role: The author states that GPT-6 Pro autonomously discovered the proof and that the author claims no credit for the proof ideas; the author subsequently verified, digested and rewrote the argument.

title: GPT-6 Pro proves a quadratic-size threshold suffices for random permutations to contain every length-n pattern
summary: The paper proves that a uniformly random permutation of length 32n² contains every permutation of length n as a pattern with probability at least 1−exp(−c n/log n), for an absolute c>0 and sufficiently large n. This removes the prior log-log factor from the sufficient-length bound, resolves Alon’s open 1000n² problem, and establishes the correct Θ(n²) order.
ai_technology: OpenAI GPT-6 Pro
organization: Yu Chen and Yiting Wang (affiliations not specified in arXiv record)

evidence.tested: The paper proves that a uniformly random permutation of length 32n² contains every permutation of length n as a pattern with probability at least 1−exp(−c n/log n), for an absolute c>0 and sufficiently large n.
evidence.unknown: ArXiv preprint. Authors report checking and digesting the proof; no separate independent validation is claimed here. The result is an asymptotic sufficient bound with constant 32 (the paper explains the constant can be reduced to any value greater than 1), not a sharp threshold constant.
evidence.ai_role: The authors state that GPT-6 Pro found the proof; they do not claim credit for its proof ideas, and say they verified and digested it and take responsibility for the manuscript.

title: GPT-6 Astra resolves the spectral isometry conjecture for arbitrary unital C*-algebras
summary: The paper proves that every unital surjective complex-linear spectral isometry between unital C*-algebras is a Jordan isomorphism; without unitality, such a map is a central-unitary multiple of a Jordan isomorphism. The proof establishes that entire one-parameter groups of unital spectral isometries are algebra automorphisms, then reduces the general case to the commutative case. The authors report that the result was formally verified in Lean.
ai_technology: OpenAI GPT-6 Astra
organization: University of Cambridge; California Institute of Technology

evidence.tested: The paper proves that every unital surjective complex-linear spectral isometry between unital C*-algebras is a Jordan isomorphism; without unitality, such a map is a central-unitary multiple of a Jordan isomorphism.
evidence.unknown: ArXiv preprint. The authors explicitly describe the article as a human exposition/digestion of an AI-found proof. Their manuscript says formal verification is in Lean; The reported formalization was not independently audited in the source review.
evidence.ai_role: Authors state GPT-6 Astra found the proof after a sequence of simple prompts. They then discussed it with ChatGPT 6 to understand the mechanisms, wrote the paper themselves, and used ChatGPT 6 only for minor language editing; the Lean formalization is evidence for proof checking.

title: GPT-6 Astra constructs mutually orthogonal Latin squares that improve lower bounds at 33 orders
summary: GPT-6 Astra produced explicit mutually orthogonal Latin-square constructions that improve known lower bounds for N(n) at 33 values of n from 22 through 494. The standout construction gives four MOLS of order 22, completing the last open case needed to show N(n)≥4 for every n>10. The same paper reports resulting bounds at other orders and derives a strongly regular graph with parameters (484,126,40,30) from the order-22 construction; these connected consequences are counted once as one paper-level result.
ai_technology: OpenAI GPT-6 Astra, used through ChatGPT Pro and the OpenAI Codex harness
organization: Christopher D. Rosin (Constructive Codes; independent research project)

evidence.tested: GPT-6 Astra produced explicit mutually orthogonal Latin-square constructions that improve known lower bounds for N(n) at 33 values of n from 22 through 494.
evidence.unknown: This is an arXiv preprint. The constructions are finite combinatorial objects, checked by code written by the author and separately reconstructed/checked by Claude Opus 5.5 as reported in the paper. Counted once despite 33 parameter values and multiple corollaries.
evidence.ai_role: The author states GPT-6 Astra found all listed MOLS constructions and wrote their descriptions/code. The author wrote independent verification code for each construction; the paper also reports an independent Claude Opus 5.5 recreation and verification from the descriptions without the supplied code.

title: GPT-6 Astra finds a counting proof of the Erdős–Sós tree-embedding conjecture
summary: A counting argument proves that every finite graph with average degree greater than t−2 contains every tree on t vertices, resolving the Erdős–Sós conjecture. The proof counts adjacency-marked vertex orderings and uses an induction on the tree to bound those not supporting a rooted copy. The exposition states the sharp classical theorem and records its proof was discovered by GPT-6 Astra; a Lean repository checks the benchmark formalization of the result. Related expository papers of the same proof are aliases, not separate discoveries.
ai_technology: Pre-release OpenAI GPT-6 Astra in the FrontierMath Erdős benchmark
organization: OpenAI FrontierMath Erdős project; exposition by David R. Wood (affiliation not stated in arXiv record)

evidence.tested: A counting argument proves that every finite graph with average degree greater than t−2 contains every tree on t vertices, resolving the Erdős–Sós conjecture.
evidence.unknown: The arXiv paper is an exposition of the proof, not the original benchmark output. The linked Lean proof is machine-checked against the benchmark formalization; the registry notes a minor parity-case difference in that compared statement, while the paper’s counting lemma derives the sharp classical average-degree threshold. This remains a preprint and the formalization is not independently audited here.
evidence.ai_role: GPT-6 Astra autonomously found the counting proof while solving Erdős problem 548 in the FrontierMath Erdős benchmark; the exposition author reports the discovery and lays out the proof. A Lean 4 repository states the proof was machine-checked by a Comparator against the benchmark’s formal statement.

title: Transformer-assisted survey identifies 87 previously unreported low-surface-brightness galaxies in Abell 194
summary: Transfer-learning transformer ensembles applied to deeper Hyper Suprime-Cam images of the Abell 194 cluster contributed to a vetted sample of 171 low-surface-brightness galaxies, including 87 reported as new discoveries. The models identified 159 sample members; Sérsic profile fitting and visual inspection were used to remove likely false positives, and the analysis characterized a subset of 28 ultra-diffuse galaxies. This is one paper-level survey result, not 87 separate catalog entries.
ai_technology: Ensembles of LSBG Detection Transformers (LSBG DETR) and LSBG Vision Transformers (LSBG ViT)
organization: National Centre for Nuclear Research, Poland; Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias; Stony Brook University; National Astronomical Observatory of Japan; collaborating institutions

evidence.tested: Transfer-learning transformer ensembles applied to deeper Hyper Suprime-Cam images of the Abell 194 cluster contributed to a vetted sample of 171 low-surface-brightness galaxies, including 87 reported as new discoveries.
evidence.unknown: The paper reports photometrically defined LSBGs and does not provide spectroscopic confirmation for every new object. The 87 are a sample-level count, not individually confirmed galaxy memberships; 12 of the 171 sample objects were found by visual inspection rather than the transformer models, so AI is not attributed to every sample detection.
evidence.ai_role: Applied models trained on Dark Energy Survey images to find low-surface-brightness structures in deeper HSC images from Abell 194 without fine-tuning; candidate masks were then assessed with Sérsic fits and human visual inspection.

title: Random-forest analysis of continuous seismic waveforms identifies five previously unreported slow-slip events in western Shikoku
summary: A random-forest regression model trained on seismic waveform features predicted GNSS-derived displacement-rate changes over roughly six years in western Shikoku, Japan. Comparing detections with earlier catalogs, the authors report five previously unreported short-term slow-slip events among 23 detected episodes; GNSS deformation patterns and fitted fault models support interpreting the transients as slow slip. The paper-level result is a retrospective detection method and event set, not prospective earthquake prediction.
ai_technology: Random-forest regression model
organization: University of Tokyo; Tohoku University; National Research Institute for Earth Science and Disaster Resilience, Japan

evidence.tested: A random-forest regression model trained on seismic waveform features predicted GNSS-derived displacement-rate changes over roughly six years in western Shikoku, Japan.
evidence.unknown: The study is retrospective and geographically limited to western Shikoku. Model-predicted rates can differ from observations; smoothing can make events appear longer, a practical threshold affects counts (raising it leaves two newly identified events), and the authors state that events without associated tremor may be missed. It does not establish a prospective earthquake-warning capability or a causal trigger for the event that followed the 2016 Kumamoto earthquake.
evidence.ai_role: Mapped statistical features from continuous seismic waveforms to GNSS-derived displacement rates and flagged sharp predicted increases as possible short-term slow-slip events; authors then fitted fault models and compared deformation with existing event catalogs.

title: Regional deep-learning phase picking reveals 24 additional earthquakes in a Gorda Ridge swarm
summary: A long-window regional phase picker and phase-association workflow detected 34 earthquakes in a 29 February 2024 swarm near the Gorda Ridge, offshore northern California: all 10 reported by the USGS plus 24 additional events. The detections were possible from stations roughly 300 km from the swarm, beyond the distance range represented by standard local-event pickers. This is one paper-level catalog result, not 24 separate discoveries.
ai_technology: SKYNET deep-learning P/S phase picker with GENIE graph-neural-network phase association
organization: Stanford University

evidence.tested: A long-window regional phase picker and phase-association workflow detected 34 earthquakes in a 29 February 2024 swarm near the Gorda Ridge, offshore northern California: all 10 reported by the USGS plus 24 additional events.
evidence.unknown: The application covers one swarm day and a specific offshore region. The paper reports 24 additional algorithmically detected events and estimates local magnitudes, but does not claim every event had independent analyst confirmation. SKYNET is designed to complement local pickers; its near-source performance is weaker than PhaseNet, and the result is not a new tectonic mechanism.
evidence.ai_role: SKYNET picked long-duration regional seismic waveforms and GENIE associated the picks into events; their combined workflow supplied the new event detections in sparsely instrumented offshore seismicity.

title: Deep learning reveals migrating foreshocks during laboratory fault nucleation
summary: In biaxial stick-slip experiments on a 0.85 m saw-cut granodiorite fault, the AEbagging ensemble deep-learning picker generated acoustic-emission catalogs for eight laboratory earthquake cycles. The model-derived catalogs revealed a foreshock sequence migrating from a lower-right fault segment toward the upper-left region where the mainshock began, alongside a precursory decrease in the b-value. This is a paper-level laboratory seismology result.
ai_technology: AEbagging ensemble deep-learning acoustic-emission picker
organization: Institute of Geophysics, China Earthquake Administration; MIT; University of Strasbourg/CNRS

evidence.tested: In biaxial stick-slip experiments on a 0.85 m saw-cut granodiorite fault, the AEbagging ensemble deep-learning picker generated acoustic-emission catalogs for eight laboratory earthquake cycles.
evidence.unknown: This is an interpretation of eight controlled stick-slip events on one laboratory fault, not evidence that the same migration pattern is a reliable precursor to natural earthquakes. The authors suggest a possible relation to fault-surface roughness; that causal explanation is not established. The result depends on the model-generated event catalog.
evidence.ai_role: A supervised ensemble of deep neural networks detected acoustic emissions and picked their primary arrivals from continuous multichannel laboratory recordings; its generated event catalogs enabled the authors to resolve the temporal and spatial foreshock migration pattern during nucleation.

title: Symbolic-regression turbulence analysis separates transferable flow physics from dataset-specific closure terms
summary: Using high-fidelity data for plane channels, zero-pressure-gradient turbulent boundary layers and adverse-pressure-gradient boundary layers, the authors used symbolic regression to decompose learned turbulence-closure corrections into inner-layer, outer-layer and pressure-gradient components. They report that retaining the generalisable inner-layer term and adding flow-specific corrections improved predictions on held-out boundary-layer and aerofoil configurations, including unseen geometries and Reynolds numbers, outperforming baseline RANS closures in a priori and a posteriori tests. The authors identify conflation of transferable and training-specific flow behavior as a source of poor model generalization in the tested setting.
ai_technology: Symbolic regression applied to high-fidelity turbulence simulation data
organization: Northwestern Polytechnical University; Pennsylvania State University

evidence.tested: Using high-fidelity data for plane channels, zero-pressure-gradient turbulent boundary layers and adverse-pressure-gradient boundary layers, the authors used symbolic regression to decompose learned turbulence-closure corrections into inner-layer, outer-layer and pressure-gradient components.
evidence.unknown: The finding concerns model-derived closure components and validation on selected numerical flow configurations, not a new direct physical measurement. The claimed root cause of poor generalization is the authors' conclusion about data-driven turbulence closures in the studied context, not a universal causal theorem about all turbulence models. Out-of-sample tests and comparative RANS simulations support the stated transfer result.
evidence.ai_role: Symbolic regression generated interpretable closure expressions from progressively expanded flow datasets. Decomposition of the learned terms let the researchers distinguish inner-layer components that transferred across flow configurations from outer-layer and pressure-gradient corrections that were specific to flow classes, enabling improved out-of-training-flow predictions.

title: Claude discovers algorithms that refute the 3SUM and APSP time-complexity hypotheses
summary: Alman and Vassilevska Williams present deterministic algorithms for 3SUM on polynomial-size integers in O(n^1.9992) time and all-pairs shortest paths on directed graphs with polynomially bounded integer weights in O(n^2.9995) time, the first polynomial improvements over the textbook exponents. The single underlying technique computes selected entries of thin matrix products more efficiently, and known reductions yield the main algorithmic consequences. The paper says an internal Anthropic Claude research model discovered the algorithm autonomously; the human authors then understood, simplified, strengthened and extended it. One paper-level theoretical-computer-science result is counted.
ai_technology: Internal Anthropic Claude research model (specific model version undisclosed)
organization: Anthropic; Columbia University; Massachusetts Institute of Technology

evidence.tested: Alman and Vassilevska Williams present deterministic algorithms for 3SUM on polynomial-size integers in O(n^1.9992) time and all-pairs shortest paths on directed graphs with polynomially bounded integer weights in O(n^2.9995) time, the first polynomial improvements over the textbook exponents.
evidence.unknown: This is an arXiv preprint as of the checked record. The stated time bounds are for polynomially bounded integer inputs; real-valued variants use Las Vegas randomization and different bounds. Lean certification covers the explicitly enumerated theorems, not every statement or presentation detail in the 76-page paper. The authors take responsibility for the paper and developed important extensions/consequences after the initial AI-discovered algorithm.
evidence.ai_role: The paper states that Claude was tasked with checking and improving cryptographic constructions but instead developed the new thin-matrix-product algorithm, first for average-case and then worst-case problems, in a 16-million-output-token session with no human input. The authors subsequently worked to understand, simplify, strengthen and extend the algorithm. Anthropic later used an internal model to Lean-certify specified main results.

title: Semi-supervised machine learning identifies two strong gravitational lenses in the Deep Lens Survey
summary: A ResNetV2-based semi-supervised workflow ranked images from the 20-square-degree Deep Lens Survey and surfaced two Grade-A lens systems for follow-up. Keck spectroscopy secured a source redshift of z=1.81 for DLS212072337, while DLS432021848 has only a tentative single-line redshift but supporting high-resolution Hubble morphology; the paper counts both as lensing systems, with the latter less secure. The broader visually inspected list contains additional candidates, not confirmed lenses.
ai_technology: ResNetV2 neural network with semi-supervised MixMatch or Pi-Model and GAN-based image augmentation
organization: University of California, Davis; University of California, Santa Cruz; University of California, Berkeley

evidence.tested: A ResNetV2-based semi-supervised workflow ranked images from the 20-square-degree Deep Lens Survey and surfaced two Grade-A lens systems for follow-up.
evidence.unknown: This is a paper-level result about a survey search and validated lens identification, not a claim that all 22 visually graded systems are confirmed. DLS212072337 has secure spectroscopic source and deflector redshifts; DLS432021848 has an ambiguous single emission line and is judged likely from HST morphology rather than conclusive spectroscopy. arXiv version 1 is a preprint; current full text was updated in 2026.
evidence.ai_role: Ranked galaxy-survey images for strong-lensing morphology; the top-ranked systems were then human-inspected and followed up spectroscopically/imaged to validate lensing.

title: Machine-learning-guided search discovers and synthesizes the rare-earth-free magnet Fe₃CoB₂
summary: A feedback workflow combining machine learning, an adaptive genetic algorithm, first-principles calculations, and experiments identified and synthesized Fe₃CoB₂, a rare-earth-free magnetic compound. Magnetic measurements reported saturation polarization Js=1.39 T and anisotropy K1=1.2 MJ/m³, properties the authors describe as suitable for rare-earth-free permanent-magnet applications. This is a discovery and synthesis of a material compound; commercial performance or device readiness was not demonstrated.
ai_technology: Machine-learning-guided adaptive feedback with an adaptive genetic algorithm and first-principles calculations
organization: Ames Laboratory; Iowa State University; University of Nebraska–Lincoln; University of Texas at Austin; University of Tokyo; Yantai University; Zhejiang Agriculture and Forestry University

evidence.tested: A feedback workflow combining machine learning, an adaptive genetic algorithm, first-principles calculations, and experiments identified and synthesized Fe₃CoB₂, a rare-earth-free magnetic compound.
evidence.unknown: The paper reports an experimentally synthesized compound and magnetic measurements, but suitability is for potential rare-earth-free permanent-magnet applications; no commercial device demonstration is reported. The workflow combines ML with adaptive genetic search, DFT and human synthesis/measurement.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning screened and informed the material search, while adaptive genetic structure search and first-principles calculations guided candidates; researchers synthesized the selected compound and measured its magnetic properties. The discovery is attributed to the integrated workflow, not the ML model alone.

title: Claude Code produces the first primary Lund jet-plane density measurement in electron–positron collisions
summary: A Claude Code agent pipeline analyzed archived 1994 ALEPH hadronic-Z data and reported the first primary Lund jet-plane density measurement in e⁺e⁻ collisions. Its unfolded 57-bin fiducial result shows the expected triangular QCD radiation structure and a shallow low-transverse-momentum turnover; the integrated mean primary-emission count is 4.751 ± 0.224 per hemisphere. This is one new measurement, not a claim of discovering new particles or physics beyond QCD.
ai_technology: Claude Code agents orchestrated by the Just Furnish Context (JFC) framework
organization: Massachusetts Institute of Technology; NSF AI Institute for Artificial Intelligence and Fundamental Interactions; CERN; ALEPH Collaboration archival data

evidence.tested: A Claude Code agent pipeline analyzed archived 1994 ALEPH hadronic-Z data and reported the first primary Lund jet-plane density measurement in e⁺e⁻ collisions.
evidence.unknown: This is an arXiv preprint, and the authors explicitly qualify the novel measurement as subject to independent verification. It uses 1994 ALEPH data and one available full-simulation sample; the corrected density is prior/model dependent, with a reported 6.0% density-weighted total uncertainty and 4.7% uncertainty on the integrated count. The shallow residual shape is within current generator-theory uncertainty, so the paper frames it as a benchmark rather than evidence excluding generators.
evidence.ai_role: Agents planned and executed the event selection, jet declustering, unfolding, uncertainty propagation, statistical checks and report drafting using archived ALEPH data and literature retrieval. The paper attributes the new Lund-plane measurement to an autonomous AI-agent analysis pipeline; human authors supplied the broad task and review framework.

title: Time-delay neural networks expose three fault-development phases across laboratory pressure regimes
summary: A time-delay neural network trained on multi-parameter acoustic-emission records from Alzo-granite triaxial tests at 5–40 MPa resolved three recurring phases: microcrack nucleation marked by waveform-scattering changes, fault growth with evolving spatial and magnitude distributions, and coalescence marked by peak-delay increases and b-value changes. The model also predicted stress-drop timing and size across axial-splitting and shear-localization failures. This is a laboratory result, not a natural-earthquake precursor claim.
ai_technology: Genetic-algorithm-optimized time-delay neural network (TDNN)
organization: University of Birmingham; University of Cambridge

evidence.tested: A time-delay neural network trained on multi-parameter acoustic-emission records from Alzo-granite triaxial tests at 5–40 MPa resolved three recurring phases: microcrack nucleation marked by waveform-scattering changes, fault growth with evolving spatial and magnitude distributions, and coalescence marked by peak-delay increases and b-value changes.
evidence.unknown: The analysis uses four laboratory experiments in Alzo granite, so results are sample- and apparatus-limited and do not establish natural-earthquake predictability. Training-data smoothing and the small number of experiments constrain generalization; stress estimates show more variability and modelled subtle phase transitions are less accurate. The observed phase interpretation is based on model-assisted analysis of acoustic emissions and measured mechanical data.
evidence.ai_role: The TDNN integrated time-dependent acoustic-emission waveform features (peak delay, coda Q/scattering) and occurrence measures (event rate, Gutenberg–Richter b-value, spatial fractal dimension), dynamically weighting them to model stress/strain evolution and identify repeatable phases across pressure conditions. Leave-one-experiment-out validation tested cross-condition generalization.

title: Machine-learning seismicity maps a 250-km eastern edge of the subducted Yakutat microplate
summary: An expanded machine-learning earthquake catalog and complementary receiver-function and ambient-noise images reveal a previously unrecognized, roughly 250-km linear cluster of about 1,750 earthquakes that the authors interpret as tracing the northeastern/eastern edge of the subducted Yakutat microplate beneath south-central Alaska. The inferred slab edge lies beneath the curved Denali fault; its possible role in the 2002 Mw 7.9 earthquake’s nucleation is a hypothesis, not an established cause.
ai_technology: Modified EQTransformer machine-learning seismic phase picker, REAL phase associator, and NonLinLoc locator
organization: Australian National University; South Dakota School of Mines and Technology; University of California, Davis

evidence.tested: An expanded machine-learning earthquake catalog and complementary receiver-function and ambient-noise images reveal a previously unrecognized, roughly 250-km linear cluster of about 1,750 earthquakes that the authors interpret as tracing the northeastern/eastern edge of the subducted Yakutat microplate beneath south-central Alaska.
evidence.unknown: This is a localized tectonic interpretation from data collected between 2018 and 2021, not prospective earthquake prediction. The 64,870-event catalog reports average location uncertainties of about 5.0 km latitude, 5.2 km longitude and 8.6 km depth; the authors support the slab-edge interpretation with seismicity, receiver functions, tremor distribution and ambient-noise tomography. They propose—but do not establish—that the slab edge influenced nucleation of the 2002 Denali earthquake and the position of volcanic fields.
evidence.ai_role: The ML phase picker helped construct a denser earthquake catalog from permanent and temporary station records. The 64,870-event catalog exposed the previously unseen long linear earthquake cluster; receiver-function and ambient-noise tomography supplied independent complementary images used to interpret its relationship to the Yakutat slab edge.

title: GPT-5.6 constructs a counterexample to Talagrand’s operator cotype problem
summary: The paper gives a negative answer, already for q=2, to Talagrand’s question whether an operator’s Rademacher cotype is universally bounded by its Gaussian cotype and its (q,1)-summing norm. For every sufficiently large power-of-two dimension it constructs a Banach space and operator violating such a universal bound. The same construction also yields a negative answer to Kwapień’s decomposition problem.
ai_technology: ChatGPT GPT-5.6
organization: Xinglong Wu (author affiliation not stated in the arXiv record)

evidence.tested: The paper gives a negative answer, already for q=2, to Talagrand’s question whether an operator’s Rademacher cotype is universally bounded by its Gaussian cotype and its (q,1)-summing norm.
evidence.unknown: This is a single-author arXiv preprint, not a peer-reviewed publication. GPT-5.6 is credited with discovering the counterexample during discussions; the author says they independently verified all arguments. No Lean or other proof-assistant formalization is reported. The mathematical scope is the stated q=2 counterexample and its stated corollary, not a complete characterization of operator cotype.
evidence.ai_role: The author states that the counterexample was discovered during discussions with GPT-5.6. The paper presents an explicit Walsh–Hadamard-based construction and proof; the author independently verified the arguments.

title: A dense nodal array and machine learning reveal a blind fault zone beneath the San Fernando Valley
summary: A machine-learning workflow analyzed one month of recordings from a 140-station nodal array and located 62 earthquakes, including 36 not in the regional catalog. Their distribution exposes a previously unidentified 5.3 × 4 km blind fault zone about 5 km beneath the southern San Fernando Valley; the small-event cluster is rare in the regional catalog despite a 2014 Mb 4.4 earthquake in the zone.
ai_technology: Previously developed machine-learning seismic phase picker, fine-tuned on similar waveforms, with two-step event association
organization: University of Texas at Austin; University of Houston

evidence.tested: A machine-learning workflow analyzed one month of recordings from a 140-station nodal array and located 62 earthquakes, including 36 not in the regional catalog.
evidence.unknown: This is a one-month temporary-array study reported as an arXiv preprint. The fault-zone dimensions and location are inferred from a small cluster of newly detected microearthquakes, not from direct imaging or a long-term catalog; it informs hazard mapping but does not predict future earthquakes.
evidence.ai_role: The model detected weak earthquake signals and picked seismic phases in high-noise recordings, enabling the expanded local event catalog from which the blind fault-zone cluster was interpreted.

title: Machine learning attributes post-2015 emissions to intensification of Europe’s recent heat extremes
summary: A diffusion model trained on ten CMIP6 climate models estimated event-specific temperature changes conditional on observed meteorology. It found >95% probability that anthropogenic emissions since the 2015 Paris Agreement intensified Europe’s summer temperature extremes in 2021–2025; for the June 2025 heatwave, regional mean temperature is estimated to have been 0.34 °C lower under 2015 cumulative emissions, with >99% probability.
ai_technology: Generative diffusion model for spatially explicit temperature fields
organization: Stanford University; Boston University; University of Auckland; Colorado State University

evidence.tested: A diffusion model trained on ten CMIP6 climate models estimated event-specific temperature changes conditional on observed meteorology.
evidence.unknown: This event-specific attribution is conditioned on observed large-scale meteorology and trained on ten CMIP6 models; it is not a direct experiment that removed emissions. The paper emphasizes uncertainty from internal variability/model spread and reports robust regional-mean effects, while grid-cell-level changes are more limited. The June 2025 value is a median modeled counterfactual estimate.
evidence.ai_role: The model learned climate-model relationships between meteorological conditions, cumulative CO₂ emissions and daily temperature fields, then generated conditional counterfactual temperature distributions to attribute the incremental post-2015 emissions effect to recent European heat extremes.

title: Observation-trained machine learning halves estimated Arctic winter sea-ice surface cooling
summary: A neural network trained on observations from five Arctic field campaigns reduced ERA5 errors in the Arctic sea-ice surface energy budget and removed ERA5’s wintertime near-surface warm bias of about 4 K. The corrected estimates imply about 50% weaker winter surface cooling and 80–120 cm seasonal thermodynamic ice growth, closer to SMOS–CryoSat thickness increases than ERA5’s 150–200 cm estimate.
ai_technology: Feed-forward neural network product SEBai
organization: Alfred Wegener Institute; Helmholtz Centre Hereon; Helmholtz AI; Deutsches Klimarechenzentrum; NOAA Physical Sciences Laboratory; University of Leeds; Norwegian Polar Institute; Karlsruhe Institute of Technology; Stockholm University; Washington State University

evidence.tested: A neural network trained on observations from five Arctic field campaigns reduced ERA5 errors in the Arctic sea-ice surface energy budget and removed ERA5’s wintertime near-surface warm bias of about 4 K.
evidence.unknown: Validation uses leave-one-campaign-out cross-validation and multiple field campaigns, but direct flux observations remain sparse in space and time. The climatology applies to ice-covered Arctic regions north of 70°N with sea-ice concentration above 80%; authors do not recommend extrapolation to marginal ice zones or coastal regions. The ice-growth values are thermodynamic estimates rather than direct pan-Arctic measurements.
evidence.ai_role: The network learned the relationship between ERA5 atmospheric states and observed fluxes from MOSAiC, SHEBA, AO2018, N-ICE2015 and ARTofMELT campaigns, then bias-corrected hourly Arctic sea-ice surface fluxes for 1994–2024 to derive a revised regional climatology and ice-growth estimates.

title: Transformer-guided genetic search finds six new champion linear error-correcting codes over F₈
summary: A transformer trained to predict minimum Hamming distance, paired with a genetic algorithm and exact Brouwer–Zimmermann distance checks, found at least six previously unknown champion generalized toric codes over F₈ at dimensions 18, 22 and 38 (length 49). The article reports more than 500 champion codes in its F₈ search and up to a twofold reduction in exact distance evaluations versus random search. The six records at the three newly improved parameter settings are one paper-level coding-theory result.
ai_technology: Transformer model adapted from GPT-2, coupled with a genetic algorithm
organization: University of London; University of Warwick; University of Oxford; London Institute for Mathematical Sciences

evidence.tested: A transformer trained to predict minimum Hamming distance, paired with a genetic algorithm and exact Brouwer–Zimmermann distance checks, found at least six previously unknown champion generalized toric codes over F₈ at dimensions 18, 22 and 38 (length 49).
evidence.unknown: The codes are newly discovered mathematical constructions in the generalized toric family, with minimum distances verified computationally using established exact algorithms and compared to known records. The reported >500 total includes known/previous champion codes, while six at dimensions 18, 22 and 38 are identified as novel; these are not six separate catalog entries. The method searches a restricted family and does not establish optimal codes over all linear codes or quantum codes.
evidence.ai_role: The transformer predicts generalized toric codes’ minimum Hamming distances and guides genetic search toward promising generator matrices. Candidate champions are then checked with the Brouwer–Zimmermann algorithm and compared with known bounds; the paper reports six previously unknown champion codes at F₈ dimensions 18, 22 and 38.

title: GPT-5.6 helps prove an exact mapping between frustrated and field-driven spin chains
summary: A single-author preprint proves that every finite one-dimensional open O(n) spin chain with arbitrary inhomogeneous nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor interactions has an exact, temperature-independent Hamiltonian mapping to a simpler nearest-neighbor chain with axial single-spin potentials. A parallel result for q-state Potts chains yields a closed-form solution for every q ≥ 2 and finite chain length. The theorem generalizes a 1990 Heisenberg-chain challenge and connects spontaneous collective behavior from competing interactions to field-induced behavior.
ai_technology: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol; GPT-5.6 Sol Pro for final adversarial manuscript review
organization: Brookhaven National Laboratory

evidence.tested: A single-author preprint proves that every finite one-dimensional open O(n) spin chain with arbitrary inhomogeneous nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor interactions has an exact, temperature-independent Hamiltonian mapping to a simpler nearest-neighbor chain with axial single-spin potentials.
evidence.unknown: This is a single-author arXiv preprint, not yet peer reviewed. The theorem concerns classical one-dimensional open chains and exact Hamiltonian mappings; the paper discusses possible experimental relevance but reports no experimental test. The author assumes responsibility for reviewing and verifying AI-generated content; Mathematica 14.3 was also used to verify results.
evidence.ai_role: The author credits GPT-5.6 Sol with scientific discovery, including generating the recursive Householder moving-frame proof and recognizing broad generalizations. The author identified the hidden reciprocity, extended the theorem to arbitrary spatial inhomogeneity, and states that all AI-generated scientific content was reviewed and verified. GPT-5.6 Sol Pro conducted a final adversarial review.

title: Generative AI designs and experimentally validates an ultrathin broadband ENZ absorber
summary: A generative deep neural network searched multilayer indium-tin-oxide/aluminum-doped-zinc-oxide designs and selected an epsilon-near-zero absorber stack. After the researchers merged two similar adjacent layers for fabrication, the approximately 159-nm device experimentally maintained more than 98% absorption over a 1,077-nm near-infrared bandwidth at 49° p-polarized illumination. The modeled design predicted 1,688 nm bandwidth; the experiment’s detector cutoff limited measurements above 2,600 nm.
ai_technology: GLONet generative deep neural network, trained in simulation loop with differentiable transfer-matrix solver TMM-Fast
organization: University of California, Irvine; Los Alamos National Laboratory; Center for Integrated Nanotechnologies

evidence.tested: A generative deep neural network searched multilayer indium-tin-oxide/aluminum-doped-zinc-oxide designs and selected an epsilon-near-zero absorber stack.
evidence.unknown: The demonstrated result is a fabricated device under p-polarized illumination at a 49° incidence angle using a prism-coupled ENZ mode; it is not an angle-independent or application-qualified absorber. Measurement above 2,600 nm was limited by the detector, so the 1,688-nm bandwidth is a simulation result and the measured bandwidth is 1,077 nm. The network-produced four-layer design was manually simplified by merging two similar layers before fabrication. Earlier work by the same group used neural networks to design homogeneous ITO stacks; this paper reports a distinct heterogeneous ITO/AZO design with experimental validation. No commercial application is demonstrated.
evidence.ai_role: The GLONet maps random latent vectors to multilayer designs, optimizing per-layer refractive/material parameters and thickness using differentiable optical simulations to maximize broadband absorption. The authors generated 10,000 candidate stacks and selected a high-performing design for experimental fabrication and measurement. A manual layer-merging step simplified the four-layer design to three layers before fabrication.

title: AI-assisted Hubble asteroid sample extends the shallow size-distribution slope to H≈20
summary: Using 632 serendipitously imaged Hubble Space Telescope asteroids found by the prior AI-assisted Hubble Asteroid Hunter survey, the authors fit trail parallax to estimate distances, absolute magnitudes, and approximate sizes. Their cumulative magnitude distribution has a shallower slope (α≈0.26) from H=15 to about H=20, extending the previously reported trend by roughly two magnitudes; the analyzed sample is dominated by potential main-belt objects smaller than 1 km.
ai_technology: Google Cloud deep-learning asteroid-trail detector trained on Hubble Asteroid Hunter citizen-science classifications (upstream survey)
organization: European Space Agency; European Space Astronomy Centre; Autonomous University of Madrid; Astronomical Institute of the Romanian Academy; University of Craiova; Jet Propulsion Laboratory; Université Côte d’Azur

evidence.tested: Using 632 serendipitously imaged Hubble Space Telescope asteroids found by the prior AI-assisted Hubble Asteroid Hunter survey, the authors fit trail parallax to estimate distances, absolute magnitudes, and approximate sizes.
evidence.unknown: The 632-object sample comprises 454 unmatched and 178 known objects; unmatched does not mean every object is independently confirmed or has a reliable orbit. Only about 40% of raw objects yielded meaningful distance estimates after filtering. Sizes assume spherical objects and a uniform albedo of 0.15. The authors state that the combined archive sample is not a dedicated or observationally unbiased survey, and the result is an extension of the size-distribution slope to H≈20 rather than a complete census.
evidence.ai_role: The primary study states that the input asteroid trails were detected in the preceding Hubble Asteroid Hunter work using a deep-learning algorithm trained on volunteer classifications. This AI-assisted search supplied the previously unidentified trail sample; the present paper then applies a parallax-fitting method and magnitude-distribution analysis to characterize it. The quantitative population result depends on this archive-scale AI-assisted detection pipeline and the present physical analysis.

title: AI-guided CORONA imagery search finds four archaeologically verified tells in Abu Ghraib
summary: A fine-tuned deep-learning model trained with 1960s CORONA satellite images flagged eight previously unrecognized tell candidates in Iraq's Abu Ghraib district. Archaeologists investigated all eight; four contained surface ceramic sherds confirming archaeological remains and enabling dating. The AI suggestions led the field team to inspect locations that routine surveys would not have visited.
ai_technology: MANet deep convolutional segmentation network with attention, transfer learning and two-stage fine-tuning
organization: University of Bologna

evidence.tested: A fine-tuned deep-learning model trained with 1960s CORONA satellite images flagged eight previously unrecognized tell candidates in Iraq's Abu Ghraib district.
evidence.unknown: This is an arXiv preprint. The results are limited to mounded tell sites in Abu Ghraib and depend on a small training set (208 images) and archaeologist-selected field follow-up. Four of eight AI-suggested sites were confirmed; the other four should not be described as archaeological finds. The source reports that the four confirmed sites were destroyed or no longer visible on the ground, with sherds establishing their presence and dates.
evidence.ai_role: Researchers retrained the existing neural model using CORONA historical imagery and generated probability heatmaps that archaeologists used to select previously unrecognized locations for field reconnaissance. Eight AI-suggested sites were investigated; four were confirmed through collected and studied ceramic sherds. The authors state the four locations would not have been investigated in routine field surveys without the model's suggestions.

title: Deep-learning ComPACT catalogue adds 116 previously unreported galaxy clusters
summary: Analysis of the CNN-detected ComPACT Sunyaev–Zel’dovich catalogue identified 116 previously unreported galaxy clusters with new redshift estimates, including five massive systems (M500c > 6 × 10^14 solar masses) at z > 0.7. The authors report 158 new cluster-mass determinations and higher completeness than ACT DR5 at fixed purity, especially for massive high-redshift systems.
ai_technology: ComPACT deep-learning convolutional neural network catalogue, followed by optical photometric redshift and SZ mass analysis
organization: Space Research Institute, Russian Academy of Sciences; HSE University; Lomonosov Moscow State University

evidence.tested: Analysis of the CNN-detected ComPACT Sunyaev–Zel’dovich catalogue identified 116 previously unreported galaxy clusters with new redshift estimates, including five massive systems (M500c > 6 × 10^14 solar masses) at z > 0.7.
evidence.unknown: The ComPACT catalogue contains 2,962 SZ-selected candidates; the paper confirms approximately 60% as clusters, so the full candidate list must not be treated as confirmed. Its newly reported cluster count relies on cross-matches and optical photometric-redshift significance criteria with an estimated 5% false-positive rate; most are not presented as new spectroscopic confirmations. Masses are scaling-relation estimates. The five high-mass, high-redshift systems are identified with redshift algorithms and SZ measurements, and their interpretation remains subject to catalogue selection/completeness and mass-estimation uncertainties.
evidence.ai_role: The CNN detected SZ cluster candidates in combined ACT+Planck maps, creating the candidate catalogue analyzed here. The authors used existing catalogues and DESI Legacy Imaging Survey photometry to validate systems and estimate redshifts, and ACT+Planck/Planck Compton-y maps with SZ scaling relations to derive masses. The CNN catalogue has higher completeness than ACT DR5 at fixed purity, particularly at high mass and redshift; it is the entry point enabling these new cluster identifications and measurements.

title: PCFNet-guided spectroscopy confirms four protoclusters at redshift 3.3–3.4
summary: Subaru/MOIRCS spectroscopy of four PCFNet-selected candidate regions confirmed four protoclusters at z = 3.316, 3.403, 3.408 and 3.425, across three regions, with galaxy-density peaks more than five times the uniform distribution. Twenty-three spectroscopically identified members are largely on the star-forming main sequence. Model-weighted estimates put star-formation-rate density above cosmic averages, while metallicity differences are marginal in two systems and consistent with the field in the others.
ai_technology: PCFNet point-cloud deep-learning protocluster finder
organization: The University of Tokyo; National Astronomical Observatory of Japan; Tohoku University; Subaru Telescope

evidence.tested: Subaru/MOIRCS spectroscopy of four PCFNet-selected candidate regions confirmed four protoclusters at z = 3.316, 3.403, 3.408 and 3.425, across three regions, with galaxy-density peaks more than five times the uniform distribution.
evidence.unknown: This is a small follow-up sample: four of 121 PCFNet candidates were targeted, and the parent catalogue is trained on simulated galaxies. Four protoclusters are confirmed across three of four observed regions; a fourth observed candidate region had no significant redshift peak. One of the confirmed regions had previously been reported as a photometric candidate, so this is a spectroscopic confirmation/characterization result rather than four wholly unprecedented structures. The halo masses are inferred from member stellar masses, not direct lensing measurements. The elevated SFR densities depend on membership-probability weighting and are sensitive to assumed geometry, volume and methodology. Metallicity excesses are only 1.4–2 sigma in two systems; two others are statistically consistent with the field. The authors’ proposed gas-inflow/recycling explanation is interpretive.
evidence.ai_role: PCFNet used broad-band optical photometry and galaxy positions to assign protocluster-membership probabilities and identify candidate regions. The model outputs determined which regions received Subaru/MOIRCS follow-up and prioritized slit targets; their probabilities also informed member selection and the authors’ volume/SFR-density estimator. Spectroscopy then tested those predictions, finding a 40% member detection rate among high-probability galaxies and confirming three of four observed regions.

title: AI-guided experiments uncover a new polymer polymorph and improve organic transistor performance
summary: An AI-powered advisor in an autonomous fabrication-and-test platform guided 64 trials of mixed ion–electron conducting polymers for organic electrochemical transistors. The study reports a mobility–volumetric-capacitance figure of merit up to 1,275 F cm⁻¹ V⁻¹ s⁻¹, a 150% improvement over conventional spin coating, identifies larger crystalline lamellar spacing and greater specific surface area as favorable structural factors, and reports a previously unknown polymer polymorph.
ai_technology: Adaptive AI decision interface and AI advisor integrated with autonomous electronic-material fabrication and testing
organization: The University of Chicago; Argonne National Laboratory; Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory; University of Southern Mississippi

evidence.tested: An AI-powered advisor in an autonomous fabrication-and-test platform guided 64 trials of mixed ion–electron conducting polymers for organic electrochemical transistors.
evidence.unknown: The primary source describes a single mixed-ion/electron conducting polymer system and an organic electrochemical transistor testbed. The reported 150% figure-of-merit improvement is relative to conventional spin coating in the study. Structural-factor associations come from a small set of ten statistically selected samples; they are not general causal rules. The new polymorph is reported in the primary paper, but the available abstract does not establish broader stability or device lifetime. The platform includes human-AI interaction and laboratory personnel performed synthesis, fabrication and characterization.
evidence.ai_role: The AI advisor monitored experimental progress in real time, analyzed results and collaborated interactively with researchers to adapt the fabrication, testing and analysis steps across a data-limited campaign. The resulting AI/AE workflow guided experimental exploration over 64 autonomous trials; the model did not merely predict properties from a benchmark dataset. Human researchers synthesized polymers, fabricated devices and performed electrical and structural characterization.

title: Unsupervised learning separates rockfall and glacier-sliding precursors before the Blatten collapse
summary: Unsupervised clustering of 20 days of seismic data before the 28 May 2025 Blatten glacier collapse separated rockfall signals from events associated with basal glacier sliding. Sliding-related event counts accelerated approximately exponentially beginning about five days before collapse, with further acceleration about 1.5 days beforehand; the authors interpret this pattern as consistent with nucleation-like slip weakening.
ai_technology: Deep scattering network, independent component analysis and hierarchical clustering (unsupervised machine learning)
organization: Université Grenoble Alpes; Institut de Physique du Globe de Paris; University of Tokyo; Service des dangers naturels, Valais

evidence.tested: Unsupervised clustering of 20 days of seismic data before the 28 May 2025 Blatten glacier collapse separated rockfall signals from events associated with basal glacier sliding.
evidence.unknown: The finding is a retrospective analysis of one event, relying primarily on a single seismic station 5.3 km from the site. The authors describe the physical mechanism as consistent with nucleation and hypothesize that rockfalls contributed to instability; these interpretations require study of other events. The inferred slip-rate proxy has high absolute uncertainty, and the approach is not an operational early-warning system.
evidence.ai_role: The unsupervised representation and clustering explored continuous single-station seismic records without event templates, separating rockfall, glacier-sliding and cultural-noise signatures. This made the evolving sliding-related event population and its acceleration measurable in the 20-day record.

title: Machine learning reconstructs deep-time crustal thickness and links thickening episodes with porphyry deposits
summary: A machine-learning mohometry model estimated paleo-crustal thickness from 66 geochemical proxies across subduction, collision and intraplate settings, extending chemical reconstruction beyond arc-related rocks. Tested reconstructions for southern Tibet and South China agreed with independently constrained crustal histories (R² = 0.937; RMSE = 4.3 km). The authors report that reconstructed thickening episodes correlate with porphyry-ore formation in ancient orogens.
ai_technology: Machine-learning mohometry regression model with feature-importance filtering
organization: Ocean University of China; University of Sydney; University of Tasmania; Laoshan Laboratory

evidence.tested: A machine-learning mohometry model estimated paleo-crustal thickness from 66 geochemical proxies across subduction, collision and intraplate settings, extending chemical reconstruction beyond arc-related rocks.
evidence.unknown: The ancient thickness histories and porphyry association are model-derived reconstructions, not direct measurements of past Moho depth or proof that thickening caused ore formation. Validation is reported in southern Tibet and the South China Block; R²/RMSE summarize the model data and do not remove uncertainty from proxy assumptions, tectonic context or the geological record. The study reports a correlation that may inform exploration, not a validated mineral-deposit prediction system.
evidence.ai_role: The regression model learned relationships between whole-rock geochemical measurements and Moho depth from a global database spanning subduction, collision and intraplate tectonic settings. It estimated ancient crust thickness from records that may be missing elements and enabled reconstruction beyond arc magmas; feature-importance filtering highlighted geochemical proxies. Those model-derived reconstructions supported the paper’s comparison of crust-thickening episodes with porphyry-deposit timing.

title: MACE-guided screening yields three corundum high-entropy oxides and a cation-ordered oxide
summary: MACE-MP-0b2 interatomic-potential calculations screened 462 four- and five-cation trivalent-oxide compositions and selected 16 for synthesis. Experiments produced three phase-pure corundum high-entropy oxides—(Al,Cr,Fe,Ga)₂O₃, (Al,Cr,Fe,Rh,Sc)₂O₃ and (Cr,Fe,Ga,Rh,Sc)₂O₃—and a separate phase-pure cation-ordered (Al,Fe,Ga,Sc)₂O₃ oxide. The ordered compound crystallized in orthorhombic Pba2; its precise cation-site occupancies were not resolved conclusively by powder diffraction.
ai_technology: MACE-MP-0b2 machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP)
organization: University of British Columbia

evidence.tested: MACE-MP-0b2 interatomic-potential calculations screened 462 four- and five-cation trivalent-oxide compositions and selected 16 for synthesis.
evidence.unknown: This is an unrefereed arXiv preprint. Only three of 16 tested compositions formed phase-pure corundum high-entropy oxides; most attempts produced competing phases, and rhodium-containing samples showed redox instability. Synthesis outcomes depended strongly on route: the three corundum HEOs were phase-pure only with one of solid-state or combustion synthesis. The ordered oxide’s structure is supported by powder diffraction/Rietveld refinement, but exact site preferences could not be conclusively determined from pXRD. The screening supports candidate ranking, not reliable prediction of phase purity or synthesis conditions for arbitrary HEOs.
evidence.ai_role: The MLIP relaxed approximately 1,000-atom disordered supercells and estimated mixing enthalpy and atom-energy-distribution descriptors for the 462-composition search. The authors combined these with a stability metric to rank 16 synthesis candidates. Experimental powder-X-ray diffraction and Rietveld refinement then assessed the predicted materials, linking model-guided selection to the new synthesized compositions.

title: LLM-guided experiments identify three phases unique to the ternary Co–Al–Ge system
summary: Researchers used an LLM to plan iterative composition measurements and experimentally mapped the Co–Al–Ge phase diagram at 900 °C. The domain-specific aLLoyM model directed early measurements into compositionally complex interior regions, enabling the earliest discovery of all three novel phases reported to form only in the ternary system; the general-purpose LLM strategy found more phases in fewer cycles. This is an arXiv preprint and the finding is bounded to this experimental phase-diagram study.
ai_technology: aLLoyM domain-specific large language model and general-purpose LLM experimental planner
organization: National Institute for Materials Science; Tohoku University; University of Tokyo

evidence.tested: Researchers used an LLM to plan iterative composition measurements and experimentally mapped the Co–Al–Ge phase diagram at 900 °C.
evidence.unknown: This source is an arXiv preprint, not a peer-reviewed journal publication as of the checked record. The source abstract supports the reported ternary phase-diagram result and three phases described as novel and ternary-only, but does not provide their formulas or independent replication evidence in the abstract. The discovery is a bounded materials result, not a claim that every phase in the full ternary diagram has been exhaustively mapped.
evidence.ai_role: LLMs selected compositions for each cycle in a closed loop with high-throughput synthesis and X-ray diffraction phase identification. The original abstract specifically attributes earliest discovery of all three newly reported ternary-only phases to aLLoyM-guided initial measurements; a general-purpose LLM chose a textbook-like measurement strategy that efficiently found a larger number of phases in fewer cycles.

title: Machine-learning mapping finds broader preservation of pre-glacial landscapes across Arctic Canada and Greenland
summary: A random-forest model using six terrain morphometrics from ArcticDEM classified glacial erosional styles across Arctic Canada and Greenland. The map indicates that regions with little or no glacial erosion, and thus potentially preserved pre-glacial landscape fragments, occur more widely than previous mapping recognized; it also finds distinct morphologies between Greenland and Canada. The authors infer that inherited topography, ice dynamics, latitude and geology help shape these patterns.
ai_technology: Random-forest machine-learning classifier
organization: Durham University; Newcastle University

evidence.tested: A random-forest model using six terrain morphometrics from ArcticDEM classified glacial erosional styles across Arctic Canada and Greenland.
evidence.unknown: The paper reports validation accuracy of about 79.5% (±4.6%) and notes low classification probabilities in some areas, where training coverage or coarse classes may limit confidence. “Little or no glacial erosion” is a model classification interpreted as possible preservation of pre-glacial terrain, not direct dating or field confirmation of every mapped tile. Proposed controls such as ice dynamics and basal hydrology are interpretations, not demonstrated causal mechanisms.
evidence.ai_role: The random forest classified ArcticDEM tiles using six elevation-derived morphometric variables, assigning class probabilities at continental scale and producing model-derived feature-importance estimates. This enabled a quantitative revision of prior qualitative landscape maps and the reported finding that minimally glacially modified terrain is more widespread than previously mapped.

title: Transformer-based SDSS search identifies two previously unreported optical–UV tidal disruption events
summary: A PCA-enhanced Transformer classifier screened 298,195 SDSS DR7 spectra and selected 14 TDE-like cases for secondary review. The authors report two newly identified TDEs: SDSS J124225.39+642919.0, whose GALEX UV source was present by the spectrum date (before 11 February 2002), and SDSS J152459.70+045423.1, whose TDE-H+He spectrum coincided with a Catalina optical outburst in 2007–08. The first is reported as the earliest optical–UV TDE then known; one other model-selected source was a previously reported likely TDE.
ai_technology: PCA-enhanced Transformer TDE spectrum classifier
organization: University of Science and Technology of China; Purple Mountain Observatory; Chinese Academy of Sciences

evidence.tested: A PCA-enhanced Transformer classifier screened 298,195 SDSS DR7 spectra and selected 14 TDE-like cases for secondary review.
evidence.unknown: The source is an arXiv preprint whose arXiv record says accepted by The Astrophysical Journal; no journal DOI was supplied in the source checked. The TDE classifications are supported by spectral and contemporaneous archival photometric evidence, not new contemporaneous follow-up observations. The event dates predate 2020, but this record uses the 2026 source-publication date for the since-2020 catalog period. The paper also reports a third previously known likely TDE, which is not counted as a new discovery.
evidence.ai_role: The Transformer classifier screened preprocessed SDSS galaxy spectra and selected TDE-like events for follow-up assessment. From roughly 298,000 spectra it produced 14 cases above the selection threshold; after checking spectral features against archival GALEX or Catalina variability and other diagnostics, the authors reported two previously unreported TDEs and one previously reported likely TDE. Reported test-set precision and recall were 0.88 and 0.99, respectively.

title: Physics-informed generative learning yields experimentally verified single-phase B2 intermetallic alloys
summary: A conditional variational autoencoder and artificial neural network, using physics-informed descriptors of B2 sublattice ordering, generated and ranked compositions in complex alloy systems. Experimental synthesis and XRD/TEM characterization verified previously unreported single-phase B2 alloys, including three Fe–Co–Ni–Ti–Zr compositions, Co19.9Ni30.5Ti38.1Zr11.5, and Cu4.7Co9.2Ni36.4Ti38.7Zr7.4Hf3.5. The study reports that random-sublattice descriptors separated B2 from multiphase alloys more effectively than conventional random-mixing descriptors in these datasets.
ai_technology: Physics-informed conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) and artificial neural network (ANN)
organization: Central South University; City University of Hong Kong; City University of Hong Kong (Dongguan); Shanghai University

evidence.tested: A conditional variational autoencoder and artificial neural network, using physics-informed descriptors of B2 sublattice ordering, generated and ranked compositions in complex alloy systems.
evidence.unknown: The result is one paper-level experimental discovery program; individual alloys are not counted separately. Experiments validated selected compositions from a small subset of the generated search space, not all model proposals. The authors report several new single-phase B2 compositions and strong structural characterization for named samples; broader property superiority and generalization to arbitrary alloy systems are not inferred here. Synthesis and characterization were performed by researchers.
evidence.ai_role: The ANN learned B2-versus-non-B2 phase likelihoods from historical alloy-composition data using 18 physics-informed descriptors, while the conditional VAE generated candidate compositions. ANN scores filtered generated compositions for experimental validation. The paper reports successful B2 structure confirmation after synthesis, including XRD/SEM and TEM evidence for long-range B2 ordering in tested alloys.

title: Deep-learning denoising reveals new short-period seismic observations of known ultra-low-velocity zones
summary: A supervised deep-learning denoising autoencoder exposed previously undocumented short-period S-diffracted wave observations associated with several known ultra-low-velocity zones (ULVZs). It also revealed four Hawaiian-ULVZ S-diff post-cursor records at Japan F-net stations from East Pacific Rise earthquakes, providing ray paths with mean azimuth about 78° from earlier North American paths. These new cross-cutting observations add constraints on ULVZ geometry and frequency/azimuth-dependent waveforms, but the paper does not present a new ULVZ detection or a completed structural inversion.
ai_technology: Supervised deep-learning denoising autoencoder (DeepSeisDAE)
organization: University of Münster; James Cook University; Utrecht University; Australian National University; Geological Survey of Denmark and Greenland

evidence.tested: A supervised deep-learning denoising autoencoder exposed previously undocumented short-period S-diffracted wave observations associated with several known ultra-low-velocity zones (ULVZs).
evidence.unknown: This paper reports new seismic observations sampling known ULVZs; it does not establish a new ULVZ structure. The Japanese post-cursors are difficult to separate from the main S-diff phases and require future 3D modelling to determine their interpretation and resolve trade-offs. Denoiser amplitude fidelity is a limitation, especially under training/application mismatch; the authors advise caution for single-station denoising. These are observational constraints, not a completed inversion of shape or composition.
evidence.ai_role: The denoiser was trained on synthetic seismic waveforms mixed with real global noise, then used to separate signal from noise in real S-diff record sections. Its output helped researchers identify short-period post-cursor observations not reported in earlier literature, including four events recorded in Japan with nearly perpendicular ray geometry to previous North American observations of the Hawaiian ULVZ.

title: AI-guided experiments uncover new zeolitic imidazolate framework crystals
summary: AIRES combined probabilistic machine-learning predictions with robotic synthesis, optical crystal screening and single-crystal X-ray diffraction to explore zinc zeolitic imidazolate frameworks. The campaign crystallized new structures using 10 of 48 previously untested linkers, doubling the discovery rate of random exploration (700 versus 1,400 experiments) and increasing the single-linker Zn-ZIF library by about one-third. The paper reports structure-resolved products, including eleven previously unreported crystals across its discovery campaign.
ai_technology: Algorithmic Iterative Reticular Synthesis (AIRES)
organization: University of California, Berkeley; Monash University; VinUniversity; University of Haifa; Humboldt University of Berlin

evidence.tested: AIRES combined probabilistic machine-learning predictions with robotic synthesis, optical crystal screening and single-crystal X-ray diffraction to explore zinc zeolitic imidazolate frameworks.
evidence.unknown: This is one paper-level experimental discovery campaign. The reported efficiency comparison is against a random-exploration baseline within the study, not an independent replication. Structures were identified by single-crystal X-ray diffraction; the paper describes discovery of ZIF crystals but does not establish application performance. The campaign covered a defined single-linker Zn-ZIF chemical and reaction space, not all reticular materials.
evidence.ai_role: AIRES used probabilistic random-forest and Gaussian-process crystallization models to guide experiment selection across linker chemistries and reaction conditions. Its greedy and batch decision rules prioritized experiments predicted to yield distinct new crystals; automated synthesis, computer-vision crystal screening and subsequent single-crystal X-ray diffraction supplied experimental outcomes for model updates and structure determination. The AI-guided campaign found structures for 10 of 48 new linkers, with twice the distinct-crystal discovery rate of random exploration.

title: LLM-guided alloy design yields self-limiting oxidation behavior at 900 °C
summary: A knowledge-enhanced AI workflow led to Co22Cr24Fe20Ni25Mo5Mn4, a non-equiatomic high-entropy alloy with experimentally observed single-phase FCC structure and self-limiting oxidation kinetics at 900 °C. After about 50 hours, the study reports a steady-state oxidation-rate constant of 1.41 × 10⁻⁸ mgⁿ cm⁻²ⁿ h⁻¹ (reaction order n = 45.35) and a Cr₂O₃/(Mn,Fe)Cr₂O₄ bilayer oxide scale. The proposed barrier–buffer explanation is the authors’ mechanistic interpretation.
ai_technology: Physics-guided ML phase classifiers and LLM-assisted alloy-design workflow
organization: Shanghai University

evidence.tested: A knowledge-enhanced AI workflow led to Co22Cr24Fe20Ni25Mo5Mn4, a non-equiatomic high-entropy alloy with experimentally observed single-phase FCC structure and self-limiting oxidation kinetics at 900 °C.
evidence.unknown: The specific oxidation result is experimentally measured for one designed alloy under the paper’s 900 °C test conditions and time interval; it is not evidence of service lifetime or performance in a component. The bilayer-oxide barrier–buffer mechanism is the authors’ interpretation from characterization and kinetic behavior. The two additional non-equiatomic FCC/BCC alloys in the study validate phase predictions and remain bundled with the principal material result. The LLM reasoning-agent model is not identified clearly in the paper; DeepSeek-R1-671B is explicitly named for processing-text parsing.
evidence.ai_role: The authors used random-forest and support-vector classifiers trained on physics-based descriptors to prioritize single-phase alloy compositions. DeepSeek-R1-671B parsed literature processing descriptions into structured features. Separately, their LLM-agent workflow synthesized oxidation literature and mechanism knowledge to propose composition changes, including increasing Cr and adding about 4 at.% Mn; this guided selection of Co22Cr24Fe20Ni25Mo5Mn4 for synthesis and oxidation experiments. The paper does not clearly identify the model used for the reasoning-agent stage, so that identity is left unspecified.

title: First observation of single-top-quark production with a W and Z boson at CMS
summary: CMS reports the first observation of single-top-quark production in association with a W and Z boson in proton-proton collisions. A Particle Transformer classifier and improved reconstruction separated the rare tWZ signal from major backgrounds in three- and four-lepton events. Combining 13 and 13.6 TeV data (200 fb⁻¹), the measured signal has 5.8σ observed significance (3.5σ expected) and cross sections of 248 ± 52 fb at 13 TeV and 242 ± 77 fb at 13.6 TeV. The result agrees with the Standard Model within 2.3σ.
ai_technology: Particle Transformer (ParT) multiclass classifier
organization: CMS Collaboration; CERN Large Hadron Collider

evidence.tested: CMS reports the first observation of single-top-quark production in association with a W and Z boson in proton-proton collisions.
evidence.unknown: This is the first observation of the Standard-Model tWZ production process, not evidence for physics beyond the Standard Model. A 2024 CMS analysis had reported earlier evidence at 3.4σ; the 2026 paper adds 13.6 TeV Run 3 data and improved reconstruction/ML analysis to reach observation. The 5.8σ result combines 13 and 13.6 TeV datasets. Cross sections and signal strength are consistent with the Standard Model within the reported uncertainties.
evidence.ai_role: CMS trained four ParT models, split by three- versus four-lepton signal region and 13 versus 13.6 TeV samples. In the three-lepton region, a four-node classifier distinguished tWZ, ttZ and other backgrounds; in the four-lepton region, a binary classifier separated tWZ from backgrounds. Its classifier-score categories entered the statistical signal extraction. The paper reports a substantial sensitivity gain versus the previous analysis: expected significance on the reused 13 TeV data rose from 1.4σ to 3.0σ, contributing to the first observation when combined with 13.6 TeV data.

title: OmniFold enables an unbinned 24-dimensional Z+jets cross-section measurement by ATLAS
summary: Using 139 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton-proton data, ATLAS simultaneously unfolded 24 correlated Z+jets kinematic observables with the machine-learning method OmniFold and released the particle-level result as an unbinned event dataset. The measured total fiducial cross section is 1,808 ± 42 fb; most illustrative differential bins have 3–5% total uncertainty, rising to about 15% in tails. The measurement is more precise than the compared predictions for many distributions, especially Sherpa. The event-level release also supports derived observables, including an infrared-and-collinear-safe τ₂₁ measurement in a specified fiducial region.
ai_technology: OmniFold iterative machine-learning unfolding
organization: ATLAS Collaboration; CERN Large Hadron Collider

evidence.tested: Using 139 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton-proton data, ATLAS simultaneously unfolded 24 correlated Z+jets kinematic observables with the machine-learning method OmniFold and released the particle-level result as an unbinned event dataset.
evidence.unknown: This is a new high-dimensional precision measurement of known Z+jets production, not a new particle or beyond-Standard-Model discovery. The released measurement is unbinned in 24 measured variables; displayed plots may be binned for presentation. The authors report mostly 3–5% uncertainties in illustrative bins, up to about 15% in tails, with dominant unfolding-prior/hidden-variable uncertainties for some observables. Pseudo-data closure is generally good, with exceptions including a p-value of 0.038 for leading-jet transverse momentum; users are given phase-space and covariance-use guidance.
evidence.ai_role: OmniFold used neural-network classifiers to iteratively reweight simulated events so the detector-level simulation matched collision data, then propagated the learned correction to particle-level events. That multivariate unfolding handled 24 correlated observables simultaneously and produced event weights with uncertainty variations, enabling a high-dimensional unbinned measurement and event-level construction of additional derived observables. The paper validates closure on pseudo-data and reports its uncertainty components.

title: Deep learning expands the Utah FORGE DAS microearthquake catalog and resolves stimulation structure
summary: A ResNet-based DASEventNet model applied to continuous distributed acoustic sensing from the April 2022 Utah FORGE Well 16A (78)-32 stimulation manually verified 5,749 microearthquakes absent from the Silixa STA/LTA catalog; 45 of 5,794 model-positive windows were false detections on manual review. The study reports events down to Mw −1.80 versus −1.14 for STA/LTA and a broader Stage 3 seismicity distribution consistent with fracture geometry seen in an independent deep-borehole geophone catalog. This is a local event-catalog and stimulation-geometry result, not a direct DAS-based event-location measurement.
ai_technology: DASEventNet (ResNet-50 convolutional neural network)
organization: Pennsylvania State University; Utah FORGE

evidence.tested: A ResNet-based DASEventNet model applied to continuous distributed acoustic sensing from the April 2022 Utah FORGE Well 16A (78)-32 stimulation manually verified 5,749 microearthquakes absent from the Silixa STA/LTA catalog; 45 of 5,794 model-positive windows were false detections on manual review.
evidence.unknown: Original JGR: Solid Earth paper reports manual review of model-positive events and comparison with conventional Silixa detections. Model predicts event presence but does not estimate event locations or magnitudes from DAS alone; timing association and location/magnitude comparison use an independent deep-borehole geophone catalog with an assumed 0.2 s matching window. Fiber placement limits direct geometry inference. Detection of cataloged events is not independent proof of every physical interpretation.
evidence.ai_role: Trained on manually checked DAS event and noise windows, the network detected weak microearthquake waveforms in continuous seven-day DAS recordings. It expanded the catalog and enabled a denser spatiotemporal characterization of the hydraulic stimulation seismicity.

title: XRD-guided learning identifies Li₆AsSe₅I as a room-temperature superionic conductor
summary: XRDMatch, a semi-supervised model using X-ray diffraction patterns as its descriptor, screened unlabeled crystal data and identified 38 lithium superionic-conductor predictions. The paper says 32 were supported by prior literature, six were new candidates assessed with ab initio molecular dynamics, and Li₆AsSe₅I was synthesized and experimentally confirmed as a superionic conductor. The source abstract does not establish that all 38 are new or experimentally validated; this record covers the single reported synthesized material.
ai_technology: XRDMatch semi-supervised learning framework
organization: East China Normal University; Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Westlake University; Microsoft Research Asia; collaborators

evidence.tested: XRDMatch, a semi-supervised model using X-ray diffraction patterns as its descriptor, screened unlabeled crystal data and identified 38 lithium superionic-conductor predictions.
evidence.unknown: The publisher abstract says six newly predicted candidates were quantified with ab initio molecular dynamics, but names only Li₆AsSe₅I as synthesized and experimentally confirmed. It reports 32 additional predictions matched recent literature. The full publisher article was inaccessible during the source review (HTTP 403); the annotation is limited to the primary publisher abstract and its article metadata.
evidence.ai_role: Consistency regularization and pseudo-labeling let the model learn from limited labeled conductivity data and unlabeled ICSD X-ray diffraction patterns. It nominated Li₆AsSe₅I for synthesis, where the researchers experimentally confirmed superionic conductivity.

title: PhaseNet-TF expands Tonga earthquake catalog and resolves the intermediate-depth double seismic zone
summary: A semi-supervised PhaseNet-TF workflow detected and relocated 13,616 events from a one-year Tonga OBS and land-station record, about 11 times the manually picked reference catalog. The denser catalog delineates the intermediate-depth double seismic zone to about 300 km and indicates that its lower plane is limited to roughly 19°–21°S, rather than continuous along the studied section. The study did not recover a deeper 350–460 km double zone; sparse events and location uncertainties limit inference at those depths.
ai_technology: PhaseNet-TF deep-learning phase picker with semi-supervised iterative retraining
organization: Michigan State University; Stanford University; University of California, Berkeley

evidence.tested: A semi-supervised PhaseNet-TF workflow detected and relocated 13,616 events from a one-year Tonga OBS and land-station record, about 11 times the manually picked reference catalog.
evidence.unknown: The catalog is based on one year of OBS and land data.
