About half of events are outside the array and have larger hypocenter uncertainty from azimuthal gaps; velocity-model choice adds absolute-location uncertainty. The authors say the absent 350–460 km double zone may reflect insufficient events, not definitive absence. Stress and hydration explanations are interpretations, and some rare events above the slab may be false.
evidence.ai_role: The time-frequency neural picker detected P/S arrivals in noisy ocean-bottom seismometer data; iterative semi-supervised retraining expanded picks, while phase association and double-difference relocation filtered unreliable events. This expanded catalog enabled the localized double-seismic-zone inference.

title: LHCb observes the doubly charmed Ωcc⁺ baryon with an 8.7σ global significance
summary: Using 6.3 fb⁻¹ of 13.6 TeV proton-proton collisions recorded in 2024, LHCb observed an Ωc⁰π⁺ mass peak with 8.7σ global significance and identified it as the weakly decaying doubly charmed Ωcc⁺ baryon. The reported mass is 3725.9 ± 1.0 (stat) ± 0.2 (syst) ± 0.4 (lifetime) ± 0.6 (external) MeV/c². A boosted decision tree suppressed random-track combinatorial background; the result is a preprint submitted to Physical Review Letters.
ai_technology: Boosted decision tree classifier (TMVA toolkit)
organization: LHCb Collaboration; CERN

evidence.tested: Using 6.3 fb⁻¹ of 13.6 TeV proton-proton collisions recorded in 2024, LHCb observed an Ωc⁰π⁺ mass peak with 8.7σ global significance and identified it as the weakly decaying doubly charmed Ωcc⁺ baryon.
evidence.unknown: The source is an LHCb collaboration preprint submitted to PRL, not yet a peer-reviewed journal publication as of its arXiv version. The observed peak has 8.7σ global significance; the mass uncertainty includes an explicit lifetime-dependent selection-bias term because the Ωcc⁺ lifetime is unknown. BDT use is an analysis component, not the sole basis of the observation.
evidence.ai_role: The BDT was trained on simulated Ωcc⁺ signal decays and wrong-charge Ωc⁰π⁻ combinations from data and used to suppress the dominant random-track combinatorial background in the offline candidate selection. The background rejection supported the mass-spectrum analysis yielding the first observation.

title: LHCb observes CP violation for the first time in baryon decays
summary: Using 9 fb⁻¹ of LHCb Run 1 and Run 2 data, the collaboration measured a phase-space-averaged CP asymmetry of (2.45 ± 0.46 ± 0.10)% in Λb⁰ → pK⁻π⁺π⁻ and its conjugate, a 5.2σ observation. In the resonance-dominated R(pπ⁺π⁻)K⁻ region, the asymmetry was (5.4 ± 0.9 ± 0.1)%, 6.0σ from zero. Machine-learning BDT selection suppressed combinatorial background; neural-network PID variables mitigated particle misidentification.
ai_technology: Boosted decision tree event classifier; neural-network particle-identification variables
organization: LHCb Collaboration; CERN

evidence.tested: Using 9 fb⁻¹ of LHCb Run 1 and Run 2 data, the collaboration measured a phase-space-averaged CP asymmetry of (2.45 ± 0.46 ± 0.10)% in Λb⁰ → pK⁻π⁺π⁻ and its conjugate, a 5.2σ observation.
evidence.unknown: This is the first reported baryon-decay CP-violation observation, with significance 5.2σ for the phase-space-integrated result and 6.0σ in the specified resonance region. Reported asymmetries average over phase space; the paper says a full amplitude-structure investigation remains future work. Small asymmetries may cancel across angular-momentum amplitudes. The measured CP asymmetry is distinct from raw yield asymmetry; production/detection nuisance asymmetries are subtracted using a control channel.
evidence.ai_role: The BDT used decay topology, displacement and kinematics to suppress random combinations in the four-track signal selection. Neural-network PID variables helped mitigate misidentified final-state particle backgrounds. These tools supported signal purity for the baryon–antibaryon asymmetry measurement.

title: Dense-array seismicity analysis infers a buried fault beneath the Three Gorges Reservoir area
summary: A two-phase dense-array catalog processed with the LOC-FLOW machine-learning workflow revealed microseismicity in three zones and shallow (0–6 km) and deep (6–15 km) layers near the northern Xiannvshan Fault Zone. A steeply dipping seismic band is interpreted as a previously hidden western extension of the Tianyangping Fault; the authors also propose fluid-permeable connections between depth layers. The enhanced catalog detects over an order of magnitude more events than the regional network catalog for the same period.
ai_technology: LOC-FLOW machine-learning seismic catalog workflow
organization: Wuhan University of Technology; Institute of Seismology, China Earthquake Administration; collaborators

evidence.tested: A two-phase dense-array catalog processed with the LOC-FLOW machine-learning workflow revealed microseismicity in three zones and shallow (0–6 km) and deep (6–15 km) layers near the northern Xiannvshan Fault Zone.
evidence.unknown: Verified from the original publisher abstract and publication metadata; full text was inaccessible in this review. The steep band is interpreted as an inferred buried fault, not independently imaged or proven fault geometry. The proposed fluid-permeable connection and dual-mechanism reservoir-modulated seismicity are hypotheses. The catalog increase reflects a dense temporary array plus machine-learning workflow, compared with the regional network catalog.
evidence.ai_role: The study used LOC-FLOW with dense-array observations to detect, locate and relocate microearthquakes for a higher-resolution catalog. The catalog made the three activity zones, depth layers and steep seismic band visible for the authors’ structural interpretation.

title: CMS makes the first hadron-collider observation of boosted Z→cc̄ decay
summary: In 138 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton-proton data, CMS observed boosted Z→cc̄ production in association with jets for the first time at a hadron collider. The measured signal strength relative to the Standard Model prediction is 1.00 with combined uncertainty +0.19/−0.17. A deep neural network (DeepDoubleX) identified large-radius jets from charm-quark pairs; the paper also sets a 95% confidence-level upper limit of 47 times the Standard Model prediction on boosted H→cc̄ production.
ai_technology: DeepDoubleX deep neural network for double-charm jet tagging
organization: CMS Collaboration; CERN

evidence.tested: In 138 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton-proton data, CMS observed boosted Z→cc̄ production in association with jets for the first time at a hadron collider.
evidence.unknown: The first-observation claim is specifically for Z→cc̄ in association with jets at high transverse momentum at a hadron collider; it is not the first observation of Z decay generally. The neural tagger is an important analysis tool, while the observation derives from the full CMS event selection and likelihood fit. In the same paper, boosted H→cc̄ was not observed; only an upper limit is reported.
evidence.ai_role: The neural network processed secondary-vertex and particle-flow candidate features to classify boosted two-prong jets as charm versus light flavor and charm versus bottom. Its charm tagging separated the Z→cc̄ signal from dominant multijet backgrounds and supported the first observation in the boosted high-transverse-momentum regime.

title: t-SNE-selected LMC radio source receives a spectroscopic AGN classification at z = 2.80
summary: SALT spectroscopy of the previously unclassified source LMC tSNE b8 (R.A. 06:22:41.86, Dec. −68:59:21.9) identified it as an active galactic nucleus at redshift z = 2.80. The source was selected from the blazar-like sequence in a t-SNE map combining VISTA near-infrared and ASKAP radio survey data with multi-wavelength photometry. This is one specific spectroscopic classification from the paper’s broader follow-up sample.
ai_technology: t-distributed stochastic neighbour embedding (t-SNE) applied to multi-wavelength source photometry
organization: Keele University; Southern African Large Telescope collaboration; collaborators

evidence.tested: SALT spectroscopy of the previously unclassified source LMC tSNE b8 (R.A.
evidence.unknown: This is an arXiv preprint. The selected source was classified as an AGN at z=2.80 from SALT spectroscopy, but the paper’s broader 18-target blazar-sequence follow-up also contains Magellanic objects and two low-S/N unconfirmed sources; those are not counted as confirmed discoveries. The claim here is limited to LMC tSNE b8. The paper calls the selection sequence blazar-like; that label does not establish this specific source as a blazar.
evidence.ai_role: t-SNE mapped 6,652 Large Magellanic Cloud and 1,356 Small Magellanic Cloud sources using optical-to-radio features. The unsupervised map exposed a blazar-like sequence from which LMC tSNE b8 was selected for SALT follow-up; spectroscopy then established its AGN classification and redshift.

title: LHCb makes the first high-significance observation of the rare Σ⁺ → pμ⁺μ⁻ decay
summary: Using 5.4 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton-proton collision data collected in 2016–2018, LHCb observed 237 ± 16 Σ⁺ → pμ⁺μ⁻ decays and measured a branching fraction of (1.08 ± 0.17) × 10⁻⁸. The dimuon spectrum showed no evidence of resonant structures, and the results are compatible with Standard Model expectations. This is the first high-significance observation; earlier HyperCP and LHCb Run 1 results were evidence only.
ai_technology: LHCb boosted decision tree (BDT) classifier
organization: LHCb Collaboration; CERN

evidence.tested: Using 5.4 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton-proton collision data collected in 2016–2018, LHCb observed 237 ± 16 Σ⁺ → pμ⁺μ⁻ decays and measured a branching fraction of (1.08 ± 0.17) × 10⁻⁸.
evidence.unknown: The paper reports an observation of the nonresonant rare decay, not evidence for the hypothetical intermediate X⁰ suggested by the earlier HyperCP candidates; no resonant dimuon structure is found. The measured branching fraction is compatible with Standard Model expectations. AI supported event selection and background reduction but is not the sole basis of the result.
evidence.ai_role: The BDT combined kinematic and geometric variables, trained on simulated signal and data sidebands representing combinatorial background, and was used in the final candidate selection. Its output threshold was optimized together with particle-identification and Λ-veto criteria to maximize expected significance. This classifier contributed to background suppression; it was one component of the analysis, alongside upgraded trigger selections, detector reconstruction, and the statistical fit.

title: Spectroscopy validates machine-selected populations of obscured active galaxies
summary: Using a sample selected by unsupervised machine learning on optical and mid-infrared photometry, the team obtained 178 MMT spectra and found the brighter class was 85% Type I active galactic nuclei (AGN), with <3% non-AGN contamination, while a fainter class was 65% Type II AGN with 15% contamination, mainly star-forming galaxies. The follow-up showed that the machine-selected classes recover redder and more obscured AGN populations than typical optical spectroscopic samples.
ai_technology: Unsupervised UMAP and DBSCAN photometric AGN selection pipeline
organization: University of Arizona; Princeton University; MMT Observatory

evidence.tested: Using a sample selected by unsupervised machine learning on optical and mid-infrared photometry, the team obtained 178 MMT spectra and found the brighter class was 85% Type I active galactic nuclei (AGN), with <3% non-AGN contamination, while a fainter class was 65% Type II AGN with 15% contamination, mainly star-forming galaxies.
evidence.unknown: This is a follow-up validation of two machine-selected candidate classes, not a claim that every cataloged object is confirmed. Spectroscopy recovered redshifts for 139 of 178 spectra; the fainter Type II class was limited to the brightest 75% of candidates and had 15% contamination, primarily from star-forming galaxies. The unsupervised pipeline is described in related work listed as in preparation in this paper; findings here are bounded to the spectroscopically analyzed sample.
evidence.ai_role: The selection pipeline applied UMAP dimensionality reduction and DBSCAN clustering to optical and mid-infrared colors and morphology, with matched spectroscopy and X-ray information used to identify AGN candidate classes. Those classes defined the targets for Hectospec follow-up; the paper then used optical spectra, emission-line diagnostics, and spectral stacking to test their AGN content. The AI selected the candidate populations, while spectroscopic diagnostics established the reported classifications.

title: PhaseNet catalog reveals a 2023 injection-linked earthquake cluster in the Raton Basin
summary: Applying PhaseNet-based phase picking to eight years of recordings from eight broadband stations, the study built a roughly 96,000-event Raton Basin catalog (local magnitudes −1 to 4.3) and resolved a previously unreported 2023 cluster with a Mw 4.3 event. Nearby wells had elevated injection volumes for about a year before the cluster; analysis of relocated events and 90 full centroid moment tensors also supports basement-rooted normal faults and possible elevated pore pressure. The authors interpret injection as a likely influence, not a demonstrated sole cause.
ai_technology: PhaseNet deep neural-network seismic phase picker in the LOC-FLOW workflow
organization: Southern University of Science and Technology; University of New Mexico; U.S. Geological Survey

evidence.tested: Applying PhaseNet-based phase picking to eight years of recordings from eight broadband stations, the study built a roughly 96,000-event Raton Basin catalog (local magnitudes −1 to 4.3) and resolved a previously unreported 2023 cluster with a Mw 4.3 event.
evidence.unknown: The authors report an association between nearby injection and seismicity and infer elevated pore pressure from positive isotropic components; this does not establish injection as the sole cause. They note possible residual isotropic-component artifacts from velocity heterogeneity or noise and explicitly limit interpretation of CLVD components. The paper gives slightly inconsistent catalog totals: 95,993 in the abstract and most text, but 95,933 in one discussion passage; this summary therefore says roughly 96,000. The newly resolved cluster is distinct from earlier Raton Basin seismicity studies cited by the authors.
evidence.ai_role: PhaseNet picked P and S arrivals directly from continuous waveforms at eight broadband stations, including four stations not telemetered for routine cataloging. These picks enabled event association, relocation, and the expanded 2016–2024 catalog used to identify and analyze the 2023 cluster. PhaseNet enabled the denser earthquake observations; the injection comparison and full-CMT mechanism analysis were subsequent statistical and geophysical analyses.

title: Graph neural network enables first observation of Λc⁺ → ne⁺νe decay
summary: Using 4.5 fb⁻¹ of BESIII electron–positron collision data, the collaboration reports the first observation of the Cabibbo-suppressed Λc⁺ → ne⁺νe decay at greater than 10σ significance. It measures a branching fraction of (3.57 ± 0.34(stat) ± 0.14(syst)) × 10⁻³ and extracts |Vcd| = 0.208 ± 0.011(exp) ± 0.007(LQCD) ± 0.001(lifetime) for the first time from a charmed-baryon decay.
ai_technology: Graph neural network (GNN) trained on BESIII electromagnetic-calorimeter shower patterns
organization: BESIII Collaboration

evidence.tested: Using 4.5 fb⁻¹ of BESIII electron–positron collision data, the collaboration reports the first observation of the Cabibbo-suppressed Λc⁺ → ne⁺νe decay at greater than 10σ significance.
evidence.unknown: The observation is an experimental result from the BESIII data sample; the branching-fraction and |Vcd| uncertainties include statistical, systematic, lattice-QCD and lifetime components as reported. The paper studies data-versus-simulation domain shift and network uncertainty; residual modeling differences contribute to systematic uncertainty. The |Vcd| extraction depends on lattice-QCD input.
evidence.ai_role: The GNN separated neutron signal showers from the dominant Λc⁺ → Λe⁺νe background, whose neutron-plus-π⁰ calorimeter patterns are difficult to distinguish with conventional selection or boosted trees. The authors trained and calibrated it using large J/ψ control samples, then fitted its output distributions to extract the signal yield.

title: Machine-learning earthquake catalog reveals scale-dependent fault controls at Gonghe geothermal site
summary: A machine-learning workflow catalogued 7,346 microearthquakes (ML −2.0 to 2.18) recorded during 2021 stimulation and circulation tests at China’s Gonghe enhanced-geothermal-system site. The catalog resolves a ring-shaped distribution with four clusters and varying faulting styles. The authors infer that site-scale seismicity reactivated mapped, pre-existing natural faults; at borehole scale, the principal seismogenic zone coincides with strong SHmax rotation. Stress modeling estimates a low fault-friction coefficient near 0.23 (95% CI 0.19–0.48) and the low-to-moderate fluid overpressure needed for slip.
ai_technology: Machine-learning earthquake-detection and cataloging workflow (model details are not stated in the publisher abstract)
organization: Southern University of Science and Technology; Institute of Geomechanics, Chinese Academy of Geological Sciences; ETH Zürich

evidence.tested: A machine-learning workflow catalogued 7,346 microearthquakes (ML −2.0 to 2.18) recorded during 2021 stimulation and circulation tests at China’s Gonghe enhanced-geothermal-system site.
evidence.unknown: The source checked here is the original publisher abstract and plain-language summary. The catalog is observed, while fault reactivation, chlorite-rich gouge consistency, stress controls and required fluid overpressure are the authors’ interpretations/model estimates, not direct causal proof. No claim is made that the AI model alone establishes these mechanisms.
evidence.ai_role: The authors state that machine learning was used to detect earthquakes and compile the high-precision 7,346-event catalog; the resolved spatial pattern supplies the seismicity observations used in their scale-dependent fault-structure interpretation and stress analysis.

title: ParticleNet enables first hadron-collider W-boson mass measurement from hadronic decays
summary: Using 138 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton–proton data, CMS reports the first measurement of the W-boson mass in an all-jets final state at a hadron collider: 80.83 ± 0.55 GeV. The result comes from unfolded groomed jet-mass distributions for boosted hadronic W+jets events. The mass-decorrelated ParticleNet graph neural network tagger provides the main result by selecting the W-jet sample and suppressing quark/gluon multijet background; a non-neural N₂ tagger is used as a cross-check.
ai_technology: ParticleNet mass-decorrelated graph neural network jet tagger
organization: CMS Collaboration

evidence.tested: Using 138 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton–proton data, CMS reports the first measurement of the W-boson mass in an all-jets final state at a hadron collider: 80.83 ± 0.55 GeV.
evidence.unknown: This is an all-jets boosted-W extraction with 0.55 GeV total uncertainty, much less precise than the CMS leptonic-channel W-mass result; the paper frames it as a first step toward future all-jets precision measurements and as a test of jet-substructure modeling. The earlier preliminary CMS result of 80.77 ± 0.57 GeV was superseded by this same paper’s published 80.83 ± 0.55 GeV result and is not counted separately. Jet tagging, QCD background estimation, unfolding, hadronization and jet-energy modeling contribute analysis dependence and uncertainties.
evidence.ai_role: The analysis uses ParticleNet as its main W-jet tagger. Its graph neural network treats jet constituents as an unordered particle cloud and classifies W→qq′ jets against QCD multijet backgrounds; its mass-decorrelated output defines the signal/control regions used for the primary measurement. The N₂ substructure observable is a separate cross-check.

title: ATLAS graph neural network enables first observation of four-top-quark production
summary: Using 140 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton–proton collisions, ATLAS observed simultaneous production of four top quarks in same-sign dilepton and multilepton events, with 6.1σ observed (4.3σ expected) significance. The measured cross-section is 22.5⁺⁶·⁶₋₅·₅ fb, consistent with the Standard Model prediction within 1.8σ. A graph neural network separated the four-top signal from dominant backgrounds in the signal extraction.
ai_technology: Event-level graph neural network built with graph_nets/TensorFlow
organization: ATLAS Collaboration; CERN

evidence.tested: Using 140 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton–proton collisions, ATLAS observed simultaneous production of four top quarks in same-sign dilepton and multilepton events, with 6.1σ observed (4.3σ expected) significance.
evidence.unknown: This is an ATLAS observation from its own 140 fb⁻¹ analysis after earlier ATLAS/CMS evidence; it is one paper-level observation, not a separate count for CMS or later combinations. The measured cross-section uncertainty is large and its central value is 1.8σ above the SM prediction, so this is not evidence of a significant deviation from the Standard Model. Background control regions and systematic uncertainties are part of the analysis.
evidence.ai_role: The GNN discriminant classified events using a fully connected graph of reconstructed jets, leptons and missing transverse momentum, with node, edge and global features. It separated four-top signal from background and supplied the discriminant used in the signal extraction and cross-section fit.

title: ATLAS boosted decision trees enable first observation of triple-W boson production
summary: In 139 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV LHC data, ATLAS observed simultaneous WWW production at 8.0σ (5.4σ expected) and measured an inclusive cross-section of 820 ± 100(stat) ± 80(syst) fb. The analysis selected same-sign dilepton-plus-jets and trilepton final states. Two boosted decision trees—one per channel—improved signal/background separation and supplied distributions for the fit. The measured rate is about 2.6σ above the Standard Model prediction, not a significant discrepancy.
ai_technology: Two boosted decision tree classifiers for the dilepton and trilepton channels
organization: ATLAS Collaboration; CERN

evidence.tested: In 139 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV LHC data, ATLAS observed simultaneous WWW production at 8.0σ (5.4σ expected) and measured an inclusive cross-section of 820 ± 100(stat) ± 80(syst) fb.
evidence.unknown: The final peer-reviewed paper reports 8.0σ (5.4σ expected), superseding the earlier 2021 conference-note/press account that quoted 8.2σ and 850 fb. CMS had previously observed combined inclusive production of three massive gauge bosons; this ATLAS paper is the first observation specifically of WWW production. The measured cross-section is about 2.6σ above the theory prediction, below a significant deviation, with data-driven background and systematic uncertainties included.
evidence.ai_role: The BDTs were trained separately for the two- and three-lepton channels, using 12 and 11 well-modelled event variables respectively, to discriminate WWW signal from background. Their output distributions entered the likelihood fit; the paper says the improved separation helped enable the observation.

title: Deep-learning lens search leads to first confirmed galaxy-scale lensed superluminous supernova
summary: The HOLISMOKES search identified the ZTF transient SN 2025wny at the position of the previously selected lens candidate PS1 J0716+3821. Follow-up imaging resolved multiple supernova images and spectroscopy classified it as a Type I superluminous supernova at z=2.008 ± 0.001; the second deflector galaxy was measured spectroscopically at z=0.375 ± 0.001. This is the first confirmed galaxy-scale strongly lensed supernova with expected time delays of days to weeks, offering a new system for time-delay cosmography.
ai_technology: Deep-learning Pan-STARRS 3π lens-candidate classification and transient-alert cross-matching pipeline
organization: Technical University of Munich; Max Planck Institute for Astrophysics; Technical University of Denmark; HOLISMOKES Collaboration

evidence.tested: The HOLISMOKES search identified the ZTF transient SN 2025wny at the position of the previously selected lens candidate PS1 J0716+3821.
evidence.unknown: The redshift, SN type and lensing are based on follow-up observations; time delays are predicted from image separations and were still awaiting high-cadence measurement in this paper. The authors note that the SN’s brightness and resolvability introduce selection effects. An independent paper analyzed the same transient; the discovery is counted once here, not as separate detections by each follow-up team.
evidence.ai_role: The discovery followed a workflow that first classified all 3 billion Pan-STARRS 3π sources with deep learning to select high-quality strong-lens candidates, then continuously cross-matched those positions to ZTF alerts. The team matched the 2025 transient to the preselected lens candidate and triggered imaging and spectroscopic follow-up, which established the lensed SLSN result.

title: ATLAS graph neural network enables first LHC observation of single-top s-channel production
summary: Using 140 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton–proton collisions, ATLAS reports the first observation of single-top-quark s-channel production at the LHC, with 5.1σ observed (5.2σ expected) significance. The measured cross-section is 10.8 ± 1.5(stat) ± 1.6(syst) pb, consistent with the Standard Model. A graph neural network discriminant separates the signal from top-pair, W+jets and t-channel single-top backgrounds; the analysis also uses broadened event acceptance, improved b tagging and refined modeling.
ai_technology: Event-level graph neural network; ATLAS GN2 graph-transformer b-jet tagger
organization: ATLAS Collaboration; CERN

evidence.tested: Using 140 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton–proton collisions, ATLAS reports the first observation of single-top-quark s-channel production at the LHC, with 5.1σ observed (5.2σ expected) significance.
evidence.unknown: This is an ATLAS preprint submitted to PRL as of the checked date; prior ATLAS analyses had reported evidence, and the Tevatron had already observed the process in a combined CDF+DØ result. The new claim is first observation at the LHC and by one experiment. The cross-section has about 20% total uncertainty and agrees with the Standard Model; the network is one of several improvements contributing to sensitivity, not the sole cause.
evidence.ai_role: The GNN uses event kinematics to distinguish s-channel signal from major backgrounds, with its score distribution used in the likelihood fit. GN2 improves b-jet identification; the paper attributes increased sensitivity jointly to the GNN, broader acceptance, improved b tagging, calibrations and theory modeling.

title: Boosted decision tree enables first observation of two simultaneously longitudinally polarized Z bosons
summary: Using 164 fb⁻¹ of 13.6 TeV proton–proton data and a statistical combination with the Run 2 measurement, ATLAS reports the first observation of ZZ production with both Z bosons longitudinally polarized, at 6.5σ observed (5.6σ expected). The combined signal strength is 1.22 ± 0.21; the Run 3 measurement also reports polarization fractions across the fiducial phase space and two four-lepton invariant-mass ranges, consistent with Standard Model predictions.
ai_technology: Boosted decision tree (BDT) classifier
organization: ATLAS Collaboration; CERN

evidence.tested: Using 164 fb⁻¹ of 13.6 TeV proton–proton data and a statistical combination with the Run 2 measurement, ATLAS reports the first observation of ZZ production with both Z bosons longitudinally polarized, at 6.5σ observed (5.6σ expected).
evidence.unknown: The ATLAS paper was submitted to PRL as a preprint on 2026-07-14; the cited official ATLAS briefing is dated 2026-08-04. The 6.5σ first observation combines the Run 3 analysis with the prior Run 2 measurement, whose standalone significance was 4.3σ. The Run 3 analysis alone reports 5.1σ. The measured fractions agree with the Standard Model; the statistical uncertainty dominates and polarization-template modeling is the leading systematic uncertainty. This is an experimental observation from ATLAS data, not evidence of physics beyond the Standard Model.
evidence.ai_role: The BDT is trained on polarization-sensitive lepton angular observables to separate longitudinal-longitudinal ZZ events from transverse or mixed-polarization events. Its score distribution is the fitted observable used to extract the signal strength and significance.

title: AI-built Baihetan reservoir catalog reveals fault-controlled and depth-dependent seismicity
summary: LOC-FLOW analysis of 55 stations and continuous waveforms from January 2021 to July 2022 identified 53,838 events around China’s Baihetan Reservoir, about four times the manual catalog, with reported relative location errors of tens of metres and recall of about 99% of manual events. The authors infer that post-impoundment seismicity is concentrated along regional structures and fractures, differs across the Jinsha River, and includes migration away from the inundation zone and with depth. They report depth-dependent b-value and water-depth/event-rate patterns consistent with different shallow and deep controls.
ai_technology: LOC-FLOW automated earthquake-detection and location workflow using PhaseNet deep-learning phase picking
organization: China Earthquake Administration; Institute of Geophysics; Institute of Earthquake Forecasting

evidence.tested: LOC-FLOW analysis of 55 stations and continuous waveforms from January 2021 to July 2022 identified 53,838 events around China’s Baihetan Reservoir, about four times the manual catalog, with reported relative location errors of tens of metres and recall of about 99% of manual events.
evidence.unknown: The catalog covers one reservoir and January 2021–July 2022. The reported location errors are relative errors, not absolute location accuracy. Spatial distribution and migration are observations from the catalog; proposed tectonic, lithologic, fluid-diffusion, poroelastic, water-load, and pore-pressure explanations are author interpretations and are not uniquely established by this study. The paper discusses the need to assess whether the larger automated catalog contains only genuine events. Summary claims are limited to the published abstract and article metadata checked here.
evidence.ai_role: The AI phase picker enabled automatic processing of continuous records from 55 stations into the high-resolution event catalog used for relocations and the spatiotemporal, depth, and b-value analyses. The authors report 53,838 detections, roughly four times the manual catalog, while recalling about 99% of the manual events.

title: Machine learning guided discovery of enhanced anomalous Hall resistivity in Fe–Ir–Pt films
summary: A machine-learning screen trained on experimental Fe–heavy-element binary alloys pointed to a ternary Fe–Ir–Pt composition range with enhanced anomalous Hall effect. High-throughput composition-spread measurements experimentally found a peak anomalous Hall resistivity of 6.5 μΩ·cm, above the prior 5.25 μΩ·cm maximum reported for Fe–X binary systems. Scaling analysis attributed the enhancement to an extrinsic contribution.
ai_technology: Gaussian process regression using Magpie composition descriptors
organization: National Institute for Materials Science (NIMS)

evidence.tested: A machine-learning screen trained on experimental Fe–heavy-element binary alloys pointed to a ternary Fe–Ir–Pt composition range with enhanced anomalous Hall effect.
evidence.unknown: This is a thin-film anomalous Hall resistivity result; the paper does not demonstrate a finished magnetic sensor or device. The machine-learning model overpredicted absolute values for the measured Fe–Ir–Pt compositions, although it qualitatively identified the enhancement and composition trend. The reported extrinsic origin comes from the paper’s scaling analysis. The result is limited to the measured composition-spread films and does not establish performance across bulk material forms or devices.
evidence.ai_role: The model was trained on measured Fe–X binary anomalous Hall data and screened 13,260 possible Fe-based ternary compositions for a larger effect. Its predicted Fe–Ir–Pt region guided experimental testing in composition-spread films; the machine-learning prediction and high-throughput measurement together identified the enhanced-effect composition range.

title: Bayesian optimization experimentally identifies a high-AHE Fe–Co–Ni–Ta–Ir amorphous film
summary: An autonomous closed-loop search combining composition-spread experiments with Bayesian optimization reached a maximum anomalous Hall resistivity of 10.9 μΩ·cm in an amorphous Fe44.9Co27.9Ni12.1Ta3.3Ir11.7 thin film deposited at room temperature. This measured value exceeded the study’s target of 10 μΩ·cm and the values found in the initial random-exploration cycles.
ai_technology: Bayesian optimization for composition-spread experiments
organization: National Institute for Materials Science (NIMS); University of Tokyo

evidence.tested: An autonomous closed-loop search combining composition-spread experiments with Bayesian optimization reached a maximum anomalous Hall resistivity of 10.9 μΩ·cm in an amorphous Fe44.9Co27.9Ni12.1Ta3.3Ir11.7 thin film deposited at room temperature.
evidence.unknown: The 10.9 μΩ·cm maximum is the best among 234 compositions explored over 18 cycles in this search, not a global proof of the maximum over all compositions. The demonstrated film is amorphous and was measured at room temperature on thermally oxidized silicon; the study does not report a completed sensor device or independent reproduction. Although the experimental decision loop was automated, human sample transfers between instruments remained.
evidence.ai_role: The method selects which five-element alloy composition-spread film to make next and which pair of elements to grade across it, using prior AHE measurements. The closed loop then executes deposition, multi-device fabrication and AHE measurement, feeding results into the next composition proposal; the Bayesian optimization was central to reaching the high-AHE Fe–Co–Ni–Ta–Ir composition.

title: AI-assisted work proves a Latin-square imbalance bound, with optimal examples through order 52
summary: A collaborative LLM-plus-symbolic-computation study proved that every n×n Latin square with n ≡ 1 (mod 3) has imbalance at least 4n(n−1)/9. It introduced near-perfect permutations that attain the bound and computationally found independently verified matching examples for every such order from 4 through 52. The universal lower-bound theorem was formally checked in Lean 4.
ai_technology: Claude Opus 4.5 LLM agent with SageMath, Rust exhaustive solver, simulated annealing and Lean 4 verification tools
organization: Cornell University; TU Wien

evidence.tested: A collaborative LLM-plus-symbolic-computation study proved that every n×n Latin square with n ≡ 1 (mod 3) has imbalance at least 4n(n−1)/9.
evidence.unknown: This is an arXiv preprint (v2 dated 2026-08-13), not yet peer-reviewed in the sources checked. The universal proven theorem is a lower bound for n ≡ 1 mod 3. Matching constructions, and hence demonstrated tightness, are computationally established only for n=4,7,…,52; the paper does not prove that the bound is attained for every larger order. Lean 4 formalizes the lower-bound inequality, not the finite construction search or universal tightness.
evidence.ai_role: The agent identified an all-even row-distance parity pattern in numerical search data, formulated and helped prove the lower bound, and used model review to catch proof errors. SageMath and a Rust solver supported symbolic analysis and enumeration; simulated annealing found matching constructions through n=52. Human strategic direction supplied the decisive pivot to the minimum-positive-imbalance question. Lean 4 formally verifies the lower-bound theorem itself.

title: Recurrent neural network reveals near-critical seeding of topological defects in Kibble–Zurek simulations
summary: In numerical simulations of a one-dimensional Landau–Ginzburg phase transition, a recurrent neural network predicted the final locations of topological defects from short sequences of order-parameter fluctuations during the Kibble–Zurek impulse regime, before freeze-out and before the defects were macroscopically visible. Prediction error across quench rates followed power-law scaling consistent with the Kibble–Zurek freeze-out time, indicating that information about the eventual defect pattern is encoded in near-critical fluctuations in this model.
ai_technology: Recurrent neural network (RNN); LSTM and Transformer architectures were also checked
organization: The University of Tokyo; Los Alamos National Laboratory

evidence.tested: In numerical simulations of a one-dimensional Landau–Ginzburg phase transition, a recurrent neural network predicted the final locations of topological defects from short sequences of order-parameter fluctuations during the Kibble–Zurek impulse regime, before freeze-out and before the defects were macroscopically visible.
evidence.unknown: This is a computational result from a noisy one-dimensional Landau–Ginzburg model, not an experimental observation of defects in a material or cosmological system. The paper uses overdamped dynamics (η=1), low noise temperature θ=10⁻⁸, a finite periodic grid and simulated training/test samples; similar behavior at another noise setting is reported in supplementary material. The finding is consistent with the Kibble–Zurek mechanism and an earlier deconstruction of its dynamics; it does not establish that this prediction method applies unchanged to all phase transitions. The PRL article was published 2026-10-05; the original arXiv preprint was submitted 2025-08-28 and revised as v2 on 2026-09-10.
evidence.ai_role: The RNN analyzed short time sequences from numerical order-parameter dynamics and inferred the final kink count and positions from small fluctuations during the impulse regime. This allowed the authors to identify when information about future defect positions becomes predictable, a quantity not directly provided by conventional Kibble–Zurek defect-density scaling. They report similar prediction behavior with LSTM and Transformer models, suggesting the result is not specific to one architecture.

title: Machine-learning earthquake catalog reveals transform fault in the Zabargad Fracture Zone
summary: A 12-month network of ocean-bottom and land seismometers yielded a high-resolution catalog of more than 3,900 earthquakes in the northern Red Sea Zabargad Fracture Zone and Mabahiss Deep. The southern cluster’s diffuse seismicity and predominantly left-lateral strike-slip focal mechanisms reveal a NE–SW transform fault, which the authors describe as possibly in an early development stage. The northern cluster instead shows NW–SE normal-faulting lineaments related to extension.
ai_technology: OBSTransformer deep-learning phase picker, transfer-learned from EQTransformer and used through SeisBench
organization: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST); GEOMAR Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research

evidence.tested: A 12-month network of ocean-bottom and land seismometers yielded a high-resolution catalog of more than 3,900 earthquakes in the northern Red Sea Zabargad Fracture Zone and Mabahiss Deep.
evidence.unknown: The transform fault is inferred from the southern seismicity pattern and selected-event focal mechanisms, not directly imaged along its full geometry; the authors describe it as possibly in an early development stage. The catalog covers a 12-month deployment and is a snapshot that may not capture episodic ridge seismicity. Exact spreading-axis configuration remains uncertain. The earthquake-processing workflow was not fully automatic: investigators manually reviewed and corrected picks, removed events recorded by fewer than three stations, and used manual focal-mechanism analysis.
evidence.ai_role: The researchers compared EQTransformer, OBSTransformer and PickBlue for automatic earthquake detection and P/S phase picking on continuous ocean-bottom and land-station data. OBSTransformer was selected because it detected more events than EQTransformer while yielding fewer false detections than PickBlue and closer agreement with manual picks. The resulting detections and picks were manually checked and corrected, then used in the catalog from which the clusters and focal-mechanism analysis revealed the faulting pattern.

title: Symbolic-regression active learning identifies 12 acid-stable oxide candidates by HSE06 calculations
summary: A SISSO symbolic-regression active-learning workflow identified 12 acid-stable oxide candidates from a pool of 1,470 within 30 active-learning iterations, using high-quality DFT-HSE06 Pourbaix calculations to evaluate oxygen-evolution stability. Many candidates had not been previously identified by widely used GGA calculations. The model’s property maps and uncertainty estimates helped direct calculations toward promising, underexplored regions of oxide space.
ai_technology: SISSO symbolic regression with bootstrap and Monte Carlo feature-dropout ensembles in an active-learning loop
organization: NOMAD Laboratory, Fritz Haber Institute of the Max Planck Society

evidence.tested: A SISSO symbolic-regression active-learning workflow identified 12 acid-stable oxide candidates from a pool of 1,470 within 30 active-learning iterations, using high-quality DFT-HSE06 Pourbaix calculations to evaluate oxygen-evolution stability.
evidence.unknown: This is a computational materials-property result, not experimental synthesis or electrochemical validation. The oxide structures were drawn from a known candidate space; the authors explicitly define “discovery” here as evaluating a previously unevaluated property, not discovering entirely new compounds. Acid stability is labeled at ΔG_Pourbaix^OER ≤ 0.10 eV/atom, a threshold that allows small positive values on the basis of potential self-passivation. The result depends on HSE06 DFT and the selected Pourbaix phases/conditions; practical catalytic stability must be tested experimentally.
evidence.ai_role: SISSO models learned compact descriptors of acid stability from existing calculations; model ensembles estimated prediction uncertainty, and a probability-of-feasibility acquisition strategy selected the next oxide for expensive DFT-HSE06 evaluation. The resulting feedback loop searched 1,470 candidates and identified 12 materials meeting the authors’ acid-stability criterion in 30 iterations, more efficiently than random selection.

title: Deep-learning seismic picks reveal upper-mantle upwelling conduits beneath Southwestern US volcanic fields
summary: Using an expanded Pn-wave travel-time database, the authors construct a high-resolution uppermost-mantle velocity and anisotropy model for the southwestern United States. The tomographic interpretation identifies separate low-velocity, anisotropic upwelling conduits beneath the Black Rock Desert, Uinkaret, and San Francisco volcanic fields along the Colorado Plateau margins, and supports remnants of the ancient Farallon slab beneath the central Great Basin.
ai_technology: Seis-PickNet deep-learning seismic phase picker
organization: Institute of Geology and Geophysics, Chinese Academy of Sciences; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences; Shandong Earthquake Agency

evidence.tested: Using an expanded Pn-wave travel-time database, the authors construct a high-resolution uppermost-mantle velocity and anisotropy model for the southwestern United States.
evidence.unknown: These are tomographic interpretations of seismic velocity and anisotropy, not direct images or direct measurements of magma conduits. The article abstract reports inferred independent thermal upwellings and supports (rather than proves uniquely) Farallon slab remnants. Resolution and tectonic interpretation depend on the travel-time picks and inversion assumptions; the paper's abstract does not establish direct volcanic plumbing connectivity.
evidence.ai_role: The authors used Seis-PickNet to automatically pick Pn phases and expand the regional travel-time database; those new picks underpin the velocity and anisotropy tomography from which the mantle structures are interpreted. The AI supplies the expanded seismic measurements used in the scientific inversion, rather than only classifying existing results.

title: LLM-guided search yields three synthesized lithium-ion cathodes with higher initial capacity than NMC811
summary: An expert-guided LLM workflow proposed three NMC811-derived cathode compositions—NMC-SiMg, NMC-SiCa and NMC-MgB—that the authors report as absent from the queried materials databases. After DFT-based computational screening, the team synthesized and characterized all three. At the third cycle, measured reversible capacities were 174, 169 and 160 mAh/g, compared with 135 mAh/g for NMC811 under the reported conditions (improvements of 28.8%, 25.2% and 18.5%).
ai_technology: ChatBattery expert-guided LLM agent framework (GPT-3.5 for composition generation; GPT-o4 for qualitative voltage ranking), with MACE-MP machine-learning potential for computational energy evaluation
organization: Université de Montréal; Mila – Québec AI Institute; University of Oxford; University College London; University of Ottawa; National Research Council Canada

evidence.tested: An expert-guided LLM workflow proposed three NMC811-derived cathode compositions—NMC-SiMg, NMC-SiCa and NMC-MgB—that the authors report as absent from the queried materials databases.
evidence.unknown: This is an arXiv preprint (v1, posted 2025-07-21); no peer-reviewed journal publication was identified in the checked source. The formulas are modifications within the established layered NMC cathode family, not fundamentally new chemistry classes. The capacity comparison is reported at the third cycle; long-term cycle life and practical cell performance are not established here. The paper notes minor unidentified impurity peaks and says the LLM's qualitative voltage ranking was not exhaustive. Human experts designed the prompts and performed synthesis/characterization, so this was an expert-guided AI discovery workflow, not autonomous discovery.
evidence.ai_role: ChatBattery generated and iteratively refined cathode hypotheses using domain-expert prompts, materials-database checks, rule-based capacity/charge screening and an LLM voltage-ranking step. The top candidates were selected for computational evaluation and wet-lab synthesis; MACE-MP screened sampled disordered supercells when direct DFT was too costly. Human experts designed prompts and conducted the experimental verification. This workflow led to the three experimentally synthesized compositions and their measured initial-cycle capacity improvements.

title: Neural-network satellite soil-moisture data expose global hotspots and pathways of rainfall coupling
summary: An information-flow analysis of daily observations found statistically significant local surface-soil-moisture effects on precipitation over about 15.7% of global land (60°S–60°N) in the boreal warm season, with eight regional hotspots. Sensible-heat mediation dominated most hotspots, while evapotranspiration mediation dominated two African hotspots; remote moisture availability and boundary-layer-height variability helped explain regional differences. Only four of 16 assessed CMIP6 models reproduced the ERA5-derived relationship between soil-moisture variability and causal coupling.
ai_technology: Neural-network-inversion satellite soil-moisture product (NNSm), analyzed with Liang–Kleeman information-flow causal inference
organization: Tsinghua University; Chinese Academy of Sciences; National University of Singapore; University of Connecticut; Peking University

evidence.tested: An information-flow analysis of daily observations found statistically significant local surface-soil-moisture effects on precipitation over about 15.7% of global land (60°S–60°N) in the boreal warm season, with eight regional hotspots.
evidence.unknown: The mapped effect is local surface-soil-moisture-to-precipitation information flow, statistically significant at the authors' p<0.1 threshold over about 15.7% of land; the analysis does not imply local soil moisture causes rainfall everywhere or exclude remote/upwind effects. The AI contribution is the neural-network-derived satellite soil-moisture product; the causal analysis is not itself an AI model. The spatial pattern was broadly checked with ERA5, while pathway attribution depends on ERA5-reanalysis variables and the assumptions/limitations of information-flow causal inference. Results concern boreal warm seasons and the analyzed 2003–2020 satellite period (ERA5 cross-check spans 1979–2021).
evidence.ai_role: The study's long-term daily satellite soil-moisture series was generated with a neural-network inversion algorithm, extending the observed record used to map global coupling. Researchers applied information-flow analysis to this AI-derived product and precipitation observations, then cross-checked the main spatial pattern using independent ERA5 reanalysis. AI provided the satellite soil-moisture input for a concrete global climate result; the causal-inference method itself is an information-theoretic statistical technique, not a learned model.

title: Bayesian optimization finds high-performance hole-transport molecules for perovskite solar cells
summary: A closed-loop workflow combined high-throughput synthesis of organic semiconductors, measured photovoltaic-device performance, molecular descriptors and Bayesian optimization to search a virtual library of about one million candidate hole-transport materials. The machine-learning-guided iterations identified high-performing molecules; after device optimization, a perovskite solar cell using a selected material reached 26.23% power-conversion efficiency (25.88% certified). The work links candidate molecular structures to measured device performance in this specific cell system.
ai_technology: Molecular-descriptor machine-learning models with Bayesian optimization in a high-throughput synthesis and device-testing loop
organization: Forschungszentrum Jülich / Helmholtz Institute Erlangen-Nürnberg; Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg; Karlsruhe Institute of Technology; Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology; Xiamen University; University of Electronic Science and Technology of China; University of Groningen

evidence.tested: A closed-loop workflow combined high-throughput synthesis of organic semiconductors, measured photovoltaic-device performance, molecular descriptors and Bayesian optimization to search a virtual library of about one million candidate hole-transport materials.
evidence.unknown: The 26.23% champion and certified 25.88% values followed device-specific optimization of a selected molecule; this does not establish that the molecule alone accounts for the full efficiency gain or that it is globally optimal among all possible molecules. The paper reports a materials-selection workflow for a particular p-i-n perovskite device setup, with performance also affected by other cell layers and processing. The million-member search was virtual and only a small selected subset was synthesized and measured; authors do not claim to have found the single best molecule in that space.
evidence.ai_role: Models trained on measured data from 149 synthesized molecules linked calculated molecular descriptors to perovskite-device performance. Bayesian optimization selected new structures from a virtual library of roughly one million; high-throughput synthesis, characterization and device tests supplied feedback for two closed-loop iterations. Three promising molecules then received individual device optimization. This workflow identified hole-transport materials yielding the reported high-efficiency perovskite cells; the AI contribution was candidate selection and structure–performance modeling, with synthesis and measurements performed experimentally.

title: ML-guided discovery of 5ANI passivator yields high-efficiency, stable perovskite solar cells
summary: An interpretable machine-learning and active-learning workflow screened a virtual library of 18,264 candidate passivation molecules and guided synthesis/testing of selected candidates for perovskite solar cells. The newly identified molecule 5-(aminomethyl)nicotinonitrile hydroiodide (5ANI) yielded 0.05 cm² devices at 27.22% power-conversion efficiency (27.18% certified) and 21.4 cm² mini-modules at 23.49%. Under the reported ISOS-L-1I operating test, 5ANI devices retained 98.7% of initial efficiency after 1,200 hours.
ai_technology: SISSO interpretable symbolic regression and NGBoost active-learning models, coupled to DFT calculations and a Bayesian-optimization/symbolic-regression automated fabrication platform
organization: City University of Hong Kong; University of Cambridge; Imperial College London; Friedrich-Alexander University Erlangen-Nürnberg; Central South University; Chinese University of Hong Kong; Hong Kong University of Science and Technology; Huazhong University of Science and Technology

evidence.tested: An interpretable machine-learning and active-learning workflow screened a virtual library of 18,264 candidate passivation molecules and guided synthesis/testing of selected candidates for perovskite solar cells.
evidence.unknown: This is a result for a specific perovskite composition, cell architecture and passivation/fabrication protocol. The ML regression was trained on only 20 initial known passivator/device datasets; four selected candidates were experimentally synthesized/validated. The reported champion efficiency is a small-area cell result; the mini-module efficiency is lower (23.49%) and laboratory-scale. The 1,200-hour stability result follows the stated ISOS-L-1I protocol and does not establish commercial lifetime. The paper reports high reproducibility from its automated setup, not factory-scale manufacturing. This is a different study and molecule from the 2024 Bayesian-optimized hole-transport materials record (Science DOI 10.1126/science.ads0901): here AI identifies an interfacial passivator 5ANI.
evidence.ai_role: The team used DFT descriptors and SISSO regression trained on measurements from 20 known passivator/device sets to learn structure–performance relationships. NGBoost active learning reduced the computational cost of estimating interfacial properties across an 18,264-molecule virtual library; model-guided screening selected four candidates for synthesis and experimental validation. 5ANI emerged as a passivator for which the automated device-fabrication loop optimized deposition and processing settings. The ML models guided material choice, while the closed-loop platform refined device fabrication and generated measured feedback.

title: Reinforcement-learning-guided experiments produce a Zr-based bulk metallic glass with 1.7 GPa yield strength and 10.2% elongation
summary: A knowledge-augmented reinforcement-learning search over composition space, guided by learned property models and then validated by synthesis, identified a Zr-based bulk metallic glass, Zr63Cu15Al10Ni10Fe2. Single-step suction-cast specimens reached 1.7 GPa yield strength and 10.2% compressive plastic strain at room temperature. Across tested Fe-alloyed compositions, measured strength trends tracked model predictions; tungsten substitutions did not show the same ductility response.
ai_technology: AIMATDESIGN knowledge-augmented reinforcement-learning framework, using machine-learning property predictors and large-language-model-assisted model refinement and domain-knowledge rewards
organization: Nanjing University of Science and Technology; Shanghai University; University of Science and Technology of China; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

evidence.tested: A knowledge-augmented reinforcement-learning search over composition space, guided by learned property models and then validated by synthesis, identified a Zr-based bulk metallic glass, Zr63Cu15Al10Ni10Fe2.
evidence.unknown: The reported measurements are room-temperature compression tests on single-step suction-cast samples; the paper notes that plastic strain was systematically lower than predicted for most tested specimens, partly because surface defects and residual stresses were not represented in the model. The 10.2% value is for the specific Fe2 composition and test protocol, not a general alloy-family property. This is distinct from a separate study of an ML-designed bulk metallic glass optimized for hardness (DOI 10.1038/s41467-026-73008-0): the present result concerns Zr63Cu15Al10Ni10Fe2 and its strength/ductility balance.
evidence.ai_role: An RL agent explored high-dimensional alloy compositions using ML classification/regression predictions as rewards and feasibility guidance. LLM-assisted feedback corrected unreliable model predictions and expert materials rules informed late-stage rewards. The authors used this workflow to choose Zr-based bulk-glass compositions for synthesis and mechanical testing; the experimentally tested Zr63Cu15Al10Ni10Fe2 composition achieved the reported strength and ductility result. This AI-guided composition search is the discovery contribution; the LLM was one component of a larger RL/ML workflow.

title: Machine-learning-selected α-MoO3 and ReS2 deliver high measured responsivity in extreme-ultraviolet detectors
summary: A cross-spectral machine-learning model trained on 1,927 visible/UV photodetector records screened materials for extreme-ultraviolet response and selected α-MoO3 and ReS2 for device validation. At the Australian Synchrotron, the α-MoO3 detector showed measured responsivity of about 50–160 A/W depending on photon energy and bias (about 60–70 A/W near 13.5 nm); ReS2 reached about 20 A/W at 91.8 eV and 1 mV, close to the model estimate. The α-MoO3 device retained repeatable current response through 100 bias cycles under high-flux exposure.
ai_technology: Extremely Randomized Trees cross-spectral response prediction model
organization: RMIT University; University of Illinois Chicago; University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign; Shahid Beheshti University; Monash University; Pakistan Institute of Engineering and Applied Sciences; Concordia University; University of Shanghai for Science and Technology; Australian Synchrotron

evidence.tested: A cross-spectral machine-learning model trained on 1,927 visible/UV photodetector records screened materials for extreme-ultraviolet response and selected α-MoO3 and ReS2 for device validation.
evidence.unknown: The reported measurements are for the fabricated devices and stated synchrotron energies, biases and exposure conditions; they do not establish equivalent responsivity across all EUV wavelengths or device architectures. The paper reports α-MoO3 responsivity ranging about 50–160 A/W across test conditions, while near 13.5 nm it reports about 60–70 A/W; ReS2 was tested at a specified energy/bias. The authors' silicon comparison varies with the comparison conditions and metric (the abstract gives about 225-fold, while the device discussion reports up to about 800-fold); this record therefore states the direct responsivity measurements without treating either ratio as universal. The material screening result is a small experimental validation set, not an exhaustive search.
evidence.ai_role: The model learned relations between material/device descriptors and detector response across wavelength ranges from a 1,927-record dataset of visible and ultraviolet photoresponse measurements. It screened candidate materials for EUV responsivity and selected α-MoO3 and ReS2 for fabrication and synchrotron testing. The AI contribution was transferring response patterns across spectral domains to prioritize materials; experiments then measured the EUV detector performance.

title: Bayesian optimization and graph learning identify two synthesized ultra-incompressible hard materials
summary: A Bayesian optimization workflow using symmetry-constrained crystal relaxation and the MEGNet graph neural network screened 399,960 transition-metal boride and carbide compositions. The study identified MoWC₂ (P6₃/mmc) and ReWB (Pca2₁), then synthesized both by in-situ reactive spark-plasma sintering; the measured hardness was reported to agree with model and DFT predictions. The result is limited to these two synthesized compounds and the authors’ tested synthesis conditions.
ai_technology: BOWSR (Bayesian Optimization With Symmetry Relaxation) with the MEGNet graph neural network energy model
organization: University of California San Diego

evidence.tested: A Bayesian optimization workflow using symmetry-constrained crystal relaxation and the MEGNet graph neural network screened 399,960 transition-metal boride and carbide compositions.
evidence.unknown: The arXiv abstract states that the two materials were synthesized and describes them as ultra-incompressible hard materials; the institutional project page reports experiments on eight selected candidates and confirmation of two novel hard materials. The result is from a preprint/journal study and the provided abstract does not give numeric hardness values. Do not imply commercial performance or broader synthesis robustness.
evidence.ai_role: MEGNet supplied graph-based formation-energy predictions; BOWSR used Bayesian optimization under crystal-symmetry constraints to relax candidate structures without DFT geometry relaxation. This enabled screening of 399,960 boride/carbide compositions, narrowing candidates for experimental synthesis.

title: Machine learning identifies five synthesized Chevrel-phase tellurides with unusual channel-site occupancy
summary: An interpretable machine-learned descriptor for decomposition enthalpy screened more than 200,000 Chevrel-phase compositions, predicting 48,501 below the study’s statistical synthesizability cutoff. Researchers selected five previously unreported tellurides for synthesis and successfully made all five; experiments also confirmed the predicted preference for intercalant cations to occupy Chevrel-phase channels, a rare motif in this family. The predicted candidate list is much larger than the experimentally attempted and confirmed subset. The date is the journal paper’s online publication; UC Davis announced it on 24 June 2021.
ai_technology: SIFT descriptor-generation and interpretable machine-learning model Hδ
organization: University of California, Davis

evidence.tested: An interpretable machine-learned descriptor for decomposition enthalpy screened more than 200,000 Chevrel-phase compositions, predicting 48,501 below the study’s statistical synthesizability cutoff.
evidence.unknown: The original paper abstract reports five successful syntheses among five tellurides attempted and confirms a predicted channel-site occupancy trend. The other thousands of predicted candidates were not demonstrated as synthesized in this study. The result concerns a specific molybdenum-chalcogenide family.
evidence.ai_role: The SIFT method generated more than 560,000 candidate descriptors; an interpretable ML model trained against DFT-computed decomposition enthalpies assessed synthesizability and selected Chevrel-phase compositions for experimental follow-up.

title: Autonomous machine-learning experiments identify a dual-anion aqueous sodium electrolyte with a wider stability window
summary: A robotic electrochemistry stand coupled to Bayesian optimization tested 140 aqueous electrolyte formulas over 40 hours and selected a non-intuitive sodium mixture of NaClO4 and NaNO3. On platinum, the blend had a wider electrochemical stability window than the NaClO4 baseline despite lower total salt concentration; follow-up tests reported a 24 mV increase in the OER potential at the stated leakage-current criterion and 58% lower current density at 2 V. The result is a measured electrolyte formulation under the paper’s electrochemical protocols, not evidence of a commercial battery or field-ready cell.
ai_technology: Dragonfly Bayesian optimization software coupled to the Otto robotic electrochemistry test stand
organization: Carnegie Mellon University

evidence.tested: A robotic electrochemistry stand coupled to Bayesian optimization tested 140 aqueous electrolyte formulas over 40 hours and selected a non-intuitive sodium mixture of NaClO4 and NaNO3.
evidence.unknown: The study measured electrochemical behavior primarily on platinum electrodes and reports a wider stability window for the selected aqueous blend under its stated protocol. This does not establish long-term performance, commercial readiness, or general improvement across battery chemistries.
evidence.ai_role: Dragonfly selected electrolyte formulations sequentially from real-time measurements and guided autonomous experiment requests to Otto; the paper reports the mixed-anion sodium formulation as the optimization result.

title: Machine-learning-guided calculations predict four rare-earth-free magnetic Fe–Co–Si compounds
summary: A crystal-graph neural network screened 357,480 hypothetical Fe–Co–Si structures; adaptive genetic search and density-functional calculations then identified four predicted ternary structures with calculated saturation polarization ≥1.0 T, easy-axis anisotropy ≥1.0 MJ/m³, and Curie temperature >840 K. Their calculated energies lie within 70 meV/atom of the ternary convex hull, supporting but not proving experimental accessibility. The paper proposes the structures for synthesis; it does not experimentally demonstrate them.
ai_technology: Crystal graph convolutional neural network (CGCNN) with an adaptive genetic algorithm
organization: University of Texas at Austin and Ames National Laboratory

evidence.tested: A crystal-graph neural network screened 357,480 hypothetical Fe–Co–Si structures; adaptive genetic search and density-functional calculations then identified four predicted ternary structures with calculated saturation polarization ≥1.0 T, easy-axis anisotropy ≥1.0 MJ/m³, and Curie temperature >840 K.
evidence.unknown: This is a theoretical, ML-guided first-principles prediction; the paper proposes the structures for synthesis and does not report experimental synthesis. The abstract describes four compounds; the results section mentions five structures meeting initial thresholds, of which four are dynamically stable. Report the four final candidates and their calculated properties only. The work establishes neither actual permanent-magnet performance nor synthesizability.
evidence.ai_role: CGCNN models rapidly screened hypothetical structures and predicted formation energy and magnetic polarization; first-principles results were fed back to train improved models across successive generations, while an adaptive genetic algorithm searched lower-energy structures. ML materially narrowed the space for the final density-functional magnetic-property calculations.

title: Machine-learning-guided synthesis yields a new blue-emitting perovskite-like single crystal
summary: A high-throughput robotic synthesis and characterization workflow used a convolutional neural network to recognize crystal growth and a machine-learning regressor to guide synthesis conditions. The team reported the first synthesis of (3-PLA)₂PbCl₄, a new perovskite-like single crystal with a direct band gap near 4 eV and strong blue emission. The reported growth conditions were restrictive and required a carefully tuned search.
ai_technology: Convolutional neural network image classifier and machine-learning synthesis-condition regressor
organization: University of Toronto

evidence.tested: A high-throughput robotic synthesis and characterization workflow used a convolutional neural network to recognize crystal growth and a machine-learning regressor to guide synthesis conditions.
evidence.unknown: The authors characterize this as a new perovskite-like material and report a laboratory single-crystal synthesis and blue emission. Synthesis conditions were restrictive; the paper does not establish device performance or scale-up.
evidence.ai_role: The CNN classified crystal-growth outcomes from images, and the model trained on high-throughput experimental results selected promising conditions for successive synthesis trials. That feedback-guided sequence enabled the first synthesis of (3-PLA)₂PbCl₄.

title: Machine-learning validation and independent cross-checks classify 50 Kepler candidates as planets
summary: A Gaussian-process classifier, supported by random-forest, extra-trees and multilayer-perceptron models, was applied to Kepler transit candidates. From 83 candidates meeting the study’s stringent ML and data-quality criteria, the authors newly validated 50 as planets after updated vespa false-positive checks also gave each less than a 1% false-positive probability. The result is statistical validation using Kepler pipeline and stellar data, not new telescope observations of the planets.
ai_technology: Gaussian process classifier, random forest, extra trees and multilayer perceptron classifiers
organization: University of Warwick

evidence.tested: A Gaussian-process classifier, supported by random-forest, extra-trees and multilayer-perceptron models, was applied to Kepler transit candidates.
evidence.unknown: The 50 are statistically validated candidates from archival Kepler observations, not newly observed planets. The authors caution that their method is trained and demonstrated on Kepler, that atypical/outlier candidates may be unreliable, and that ML and vespa disagree for 33 other high-ML candidates; those were not counted as validated. This entry counts one paper-level validation result, not 50 separate records.
evidence.ai_role: Four machine-learning classifiers jointly ranked candidate transit signals against planet and false-positive scenarios. The paper required all four to cross 0.99 planet probability plus positional, stellar, binary and outlier checks; an updated vespa calculation then independently cross-checked the retained candidates.

title: AI-guided polyVERSE discovery yields a high-temperature dielectric polymer with 8.3 J cm⁻³ energy density
summary: The polyVERSE workflow used reaction-aware polymer generation and machine-learning property screens to identify PONB-2Me5Cl, which the researchers synthesized and cast into films. Experimental characterization measured a discharged energy density of 8.3 J cm⁻³ at 200 °C and a breakdown field of 750 MV m⁻¹; the paper compares this energy density with commercial polymer dielectrics at the same temperature. This is a laboratory polymer-film result, not a packaged capacitor or aerospace-ready device.
ai_technology: polyVERSE with four polymer graph neural-network property predictors
organization: Georgia Institute of Technology and University of Connecticut

evidence.tested: The polyVERSE workflow used reaction-aware polymer generation and machine-learning property screens to identify PONB-2Me5Cl, which the researchers synthesized and cast into films.
evidence.unknown: The reported 8.3 J cm⁻³ is measured on synthesized polymer films under the article’s laboratory breakdown and dielectric characterization protocol. The comparison with commercial polymers is the authors’ reported comparison; the work does not demonstrate a packaged capacitor, operational lifetime, aerospace use, or scale-up. Other suggested polyimides in the paper remain predicted and are not counted here. The reported polymerization used non-green solvents.
evidence.ai_role: polyVERSE generated polymers from commercially available monomers using encoded reaction templates, then machine-learning models predicted glass-transition temperature, band gap and dielectric properties for screening. AI down-selected polymer candidates for synthesis; PONB-2Me5Cl was subsequently synthesized and its dielectric properties were measured.

title: ML-guided experiments synthesize single-phase Ba–Sr cerate perovskite solid solutions
summary: Machine-learning screening and expert down-selection identified Ba–Sr cerate oxide compositions for synthesis. The researchers used an automated rapid-sintering and dielectric-characterization platform and reported X-ray diffraction evidence of single-phase solid-solution specimens with refined orthorhombic Pnma structures. The finding is an experimental validation of selected ML-predicted compositions and a process-structure result; it does not establish device performance or broad predictive success.
ai_technology: Gradient-boosting perovskite classifier; VAE and composition-embedding screening
organization: Queen Mary University of London; QinetiQ

evidence.tested: Machine-learning screening and expert down-selection identified Ba–Sr cerate oxide compositions for synthesis.
evidence.unknown: The paper experimentally reports selected ML-predicted Ba–Sr cerate compositions as single-phase by XRD and refines their structures, while additional tested compositions showed multiple phases; ML prediction alone did not guarantee synthesis. The text is inconsistent about the Sr fraction for one reported specimen (abstract/table/figure versus one results sentence), so this entry avoids assigning that composition. The paper validates selected members of a prior predicted set rather than claiming a universal synthesis predictor. Dielectric analysis is reported, but no application/device performance is established.
evidence.ai_role: A gradient-boosting classifier trained on experimental perovskite/non-perovskite structures screened roughly 0.6 million possible compositions, assigning high perovskite likelihood to a candidate set. Variational-autoencoder and element-composition embeddings, plus human literature and synthesis-feasibility review, down-selected compositions that were then synthesized and characterized.

title: Data-science-guided experiments discover a Co–Ta–Sn rutile alloy oxide with tunable transparency and acid-stable electrocatalysis
summary: A high-throughput optical screen and data-science models identified a Co–Ta–Sn composition region whose optical trends indicated phase behavior beyond simple mixtures. Follow-up X-ray diffraction verified a rutile substitutional-alloy oxide, (Sn,Co,Ta)O₂. Composition tuning produced optical transparency and oxygen-evolution electrocatalytic activity with stability in strong-acid electrolyte, as reported by the authors.
ai_technology: Physics-aware data-science phase-diagram and emergent-property models
organization: Google Research; California Institute of Technology

evidence.tested: A high-throughput optical screen and data-science models identified a Co–Ta–Sn composition region whose optical trends indicated phase behavior beyond simple mixtures.
evidence.unknown: The phase inference initially came from optical data and the authors discuss potential false positives from extrinsic film morphology; the selected Co–Ta–Sn rutile phase was followed up and verified by XRD. The optical screen identifies promising regions, not all possible phases, and may miss phases without emergent optical signatures. Reported oxygen-evolution performance and acid stability are laboratory electrocatalysis results; no commercial device or scale-up is established.
evidence.ai_role: Models analyzed high-throughput optical absorption measurements across 376,752 compositions in 108 three-cation oxide systems. They inferred candidate phase diagrams and flagged optical trends inconsistent with lower-order phase mixtures, guiding the Co–Ta–Sn follow-up composition and XRD experiments that verified a rutile alloy phase; this screening also guided catalytic characterization.

title: Machine-learning-guided synthesis realizes four single-phase refractory carbide compositions
summary: A random-forest model ranked new chromium-containing multicomponent carbide compositions by predicted entropy-forming ability. After density-functional calculations and experimental synthesis, X-ray diffraction identified four previously unreported single-phase rock-salt compositions: CrMoNbVWC₅, CrMoNbTaWC₅, CrMoTaVWC₅, and CrMoTiVWC₅. The first three were high-EFA selections; CrMoTiVWC₅ was a medium-EFA composition and required extended annealing to reach chemical homogeneity.
ai_technology: Random-forest models using chemical attributes, with and without CALPHAD thermodynamic features
organization: University of California San Diego; Duke University

evidence.tested: A random-forest model ranked new chromium-containing multicomponent carbide compositions by predicted entropy-forming ability.
evidence.unknown: Only seven of the 70 model-screened candidates were selected for DFT and synthesis, and several tested compositions formed multiple phases. Single-phase identification used XRD and was supported by microstructure, elemental mapping and EBSD; the medium-EFA CrMoTiVWC₅ sample required extended annealing. The paper establishes synthesis and phase formation, not measured application performance or engineering readiness.
evidence.ai_role: The random-forest models learned entropy-forming ability from 56 previously reported carbide compositions and rapidly screened 70 new chromium-containing candidates. Model rankings guided selection of seven compositions for DFT calculations and synthesis; experimental phase outcomes agreed with predicted rankings, including four single-phase materials.

title: Generative machine learning identifies and validates new dual- and tri-phase eutectic compositionally complex alloys
summary: A conditional variational autoencoder generated candidate alloy compositions and an artificial neural network ranked eutectic-forming likelihood. The team experimentally validated previously unreported eutectic compositionally complex alloys across quaternary to senary systems. Reported examples include Al₁₆Cr₁₈Fe₂₄Ni₄₂ with a dual-phase FCC/BCC eutectic lamellar structure and Al₁₁.₃Nb₁₃.₇Co₃₆.₆Cr₈.₂Fe₇.₉Ni₂₂.₃ with a tri-phase FCC/BCC/Laves eutectic structure, supported by XRD, SEM and DSC.
ai_technology: Conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) and artificial neural network (ANN)
organization: City University of Hong Kong; Shenzhen University

evidence.tested: A conditional variational autoencoder generated candidate alloy compositions and an artificial neural network ranked eutectic-forming likelihood.
evidence.unknown: The authors report five newly identified ECCA compositions across the studied systems; this is one paper-level result, not five records. The entry names two representative experimentally examined compositions. Validation is limited to the reported arc-melted samples and XRD/SEM/DSC characterization; no long-term mechanical performance or application testing is established. The training data were sparse and imbalanced, and dataset filtering was part of the framework.
evidence.ai_role: A CVAE generated candidate compositions conditioned on eutectic/non-eutectic microstructure labels; an ANN trained on composition and thermodynamics-derived descriptors estimated eutectic-forming likelihood and selected generated candidates for experimental validation.
